title: Walmart, Target, and Home Depot Figured Out a Really Aggressive Way to Avoid Taxes. Is It Brilliant or Totally Unfair?
summary: Major retailers like Walmart, Target, and Home Depot are aggressively reducing their local property tax bills through a method called "dark store theory." This strategy involves assessing corporate properties based on their vacant value, shifting the tax burden to residents and smaller businesses. This approach has led to significant tax savings for corporations but substantial revenue loss for local governments.

title: JB Hunt acquires ‘big and bulky’ last-mile provider
summary: J.B. Hunt has acquired Cory 1st Choice Home Delivery for $100 million to expand its final mile delivery capabilities for "big and bulky" products, especially furniture. This strategic investment aims to address the growing demand in e-commerce for oversized items and mitigate issues like damaged deliveries. The acquisition includes 14 warehouses and leverages over 1,000 independent contractors to perform more than 2 million annual deliveries.

title: The top 100 retailers and Canada’s top 10 retailers
summary: This report from the Centre for the Study of Commercial Activity (CSCA) details the top 100 retail conglomerates in Canada for fiscal 2017, ranked by estimated annual retail sales. It highlights the significant concentration of retail buying power among a small number of large organizations, with the top three conglomerates accounting for 28% of total non-automotive retail sales. The article also discusses notable rank changes due to mergers, acquisitions, and performance shifts, and examines the market control dynamics between Canadian and U.S. retailers.

title: Customer Engagement Company LivePerson to Expand Israeli Operations
summary: LivePerson Inc., a Nasdaq and Tel Aviv-listed customer engagement company, is expanding its Israeli branch. The company plans to hire 50 additional employees, adding to its current 350 Israeli staff, with a focus on leveraging Israel's cybersecurity and machine learning expertise. LivePerson develops cloud-based systems for customer interaction across various platforms.

title: Home Depot inks major lease in Hines' new business park
summary: The Home Depot Inc. (NYSE: HD) has signed a 20-year lease for a 770,640-square-foot warehouse in Hines' Grand National Business Park. This move follows previous reports that the company was seeking additional industrial space in the Houston area.

title: Walmart on a roll
summary: Walmart is experiencing strong growth, marked by a $1.7 million remodeling project at its Pueblo superstore and impressive holiday sales nationwide. The company reported its strongest holiday quarter in years, with a 4.2% jump in same-store sales and a 43% increase in e-commerce sales, signaling its growing competitiveness against online giants like Amazon. Walmart's success is attributed to a robust economy, strategic investments in store upgrades and employee wages, and an expanding online presence.

title: Walmart flexes in the fourth quarter, beats all expectations
summary: Walmart significantly exceeded Wall Street's expectations for its fiscal fourth quarter profits and sales, driven by strong e-commerce growth and robust performance across various product categories. This positive report defied a gloomy December government retail sales report, indicating that Walmart's strategic investments in online services and grocery pickup are widening its competitive advantage. The company's strong results suggest that consumers are benefiting from a stronger economy, enabling Walmart to attract a broader demographic and pose a more serious threat to Amazon in the online retail space.

title: strolling The Home Depot Canada to hire 5,500 new associates
summary: The Home Depot Canada announced plans to hire over 5,500 new associates across the country for its upcoming spring season. To streamline the application process, the company is introducing a new "Text-To-Apply" feature, allowing candidates to apply via text message. This hiring drive aims to staff various roles including sales associates, cashiers, and garden centre associates, with attractive benefits and career growth opportunities highlighted.

title: Home Depot backs $37M investment in Atlanta-based delivery service
summary: The Home Depot has backed a $37 million Series C funding round for Roadie, an Atlanta-based delivery service. Roadie's founder and CEO, Marc Gorlin, announced the significant investment. This highlights increasing interest in same-day, next-day local delivery services.

title: Home Depot posts record 2018 sales, profits, expects more in 2019, 2020
summary: Home Depot reported record sales and profits for fiscal year 2018, with sales reaching $108.2 billion, a 7.2 percent increase from 2017. The company is optimistic about future growth, forecasting total sales between $115 billion and $120 billion for fiscal year 2020. This indicates a strong financial performance and a positive outlook for the coming years.

title: Lowe’s Posts Solid 4Q Results as Rival Home Depot Stumbles
summary: Lowe's reported solid fourth-quarter results, with revenue largely in line with estimates and a 1.7% same-store sales gain. CEO Marvin Ellison highlighted a strong 5.8% surge in U.S. comparable sales in January, surpassing rival Home Depot's performance for the month. Despite weather-related headwinds, the company reiterated its full-year sales forecast, indicating investor confidence in Ellison's strategic decisions.

title: It's A Bright New Day in Residential Solar with The Home Depot, Sunrun and Vivint Solar
summary: The Home Depot announced an expansion to its residential solar program, partnering with Sunrun Inc. and introducing Vivint Solar. This collaboration aims to make clean, renewable energy more accessible and affordable to households across the United States. Sunrun will expand its presence to nearly 700 Home Depot stores in 15 states, while Vivint Solar will deploy representatives to stores in eight states, allowing customers easy access to solar solutions.

title: Longtime Dollar General exec to retire
summary: Bob Ravener, Dollar General's top human resources executive, is set to retire in late May after nearly 11 years with the company. He joined Dollar General after holding senior HR roles at Starbucks and The Home Depot, and during his tenure, the company added over 60,000 net new jobs and saw significant increases in internal promotions and employee satisfaction. CEO Todd Vasos credited Ravener's strategy and vision for supporting the company's growth and success.

title: Home Depot CFO Carol Tomé to retire at the end of August
summary: Home Depot announced that its CFO, Carol Tomé, will retire on August 31 after 24 years with the company. Richard McPhail, the current senior vice president of finance control and administration, will succeed her. CEO Craig Menear credited Tomé with significant shareholder value creation and expressed excitement for McPhail's promotion.

title: General Counsel Awards: Teresa Roseborough works to extend Home Depot's value system
summary: Teresa Roseborough, Vice President, General Counsel, and Corporate Secretary of The Home Depot, is highlighted for her work in extending the company's value system. Roseborough reflects on how the historic Brown v. Board of Education decision influenced her perspective. This article is part of the General Counsel Awards feature.

title: Focus On Leadership: Paul De Cock plans to bring fresh energy to Mohawk’s flooring business - Feb 2019
summary: Paul De Cock, the new president of Mohawk Flooring North America, discusses his background and plans for the company in an interview. He outlines his strategy to realign business units, grow the resilient flooring segment, and enhance the customer experience for both retailers and consumers. De Cock also reflects on his Flemish heritage's influence on leadership and the ongoing changes in consumer product selection.

title: World's largest tool maker bringing major manufacturing plant, 500 jobs to DFW
summary: The world's largest tool manufacturer, which recently announced a 1.2 million-square-foot distribution center at AllianceTexas, has revealed plans for a new manufacturing plant in the DFW area. This new facility is expected to create 500 jobs. This represents another significant investment by the company in the Dallas-Fort Worth region.

title: Big Retailers’ Sales Lag as They Gird for Tariffs
summary: Sales at several major retailers, including Kohl's, J.C. Penney, and Nordstrom, declined in the latest quarter, while Home Depot's comparable-store sales increased less than expected. This slowdown in the retail sector is occurring as companies prepare for the potential impact of higher tariffs on merchandise imported from China. The industry is also undergoing a significant shift towards e-commerce.

title: Home Depot revenue up, same-store sales growth slows
summary: Home Depot reported its slowest same-store sales growth in at least three years, missing Wall Street estimates due to poor weather in February and a steep fall in lumber prices. Despite this, net income and net sales surpassed analyst expectations.

title: Red-Letter Day for Target
summary: Target Corporation reported surprisingly strong first-quarter sales growth, with overall sales up 5.1 percent to $17.4 billion and comparable store sales increasing by 4.8 percent. The company's digital sales saw a 42 percent rise, driven significantly by same-day fulfillment services, and its operating income and net income also showed healthy growth. Analysts view Target's strategic investments in pricing, merchandising, store remodeling, and digital services as key to its success and position it as a retail "survivor" comparable to industry leaders.

title: Home Depot sees opportunity in tool rental
summary: Home Depot Inc. is seeing significant growth in its tool rental business, particularly among professional customers. Despite this improvement, the company believes there is still substantial opportunity for further expansion by continuing to invest in and enhance its tool rental experience. Analysts also project a potential $800 million impact from lumber deflation.

title: Supreme Court Decides Home Depot v. Jackson
summary: The Supreme Court ruled in Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. v. Jackson that a third-party counterclaim defendant cannot remove a case to federal court under either the general federal removal statute or the Class Action Fairness Act. The decision clarifies that "defendant or defendants" in removal statutes refers specifically to defendants of the original complaint. This affirmation of lower court decisions restricts the ability of third-party counterclaim defendants to move cases to federal jurisdiction.

title: Here's how much Home Depot will pay its new CFO
summary: The Home Depot Inc. announced that Richard McPhail, senior vice president of finance control and a 14-year company veteran, will become its new executive vice president and chief financial officer. He will succeed Carol Tomé, who is set to retire at the end of August. The article was published by the Atlanta Business Chronicle.

title: Home Depot wants to build $67 million distribution hub in Florida
summary: Home Depot plans to construct a $67 million distribution hub in Plant City, Florida, as part of a larger initiative to expand its supply chain across the nation. This development is integrated into the home improvement retailer's broader strategy to enhance its national distribution network. The article highlights Home Depot's focus on strengthening its supply chain.

title: Home Depot wants to build $67 million distribution hub in Plant City
summary: Home Depot plans to construct a $67 million distribution center in Plant City, Florida, expanding its supply chain network. This move is part of the home improvement retailer's broader initiative to bolster its distribution capabilities nationwide.

title: Update: New Home Depot CFO joins list of top Atlanta home sales for Q1 2019
summary: The article reports on some of the top home sales in Atlanta for Q1 2019, highlighting properties that sold for prices ranging from $2.5 million to over $4 million. Notably, the new Home Depot CFO is among those who purchased one of these high-value homes. The piece also mentions other significant real estate transactions in the Atlanta area.

title: Home Depot, Walmart Sued Over ‘Instant’ Tent Canopies
summary: Major retailers including Home Depot and Walmart are facing a patent infringement lawsuit over collasible "instant" tent canopies. Caravan Canopy Int’l Inc. filed the lawsuit, alleging infringement of U.S. Patent No. 5,944,040 by these companies for manufacturing, distributing, and selling such tents. The lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California.

title: A Couple Walked Into Home Depot. What Happened Next Wasn't the Sort of Customer Service They'd Expected
summary: A couple visited Home Depot seeking materials to build a walker for their two-year-old son, Logan, who has hypotonia. Rather than just selling them materials, the staff at the Cedartown, Georgia store built the walker for them free of charge, exemplifying extraordinary customer service and generosity. This act highlights a rare instance of genuine human kindness and going above and beyond expectations in a world often perceived as lacking such gestures.

title: Home Depot Inc. v. Jackson: The Supreme Court Deals Class Action Plaintiffs a Major Victory
summary: The Supreme Court ruled in Home Depot Inc. v. Jackson that third-party counterclaim defendants cannot remove their cases to federal court, marking a significant victory for class action plaintiffs and consumers. This decision allows class action causes of action brought as counterclaims to potentially remain in state court, a preference for plaintiffs but a challenge for defendants who typically prefer federal jurisdiction. Justice Thomas sided with the more liberal wing of the Court in this 5-4 decision, emphasizing statutory interpretation over traditional ideological divisions.

title: Plant City approves Home Depot deal for distribution hub
summary: Plant City has approved a deal for Home Depot to build a nearly 800,000-square-foot distribution hub. This new facility is expected to create up to 345 jobs within the region. This development follows Home Depot's proposal to construct a $67 million distribution hub in Plant City.

title: Home Depot (HD) Dividend Stock Analysis
summary: This article analyzes Home Depot (HD) as a dividend growth stock, highlighting its consistent dividend increases and strong earnings growth over the past decade. It discusses the company's business model, competitive advantages, future growth opportunities, and financial metrics like payout ratio and valuation compared to its competitor Lowe's (LOW). The analysis suggests that while dividend growth may slow during recessions, HD remains a solid long-term investment.

title: Nelson Peltz May Want To Flush Plumbing Company Out Of Brexit Britain
summary: Activist fund Trian Partners, led by Nelson Peltz, has acquired a 6% stake in Ferguson Plc, a British plumbing products company, days after disappointing results. While Ferguson has already undertaken many reforms, Peltz may push for the company to move its listing out of London to secure a better valuation, as over 90% of its revenue comes from the U.S. and its stock appears to be undervalued due to its UK association.

title: Home Depot CEO: You just can't offset 40% deflation (video)
summary: Home Depot CEO Craig Menear discussed the challenge of 40% lumber deflation attributing it to wet weather and stating it cannot be offset. He also indicated the company is exploring ways to mitigate Chinese tariffs. This comes as Home Depot reached $100.9 billion in sales in 2017 and aims for $120 billion by 2020.

title: Tractor Supply Co. opening in Middletown, and you can bring your pig
summary: Tractor Supply Co. is opening a new 30,000-square-foot store in Middletown, New Jersey, catering to those living a "rural lifestyle" and offering products for animals, home gardeners, and DIY enthusiasts. The store is pet-friendly, allowing customers to bring various animals, including pigs, goats, and mini-pigs, mirroring their policy of welcoming all pets in other locations. The official grand opening is scheduled for July 20 with a storewide discount, and the company is praised by local officials and the Chamber of Commerce for its community involvement.

title: Perimeter Solutions Launches PHOS-CHEK® WILDFIRE HOME DEFENSE
summary: Perimeter Solutions has launched PHOS-CHEK® WILDFIRE HOME DEFENSE, providing homeowners with professional-grade wildfire protection previously used by services like CalFire. The product, a phosphate salt-based concentrate, makes wood non-flammable and can protect properties for months, significantly increasing chances of avoiding destruction from wildfires. It will be available in select Home Depot and Tractor Supply Company stores and online.

title: How to protect yourself after the Capital One data breach
summary: Following the Capital One data breach impacting over 100 million people, security experts advise assuming personal data has been compromised. The article details critical steps consumers should take, including freezing credit, signing up for credit monitoring, and changing passwords, to protect against identity theft. The breach is compared in severity to the 2017 Equifax breach, highlighting the need for vigilance.

title: Real Estate Notebook: Atlantic Station tower sells for $177M, Cousins buys out Terminus
summary: This article provides a rundown of top real estate news in Atlanta, highlighting the $177 million sale of the Atlantic Station tower, also known as 171 17th Street or the Wells Fargo tower. It also notes that Cousins has bought out Terminus. Related articles cover Home Depot's search for fulfillment center sites, the sale of Buckhead's Salesforce Tower for $205 million, and potential housing transformation in west Atlanta.

title: Perth Amboy Welcomes Home Depot
summary: The City of Perth Amboy is welcoming Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. as it establishes a new warehousing facility in the city as part of the Elm Street Logistics Center project. This development, led by Duke Realty, involves a $100 million investment, remediation of 92 acres, and is expected to create 400-600 jobs and new public amenities, including waterfront access and recreational areas. Home Depot's investment aligns with its $1.2 billion supply-chain overhaul to enhance delivery services.

title: I Worked at Capital One. Hacks Like This Are Most Dangerous for Low-Income People.
summary: The Capital One data breach, which compromised the data of 100 million Americans, poses a particular risk to the 80,000 applicants for secured credit cards due to the exposure of bank account information. The author, a former Capital One employee, highlights that secured card customers are often low-income and more vulnerable to the financial shock of checking account fraud, unlike credit card or identity theft which typically results in less direct financial loss. The article also questions whether secured cards, despite being touted as credit-building tools, are truly beneficial for low-credit score consumers given the high interest rates and minimal credit score improvement.

title: Metro Phoenix's west side to land 300 new distribution jobs by end of next year
summary: Chino, California-based Quetico is establishing a distribution center in Goodyear, Arizona, which is expected to create 300 new jobs by the end of 2020. The company purchased nearly 40 acres near the Phoenix Goodyear Airport, citing the location's connectivity and competitive business costs. This addition continues a trend of job growth in Goodyear, following announcements from Nike, Chewy Inc., UPS Inc., Ball Corp., and Microsoft.

title: Home Depot says suppliers are moving manufacturing out of China to avoid tariffs
summary: Home Depot's executives stated that their suppliers are actively moving manufacturing out of China to mitigate the impact of rising tariffs. This strategic shift to countries like Taiwan, Vietnam, and Thailand is expected to reduce the tariffs' cost impact on U.S. sales from an projected 2% ($2 billion) to about 1%. The company, which had already lowered its sales outlook for the year, is closely monitoring how these tariffs will affect consumer demand and product pricing.

title: Tom Lydon on Varney & Co: Hot Online Retail ETFs
summary: ETF Trends CEO Tom Lydon appeared on Fox Business Network's "Varney & Co." to discuss online retail ETFs, highlighting the decline of big-box retailers and the rise of online sales. He introduced ETFs like ProShares Decline of the Retail Store ETF (EMTY) and ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN), as well as ProShares Long Online/Short Stores ETF (CLIX) for a combined strategy. The article also touches on mixed Q2 earnings for Home Depot and Kohl's, despite the general downturn in traditional retail.

title: Home Depot will feel the impact of lumber price deflation and Lowe’s improvement
summary: Home Depot Inc. is facing sales pressure due to two main factors: a decline in lumber prices and improved performance from competitor Lowe’s Cos. Inc. The company has acknowledged that falling lumber prices since last year will negatively impact its sales figures. Despite a sales shortfall, Home Depot shares still rose.

title: Target, Like Walmart, Proves Main Engine of Economy Is Humming
summary: Despite recession fears, major discount retailers like Walmart and Target significantly beat Q2 sales expectations and raised full-year profit guidance, indicating a robust U.S. consumer economy. This performance, coupled with strong results from home improvement retailers, suggests a positive outlook for the upcoming holiday season. The retailers' success is attributed to strong fundamentals like price, assortment, and convenience, alongside strategic investments in online options and store remodels.

title: Home-improvement stocks mixed as hurricane expected to both help and hurt
summary: Shares of home-improvement retailers were mixed on Friday as analysts assessed the potential impact of Hurricane Dorian. While an initial sales boost is expected from Floridians preparing for the storm, concerns exist that this may not translate into higher profits for retailers. Hurricane Dorian, a Category 3 storm, was anticipated to significantly threaten Florida and the Northwestern Bahamas.

title: In Depth: Engineered wood products
summary: The article discusses the current state and future prospects of engineered wood products (EWP) in the construction industry. Despite a projected flat to slightly down year for EWP sales due to slowing housing starts, manufacturers see opportunities for market share growth by highlighting benefits like consistency, flexibility, and sustainability. The piece emphasizes how EWP addresses challenges such as labor shortages and evolving building codes, making it an increasingly attractive option for builders and remodelers.

title: Exclusive: Home Depot sizes up commercial space in Central Florida
summary: Home Depot is looking to secure new commercial space east of Orlando, Florida. This move is part of the company's broader $11 billion investment across the U.S. This expansion indicates Home Depot's focus on enhancing its operational footprint in Central Florida.

title: Homebuilders could be heading toward a bigger breakout, trader says
summary: Homebuilder stocks like D.R. Horton, Lennar, and KB Home have seen significant surges this year, with the XHB homebuilder ETF also posting strong gains. Technical analyst Mark Newton believes the rally is sustainable, citing constructive patterns and moderate RSI levels that suggest further upside. Gina Sanchez added that the rally is tied to the Federal Reserve's actions, noting recent improvements in housing starts after a period of softening.

title: Lowe’s CEO Ellison remodels the home-improvement giant
summary: Marvin Ellison, CEO of Lowe's Cos., has been implementing significant changes since July 2018, including overhauling the executive team, changing store operations, and initiating a major technology push with a new 2,000-employee office in Charlotte. Ellison discusses the challenges and successes of his first year, focusing on improving retail fundamentals, addressing profit margin issues due to wholesale prices, and leveraging technology to compete more effectively with rivals like Home Depot and e-commerce companies. He emphasizes Lowe's commitment to its in-store experience due to the nature of home improvement products.

title: Green path in pesticides
summary: Christopher Stidd, a Sarasota native, founded EcoClear Products, which now boasts over $20 million in annual sales with its poison-free pesticides like RatX. The company is set to introduce six new products in 3,000 Walmart stores and has secured a deal with Tractor Supply, significantly boosting its sales. Stidd's journey from struggle to success is marked by innovative product development and a commitment to employee welfare, while continuing to explore new markets like hemp-based pet products.

title: Bullish bias persists, S&P 500 nails the breakout point
summary: The article reports on the persistent bullish bias in the market with the S&P 500 reaching a breakout point. U.S. stocks showed gains early Thursday, influenced by news of a tentative Brexit agreement. The major U.S. benchmarks are performing well technically, extending a mid-month rally.

title: Honing In On HOMZ For REIT Upside
summary: The Hoya Capital Housing ETF (HOMZ) offers diversified exposure across the entire US housing sector, making it a unique offering among real estate ETFs. Since its April debut, HOMZ has surged over 16%, driven by its focus on the residential real estate ecosystem, including home improvement companies and homebuilders. The ETF tracks the Hoya Capital Housing 100 Index, which is composed of 100 companies representing the US Housing Industry and weighted by their contribution to US GDP.

title: Genuine Parts Appoints former HD Supply Facilities Maintenance Head as Chief Transformation Officer
summary: Genuine Parts Company (GPC) has appointed William Stengel, formerly of HD Supply, as its new Executive Vice President and Chief Transformation Officer. In this role, Stengel will oversee GPC's short- and long-term transformation initiatives, including strategic growth, operating efficiency, and cost savings across the organization. He brings over a decade of executive experience from HD Supply to his new position.

title: Home Depot cuts 2019 forecast after sales miss, shares drop
summary: Home Depot's shares dropped after the company announced it was cutting its 2019 sales forecast due to investments taking longer to pay off than anticipated. Despite beating earnings expectations, sales and same-store sales growth fell short of analyst estimates. The company attributed the miss to internal issues related to IT and supply chain improvements, rather than broader economic headwinds.

title: Home Depot shares sink after sales miss but there’s reason to be optimistic
summary: Home Depot shares dropped after the company reported sales that missed expectations, despite earnings per share meeting forecasts. Raymond James analysts maintain an optimistic outlook for the home improvement giant. One analyst suggests that a stronger Lowe's could be impacting Home Depot's performance.

title: Class Action Claims Recall for Self-Starting Whirlpool Glass Cooktops Is Inadequate
summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Whirlpool Corporation, KitchenAid, Inc., and Jenn-Air Corp., alleging that their electric glass cooktops can turn on by themselves, posing a serious fire hazard. The lawsuit claims that Whirlpool's voluntary recall of these cooktops in August 2019 was inadequate, failing to sufficiently notify consumers of the substantial safety risk and to provide timely replacements. The plaintiff argues that Whirlpool prioritized its stock value over consumer safety, leaving many users unaware of the defect and at risk.

title: How Home Depot Is Leveraging the Pro Customer Opportunity
summary: Home Depot is focusing on "pro customers" as a key growth driver, expecting to increase its top line to $101 billion over the next three years. These professional customers, despite being a small percentage of the customer base, account for a significant portion of the retailer's sales. The company is implementing various strategies, including specialized merchandise and services, to cater to this valuable segment.

title: How Home Depot Drives Membership Loyalty With Pro Customers
summary: Home Depot's strategy to drive loyalty among its pro customers involves focusing on installation services, which also generates product demand, and leveraging its Pro Xtra loyalty program. This program offers benefits like purchase tracking and rewards, leading to significantly higher spending from enrolled members. Additionally, Home Depot provides credit financing options with extended benefits for pro customers, showcasing its commitment to this valuable segment.

title: Verizon calls up Carol Tomé to its board of directors
summary: Carol Tomé, formerly CFO of The Home Depot Inc., will join Verizon's board of directors on January 1, 2020. This marks her second major board appointment since retiring from Home Depot on August 31. Tomé's appointment follows her extensive career and previous board engagement with Sovos Brands.

title: Tractor Supply Company Announces CEO Succession Plan
summary: Tractor Supply Company announced that Hal Lawton, formerly President of Macy's, will succeed Greg Sandfort as President, Chief Executive Officer, and Board member, effective January 13, 2020. Sandfort, who is retiring, will remain with the company for a transition period. The Board expressed confidence that Lawton's omnichannel experience and past results make him the right leader for Tractor Supply's future growth.

title: Former eBay Exec Named CEO of Tractor Supply Company
summary: Hal Lawton, former Senior Vice President of eBay North America and President of Macy's, has been named CEO of Tractor Supply Company, effective January 13, 2020. Lawton is credited with a strong track record of driving innovative growth strategies and building Home Depot's internet business to nearly $2 billion in sales. His compensation history shows substantial packages from eBay and Macy's, with his Tractor Supply compensation yet to be disclosed.

title: Carol B. Tomé Elected to Verizon Board of Directors
summary: Verizon Communications Inc. announced the election of Carol B. Tomé, former Chief Financial Officer and Executive Vice President - Corporate Services of The Home Depot, Inc., to its Board of Directors, effective January 1, 2020. Tomé brings significant financial and strategic planning expertise from her 24-year career at Home Depot and her prior board directorships. Her addition will increase Verizon's board membership to 11.

title: Verizon names Carol Tomé to its board of directors
summary: Verizon has announced that Carol Tomé will join its board of directors on January 1, 2020. This marks Tomé's second major board appointment since her retirement from The Home Depot Inc. on August 31. The article also lists related board appointments at other companies.

title: He tried to fix Macy’s. Now he is the new Tractor Supply CEO
summary: Hal Lawton, who served as president of Macy's, is leaving the struggling department store chain to become the CEO of Tractor Supply. Lawton previously worked at eBay and Home Depot. Tractor Supply's stock rose on the news, while Macy's stock also saw a slight increase, though the company has faced significant challenges with declining sales and profits.

title: Home Depot says investments in revamp of online operation will drag on 2020 margins
summary: Home Depot forecasts 2020 sales below Wall Street expectations due to significant investments in its "One Home Depot" online overhaul program. These investments, peaking in 2020 at $3.9 billion, are expected to pressure operating margins. The company also anticipates lower comparable and total sales growth than analysts predicted, acknowledging ambitious timelines for realizing benefits.

title: Throwback Thursday: A Depot Diner
summary: This "Throwback Thursday" article from HBSDealer revisits a 1993 National Home Center News photo detailing the opening of Home Depot's "Depot Diner." The 1,200-square-foot fast-food restaurant was attached to a Home Depot warehouse home center in Woodstock, Ga., and though the concept involved partnerships with major food brands, it ultimately did not succeed. The article is sponsored by Schaffer Associates.

title: Home Depot to bring its design center concept to Rockville, the only location outside of California
summary: Home Depot is bringing its design center concept to Rockville, Maryland, marking its first location outside of California. Federal Realty has filed a permit to convert a former Golf Galaxy into the new Home Depot Design Center. The facility will be two stories and roughly 36,000 square feet.

title: Who is Tractor Supply Co, and Why Did Hal Lawton Go There?
summary: This article discusses Hal Lawton's move from Macy's to become CEO of Tractor Supply Co. (TSC), highlighting TSC's significant but often overlooked presence in modern retail. It explores TSC's business model, financial performance, and the potential reasons for Lawton's appointment, particularly his digital and technological expertise, suggesting a focus on boosting TSC's e-commerce efforts while maintaining its strong physical store connections.

title: ATL Deal Book: Home Depot adds space beside 6500-employee HQ
summary: Home Depot recently completed a deal to acquire more space next to its headquarters in Atlanta. The expansion comes as the company's headquarters is home to 6,500 employees. The new space is located in the six-story Paces Summit building, directly across from their existing HQ.

title: Intel expands paid leave benefits
summary: Intel is significantly enhancing its paid leave benefits, expanding leave for new parents to 12 weeks, providing up to eight weeks for family care, and increasing bereavement leave to two weeks. The company is also introducing a new parent reintegration program allowing part-time work with full-time pay for up to four weeks, alongside a breast milk shipping benefit for traveling mothers. These changes aim to support employee well-being and aid in talent attraction and retention.

title: Lowe's is looking to hire 53,000 people this spring
summary: Lowe's announced plans to hire at least 53,000 workers for the busy spring season in 2020, a decrease from its 2019 goal of 65,000. These jobs include part-time and full-time roles, with hiring events scheduled across its 1,700 U.S. stores. In 2019, about 50% of seasonal hires transitioned to permanent positions, highlighting potential long-term opportunities within the company amidst a tight labor market.

title: Aramark Names Thomas Ondrof as Chief Financial Officer
summary: Aramark has announced the appointment of Thomas Ondrof as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective January 27, 2020. Ondrof brings extensive financial and operational leadership experience from various global companies, including Performance Food Group and MSC Industrial Direct. He will report to President and CEO John Zillmer, who praised Ondrof's strategic contributions during a previous tenure at Aramark.

title: Billionaire Ken Langone And Group of Investors Partners With La Tortillería and Abasto Media
summary: Billionaire Ken Langone and a group of prominent investors have formed a strategic alliance with La Tortillería, a leading Hispanic food distributor, and its sister company Abasto Media. This partnership is expected to accelerate the business growth of both companies, particularly in the Hispanic food market. The investors, including co-founder of Home Depot Ken Langone and former PepsiCo North America CEO Al Carey, expressed confidence in the Calhoun brothers' management and the significant growth potential within the Hispanic market.

title: Court revives 52-year-old Home Depot manager’s constructive discharge claim
summary: A 52-year-old Home Depot manager's age bias lawsuit has been revived by the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, alleging she was "compelled to resign" due to intolerable employment conditions. Janet Wheeler, who had a history of excellent performance reviews, experienced a sudden string of disciplinary notices and felt targeted due to her age and higher salary. The case highlights the prevalence of ageism in the workplace and the legal efforts to combat it.

title: Austin-based Wikibuy is Booming Since its Acquisition by Capital One
summary: Austin-based Wikibuy has experienced significant growth and success since its acquisition by Capital One in November 2018. The company has expanded its employee base and user count, evolving from a comparison-shopping engine to include features like automatic coupon application and cash-back rebates. Wikibuy continues to operate from Austin, contributing to the city's booming e-commerce sector.

title: Grainger, Fastenal Lead Industrial Distributors on Fortune’s 'Most Admired' Companies
summary: Grainger and Fastenal were recognized among Fortune's 'World’s Most Admired Companies' for 2020, leading the diversified wholesalers industry. Grainger ranked first in the diversified wholesalers industry for the seventh consecutive year, while Fastenal placed third. Several other industrial, electrical, and general manufacturers relevant to the industrial supplies space were also included on the prestigious list.

title: Black & Decker agrees to buy major Boeing supplier for $1.5 billion
summary: Stanley Black & Decker has agreed to acquire Consolidated Aerospace Manufacturing (CAM), a key supplier to Boeing, for over $1.5 billion. A significant portion of the purchase price, around $200 million, is contingent on the FAA re-authorizing the 737 MAX to return to service, highlighting the broader impact of the MAX grounding on the supply chain. This acquisition is part of Stanley Black & Decker's strategy to expand beyond tools and strengthen its engineered fastening and infrastructure business.

title: The Home Depot Canada to hire 5,500 new associates
summary: The Home Depot Canada is hiring over 5,500 new associates across the country for its busy spring season, offering full-time, part-time, and seasonal positions. The company emphasizes a values-based hiring approach, seeking individuals who align with its core values, and provides extensive training and competitive benefits. A significant number of their store managers began as hourly associates, highlighting opportunities for career growth within the company.

title: The Home Depot Canada to Hire for 5,500 Job Openings
summary: The Home Depot Canada is hiring over 5,500 new associates across the country for full-time, part-time, and seasonal positions to prepare for its busy spring season. The company offers over one million hours of innovative training and competitive benefits. Over 75% of store managers started as hourly associates, highlighting opportunities for career growth.

title: Universal Forest Products Inc (UFPI) Q4 2019 Earnings Call Transcript
summary: Universal Forest Products (UFPI) reported strong financial results for Q4 and full-year 2019, with records in unit sales, EBITDA, and EPS. The company highlighted growth in retail and construction markets, increased Deckorators product sales, and a new organizational structure aimed at achieving $10 billion in sales. Management also discussed capital allocation, M&A opportunities, and the positive impact of new product development, while addressing questions on lumber markets and business strategy.

title: Gerber directed more than $11M in giving to Atlanta from Home Depot Foundation
summary: Shannon Gerber of The Home Depot Foundation directed over $11 million in charitable giving to benefit the city of Atlanta. Gerber was recognized as a Top Practitioner honoree in the Atlanta Business Chronicle's inaugural Leaders in Corporate Citizenship Awards for her significant contributions.

title: Home Depot’s same-store sales surge in final quarter of 2019
summary: Home Depot reported better-than-expected financial results for the fourth quarter of 2019, driven by strong comparable-store sales and a 10% increase in its quarterly dividend. The company's earnings and revenue surpassed analyst forecasts, with U.S. comparable sales rising by 5.3%. This performance suggests underlying consumer confidence and a positive housing market trend.

title: The Home Depot Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2019 Results; Reiterates Fiscal 2020 Business Outlook; Increases Quarterly Dividend by 10 Percent
summary: The Home Depot reported strong fourth quarter and fiscal year 2019 results, with comparable sales increasing by 5.2% and 3.5% respectively. The company also announced a 10% increase in its quarterly dividend to $1.50 per share and provided a positive business outlook for fiscal 2020, including projected sales growth of 3.5% to 4.0%.

title: Home Depot’s big-ticket items are a hit with shoppers and analysts
summary: Home Depot's sales of big-ticket items, specifically those over $1,000, saw double-digit growth in the latest quarter, contributing positively to their fourth-quarter results. This performance, driven by items like appliances and vinyl plank flooring, led several analysts to increase their price targets for the company's stock. The robust sales in this segment represent approximately 20% of Home Depot's U.S. sales.

title: UPS picks former Home Depot exec as its next CEO
summary: Former Home Depot executive Carol Tomé will become the next CEO of UPS, succeeding David Abney. Her appointment makes her one of the country's highest-profile female chief executives. Tomé expressed her intent to build on Abney's success and leverage UPS's culture and values.

title: Here's how much UPS will pay new CEO Carol Tomé
summary: UPS announced on March 12 that Carol Tomé, former CFO of The Home Depot Inc., will become its new CEO in June 2020. She will succeed David Abney, who will retire after 46 years with the company. The article focuses on her new compensation package.

title: Thousands of Target employees work over 50 hours a week. Why don’t they get overtime?
summary: Target Corporation is facing multiple class-action lawsuits from "executive team leaders" who claim they are misclassified as exempt employees and are due overtime pay for working over 50 hours a week. These workers argue their duties are largely non-managerial, similar to hourly employees, despite Target's classification. The lawsuits highlight a common retail strategy of using salaried assistant managers to avoid overtime costs, and if successful, could cost Target tens of millions of dollars.

title: The Home Depot Canada Temporarily Adjusts Store Hours and Extends Paid Time Off in Response to COVID-19
summary: The Home Depot Canada is temporarily adjusting store hours, closing daily at 6 p.m. starting March 21st, to allow for restocking and cleaning in response to COVID-19. The company is also extending paid time off for hourly associates, providing an additional 80 hours for full-time and 40 hours for part-time employees, valid until the end of the year. These measures aim to support employees and continue serving customers for essential home improvement needs.

title: COVID-19: Home Depot Canada Reduces Store Hours
summary: The Home Depot Canada announced it is temporarily reducing store hours in response to COVID-19, effective March 21, 2020, with stores closing daily at 6 p.m. This change allows for restocking, cleaning, and appropriate staffing, while also limiting the number of customers inside at one time. The company will also provide paid sick or personal time for associates self-quarantining due to direct COVID-19 exposure.

title: Wood Flooring Market to Reach a Valuation of ~ Us$ 123 Bn by 2027
summary: The global wood flooring market is projected to reach approximately US$123 billion by 2027, growing at a CAGR of about 6% from its 2018 valuation of US$73.4 billion. This growth is primarily driven by the residential sector, especially in Europe, although the market faces challenges from substitutes like luxury vinyl plank, wood-look tiles, laminate, bamboo, and cork flooring. Key players in the market include Mohawk Industries, Shaw Industries Group, Tarkett Group, Kähärs Holding AB (publ), and Armstrong Flooring, Inc.

title: Here's how much Equifax paid CEO Mark Begor, other execs in 2019
summary: This article details the compensation of Equifax CEO Mark Begor and other executives for 2019. It highlights that Equifax CEO Mark Begor was Georgia's highest-paid public company CEO in 2018 based on his compensation. The report was published by the Atlanta Business Chronicle.

title: Costco, Home Depot limiting number of customers in store
summary: Costco and Home Depot are implementing new policies to limit the number of customers in their stores to help prevent the spread of the coronavirus. Costco will allow only two people per membership card, adjust closing times, and change gas station operating hours. Home Depot will also limit customer numbers, eliminate major spring promotions, adjust closing times for cleaning, and provide thermometers to associates for health checks.

title: Costco, Home Depot to limit number of shoppers in stores
summary: Major retailers Costco Wholesale Corp. and Home Depot are implementing new policies to limit the number of shoppers in their stores to promote social distancing. Costco will allow no more than two people per membership card and has special hours for seniors, while Home Depot will close earlier for cleaning and restocking, and is eliminating major spring promotions to reduce store traffic. Both companies are also prioritizing essential supply shipments and donating personal protective equipment.

title: Home Depot makes more changes at stores due to COVID-19
summary: Home Depot has implemented new benefits for its employees in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, including additional paid time off for both full-time and part-time hourly workers. This action comes as Georgia reports a significant number of confirmed cases, hospitalizations, and deaths due to the virus.

title: Home Depot Halts Sales of N95 Masks Amid Shortage, Company Says (Published 2020)
summary: Home Depot has halted sales of N95 masks at all of its North American stores and redirected them to healthcare providers and emergency responders due to the coronavirus pandemic. Other retailers like Lowe's and Target have also taken similar actions, while 3M, a mask manufacturer, has expressed concern over retailers continuing to sell protective gear. The move aims to address the critical shortage of personal protective equipment for frontline workers.

title: Home Depot Stores in Ontario Open Only For Curbside Pick-Up
summary: Effective April 5th, Home Depot stores in Ontario will close to in-store customers, transitioning to curbside pick-up only for essential items following a provincial government order. This closure was initially for a minimum of 14 days, though an update notes that hardware stores were permitted to reopen from May 9th. Stores in other provinces will remain open with adjusted hours, while Quebec stores will be closed every Sunday in April.

title: These Cozy & Chic Zoom Home Backgrounds Are Like Virtual Makeovers For Your Space
summary: This article provides a list of 35 cozy and chic Zoom home backgrounds for virtual makeovers. It explains how to set up virtual backgrounds on Zoom and suggests various themed backdrops from different home interior companies, allowing users to virtually transform their space for video calls.

title: Colgate-Palmolive partners with World Health Organization to make millions of soap bars
summary: Colgate-Palmolive is partnering with the World Health Organization to produce and donate 25 million soap bars to agencies in the U.S. to combat the spread of COVID-19. The company is also donating $20 million in health and hygiene products to local nonprofits and launching a matching gift campaign for its employees. This initiative is part of the #SafeHands effort, with Colgate utilizing five manufacturing plants for soap production.

title: Deal Dash: Charlotte, Atlanta developers tee up apartments; Home Depot lands in Antioch
summary: This "Deal Dash" article from the Nashville Business Journal reports on significant commercial real estate activity in the region. It highlights Charlotte and Atlanta developers planning new apartment projects and Home Depot (NYSE: HD) establishing a presence in Antioch.

title: Home Depot expanding paid time off, doubling overtime pay
summary: The Home Depot Inc. has expanded paid time off for hourly workers, provided additional paid time off for high-risk employees, and offered weekly bonuses and double overtime pay to support its employees during the coronavirus pandemic. These actions resulted in a pre-tax expense of approximately US $850 million for the company. The initiatives focused on ensuring the safety and well-being of associates and customers while providing essential products.

title: Home Depot hit with $850M coronavirus-related charge
summary: Home Depot reported an 11 percent slide in first-quarter profit due to an $850 million pre-tax charge related to coronavirus safety measures and enhanced employee benefits. Despite these costs, the home-improvement retailer saw a 7.1 percent increase in revenue and 6.4 percent growth in comparable store sales, driven by an 11 percent jump in the average sales ticket. The company withdrew its 2020 outlook due to pandemic uncertainty but its shares had outperformed the S&P 500 year-to-date.

title: Lowe's same-store sales surge 11.2% as coronavirus restrictions spark home improvement spending
summary: Lowe's reported a significant 11.2% surge in same-store sales for Q1 2020, beating analyst expectations, as coronavirus restrictions led Americans to invest more in home improvement projects. Despite the strong performance, the company warned that sales growth might moderate later in the year and withdrew its full-year 2020 guidance due to economic uncertainty. Lowe's benefited from being deemed essential, keeping stores open, and experienced an 80% increase in online sales.

title: Lowe’s and Home Depot get a boost as customers stay-at-home
summary: Lowe's and Home Depot saw significant sales jumps in their first quarters due to customers tackling home projects during stay-at-home orders, with digital investments playing a key role. While consumer sales surged, professional contractor sales lagged due to pandemic-related restrictions. The article also discusses potential future headwinds and opportunities for these retailers.

title: Home Depot appoints corporate controller to new C-suite role
summary: Home Depot has appointed Stephen Gibbs, its corporate controller, to a new C-suite role, formalizing his function as the company's principal accounting officer. This change comes amidst other news related to Home Depot's performance and operational adjustments during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Se disparan las ventas de piscinas inflables: el nuevo símbolo de estatus en Instagram
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic and lockdown measures have led to an unexpected surge in the popularity of inflatable pools, transforming them into a new status symbol on Instagram. These pools, originally for children, are now being resold at exorbitant prices on platforms like eBay, far exceeding their retail value from stores such as Walmart. This trend reflects people's desire for a relaxing summer experience at home amidst the pandemic, even leading to increased searches for homes with pools.

title: Home Depot’s Interconnected Retail Strategy is Helping Sales Surge
summary: Home Depot's omnichannel strategy, which CEO Craig Menear calls its "interconnected retail strategy," has been crucial in driving sales growth, including a 21.4% increase in fiscal 2019. This approach emphasizes the digital world as the starting point for customer shopping experiences, even for in-store pickups, and extends to meeting the needs of B2B pro customers through significant investments in its digital business and a dedicated B2B portal. Home Depot's success highlights the importance of digital business transformation in adapting to changing market conditions.

title: Home Depot fined $22K for mishandling lead, arsenic-contaminated soil in Worcester
summary: The Massachusetts Department of Environmental Protection has fined Home Depot $22,000 for failing to report lead and arsenic-contaminated soil during a 2017 excavation in Worcester. Home Depot disposed of 280 cubic yards of the contaminated soil before notifying the state in June 2018, despite regulations requiring immediate reporting. The soil was excavated for the installation of fuel cells at their Gold Star Blvd. location.

title: Ulta reviews 1,254 stores for closures
summary: Ulta Beauty Inc. is conducting a "clean sheet" review of its 1,254 stores, exploring closures, moves, or remodels due to pressures facing retailers, including the coronavirus pandemic. The company's CFO, Scott Settersten, stated Ulta could close additional stores but also aims to capitalize on the retail downturn to negotiate better lease terms or relocate. Despite a projected slower pace of new store openings and a significant dip in Q1 net sales, analysts believe Ulta is still poised to gain market share, especially with its appeal across various price points and its growing digital presence.

title: Booking.com can trademark its name, US Supreme Court rules
summary: The US Supreme Court has ruled that Booking.com can trademark its name, overturning a federal agency's decision that it was too generic. The court found, in an 8-1 decision, that consumers understand "Booking.com" refers to a specific company, not a general online hotel reservation service. This ruling could influence trademark protection for other ".com" companies.

title: Home Depot changes rope sales practice after nooses are found in store
summary: Home Depot has altered its rope sales policy, opting to sell pre-cut lengths instead of rope from large spools, following multiple incidents of nooses being found in its stores. The company stated this is a precautionary measure to prevent the creation of hate symbols, acknowledging the noose as a threatening symbol of racism. This change was prompted by recent customer reports and follows similar occurrences in previous years, coinciding with broader national conversations about systemic racism.

title: Home Depot changes rope sales after nooses found
summary: Home Depot announced changes to its rope sales practices after nooses were found in one of its North Carolina stores. The company, appalled by these incidents, will now sell rope in pre-cut lengths instead of from large spools to address the use of nooses as symbols of racism and hatred. This decision comes amidst ongoing conversations about systemic racism.

title: Home Depot, Norcold, SiriusXM Checks In The Mail
summary: Top Class Actions readers are reportedly receiving settlement checks from several class action lawsuits. Payments include up to $2,441.84 from a Home Depot TCPA settlement, $113.69 from a Norcold RV refrigerator settlement, and $38.45 from a SiriusXM TCPA settlement. The article details the nature of each lawsuit and how consumers qualified for payments.

title: The Home Depot to Require Face Masks in All U.S. Stores
summary: The Home Depot announced that face masks will be required for all shoppers in U.S. stores starting July 22, 2020, with exceptions for small children and those with medical conditions. This measure expands on existing local requirements and associates' mask use, aiming to protect customers and staff during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company will provide masks and remind customers through signage and announcements, while also offering alternative shopping options like curbside pickup and home delivery.

title: Home Depot leans on efficiency analysis for sustainable transport plan
summary: Home Depot is focusing on efficiency analysis to achieve its sustainable transport goals, aiming to reduce Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 40% by 2030 and 50% by 2035. The company optimizes truck loading, utilizes technology for route optimization, and considers taking over tasks from suppliers for greater efficiency. While the retailer has not yet set a target for Scope 3 emissions, it is exploring electrification for its internal fleet, particularly box trucks, as a future path to significantly lower emissions.

title: The Home Depot Announces Renewable Energy Goal and Pledges to Eliminate EPS Foam and PVC Film from Private Brands by 2023 in Annual Responsibility Report
summary: The Home Depot has released its 2020 Responsibility Report, outlining significant sustainability progress and new goals. Key commitments include plans to source 335 megawatts of renewable energy by 2025 and eliminate EPS foam and PVC film from private brand packaging by 2023. The report also highlights efforts in diversity and inclusion, associate support during COVID-19, and community strengthening through The Home Depot Foundation.

title: Home Depot drops Ego power equipment brand, which lands deal with Lowe's
summary: Home Depot has decided to cease carrying the Ego brand of cordless outdoor power equipment as part of a "reset" of its inventory. Following this decision, Ego, developed by Chervon, has secured a new deal with Lowe's. This move indicates a significant shift in retail partnerships for the power equipment brand.

title: 99,000 artificial Christmas trees sold at Home Depot recalled due to burn hazard risk
summary: Approximately 99,000 artificial Christmas trees sold at Home Depot have been recalled due to fire and burn hazards. The recall involves Home Accents Holiday Artificial Christmas Trees with a foot-pedal controller that can overheat, leading to 509 reports of overheating and one burn injury. Consumers are advised to stop using the affected trees, which include specific 7.5 ft. and 9 ft. models from 2019, and contact Willis Electric for resolution.

title: Recall announced for artificial Christmas trees sold at Home Depot
summary: A recall has been issued for nearly 100,000 pre-lit Home Accents Holiday artificial Christmas trees sold at Home Depot last year. The article states there is "a problem" with the trees, leading to the recall notice.

title: Walmart, CVS, Lowe’s among the retailers that will start requiring face coverings on Monday
summary: Walmart, CVS Health Corp., and Lowe's Cos. are implementing new nationwide face covering requirements for customers starting Monday. Walmart has also created a new role, "health ambassador," to help enforce this new rule in its U.S. stores and Sam's Club warehouses. The National Retail Federation encourages all retailers to adopt similar face mask requirements.

title: BJ’s Wholesale Club Appoints Chief Digital Officer
summary: BJ’s Wholesale Club announced the appointment of Monica Schwartz as senior vice president, chief digital officer, effective August 3, 2020. Schwartz, previously from Home Depot, will be responsible for the company’s digital business and will report directly to BJ's President and CEO, Lee Delaney. Her role will focus on scaling and enhancing BJ's digital offerings and capabilities, building on the company's recent progress in this area.

title: BJ’s Wholesale Club names chief digital officer
summary: BJ's Wholesale Club has appointed Monica Schwartz as its new senior vice president and chief digital officer. Schwartz previously held a position at Home Depot before joining BJ's.

title: Regency Centers Evolving and Adapting With CEO Lisa Palmer
summary: Lisa Palmer discusses her journey to becoming CEO of Regency Centers and how the company has grown and adapted over her 24-year tenure. She highlights the importance of the company's culture, community involvement, and strategic advantages, while also touching on her personal experiences with sports and mentorship. Palmer outlines Regency's future goals amidst a rapidly changing retail real estate industry and the company's response to the pandemic and calls for racial justice.

title: Marvin Ellison
summary: Marvin Ellison has been the president and CEO of Lowe’s Companies, Inc., since July 2018, bringing over 30 years of leadership in retail, including experience at J.C. Penney Co. and Home Depot Inc. He holds degrees from The University of Memphis and Emory University and serves on several boards, including FedEx Corporation. Ellison is also recognized for his civic leadership and commitment to mentoring minority youth.

title: How Arthur Blank, Bernie Marcus co-founded Home Depot after being fired
summary: Arthur Blank and Bernie Marcus were fired from Handy Dan Home Improvement in 1978, leading them to co-found Home Depot. Their vision for Home Depot, focused on low prices and well-trained employees, eventually led to its significant success despite initial struggles. Today, Home Depot is a massive retailer, and both Blank and Marcus are billionaires.

title: Trump fires Tennessee Valley Authority chair, cites hiring of foreign workers
summary: President Donald Trump announced the firing of Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) chair, Skip Thompson, and another board member, citing the authority's practice of hiring foreign workers under H1-B visas. Trump also threatened to remove other board members and mandated that the new CEO's salary should not exceed $500,000, significantly less than the previous CEO's $8 million. The decision followed a TV ad criticizing the TVA for replacing American workers with foreign contractors, a move that Senator Lamar Alexander disputes, stating the TVA operates without taxpayer money and has competitive rates.

title: Home Depot adds 3 warehouses as DIY demand grows
summary: Home Depot is expanding its distribution network by adding three new warehouses in the Atlanta area to meet the soaring demand for DIY projects. This expansion is part of a larger $1.2 billion investment announced in 2017 to enhance its supply chain capabilities, including same- and next-day delivery options. The pandemic has accelerated the company's omnichannel strategy, pushing it to adapt quickly with services like curbside pickup and leveraging increased consumer interest in home improvement projects.

title: The Home Depot Opening Three New Distribution Centers in Georgia
summary: The Home Depot announced it will open three new distribution centers in Georgia over the next 18 months to meet growing demand for flexible delivery and pick-up options for Pro and DIY customers. This expansion is expected to create approximately 1,000 new jobs in the greater Atlanta area. These centers include a large facility in Locust Grove for fast store replenishment, a flatbed delivery center in Stonecrest for bulk orders, and an order fulfillment operation in East Point for institutional business customers.

title: Home Depot to open new distribution center in Locust Grove, hiring 600 associates.
summary: Home Depot is opening a new 657,600 square foot distribution center in Locust Grove, Georgia, located at 3150 Highway 42 South. This facility is the first of three planned for the metro Atlanta area and is expected to create 600 new jobs, increasing Home Depot's total employment in Henry County to over 1,600 associates. The new center is part of a larger development in Gardner Logistics Park, and the city is implementing transportation improvements, including new traffic signals and road upgrades, to support the increased activity.

title: Home Depot opening 3 new Georgia distribution centers, with 1,000 jobs
summary: The Home Depot is opening three new distribution centers in Georgia, creating 1,000 jobs. This expansion contributes to the over 5,000 new jobs the company has generated in Georgia over the past five years through various distribution and office openings. The largest new facility is a 657,600-square-foot distribution center located in Locust Grove.

title: Home Depot adds three DCs in Atlanta area
summary: Home Depot plans to open three new distribution centers in the Atlanta metropolitan area over the next 18 months to expand its fulfillment and delivery capabilities. These facilities will serve both professional contractors and the growing do-it-yourself (DIY) customer base, a segment that has seen a significant boost due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The expansion includes centers specializing in store replenishment, flatbed deliveries, and same/next-day deliveries for institutional clients.

title: Fertitta-backed blank check firm to take Hillman public in $2.64 billion deal
summary: Hillman Group Inc, backed by private equity, is set to go public through a merger with billionaire Tilman Fertitta’s blank-check firm, Landcadia Holdings III Inc, in a deal valued at $2.64 billion. The transaction will be partly financed by $500 million cash from Landcadia's IPO and a $375 million investment from Columbia Threadneedle Investments and Wells Capital Management. The deal is expected to close in Q2 2021, with Hillman listing on Nasdaq under the ticker “HLMN”.

title: The Home Depot Donates a Half Million Kids Workshop Kits to Nonprofits; Offers Live-Stream and Digital Workshops
summary: The Home Depot has donated over 500,000 Kids Workshop kits to more than 100 nonprofit organizations and schools nationwide while in-store classes are paused. The company is actively introducing virtual DIY project content for children and has launched live-streaming "Homeowner 101" workshops for adults led by expert associates. These initiatives aim to continue engagement with DIY activities for both kids and adults, with new content being added regularly.

title: Home Depot and Lowe’s are in a race against time and each other
summary: Home Depot and Lowe's are both investing significantly in their supply chains to speed up delivery and pickup of online orders for both professional and DIY customers. Home Depot plans to open three new distribution centers in Georgia as part of a $1.2 billion investment, aiming for same- and next-day delivery capabilities for 90% of the U.S. population. Lowe's is opening a second direct fulfillment center in California and plans to expand with 50 cross dock delivery terminals, seven bulk distribution centers, and four e-commerce fulfillment centers to achieve two-day delivery for almost 100% of its customers, as part of a $1.7 billion supply chain upgrade.

title: Chewy Founder Ryan Cohen, Who Sold His Company For $3 Billion, Shares His Best Advice
summary: Ryan Cohen, founder of Chewy, shares his entrepreneurial journey, including overcoming 100 investor rejections and successfully building Chewy into a multi-billion dollar online pet retailer. He emphasizes customer obsession, strategic risk-taking, and the timeless advice from his father to prioritize customer happiness over immediate profit.

title: Home Depot Doubles Comp. Sale Growth Rate in Q2 Due to Remodeling Amid COVID
summary: Home Depot saw its comparable sales double in Q2 2020 due to a surge in home remodeling projects during the COVID-19 pandemic, despite canceling typical spring sales events. The company adapted its business model, moving away from usual growth indicators like GDP and housing data, as customers used stimulus checks and saved money from other activities to fund home improvements. This unexpected boost highlights a shift in consumer behavior and retail dynamics during the pandemic, benefiting major home improvement retailers while other sectors struggled.

title: QuinStreet acquires home improvement company Modernize
summary: QuinStreet, a performance marketing company, has acquired Modernize, an Austin, TX-based home improvement company, for $67.5 million in cash and notes. Modernize connects homeowners with home service providers and has a network of over 1,000 contractors. This acquisition is expected to add $50-60 million to QuinStreet's FY2021 revenue and is projected to be immediately accretive to the company's EBITDA.

title: Home Depot sees sales boost as Americans take up do-it-yourself projects during pandemic
summary: Home Depot experienced a significant sales boost during the initial phase of the COVID-19 pandemic as Americans, confined to their homes, focused on do-it-yourself projects. Foot traffic to stores surged by approximately 35% above 2019 levels since April, and comparable sales rose by 6.4% in the fiscal first quarter, more than doubling the previous year's growth. Despite an anticipated downturn, the company adapted its business model to meet the unexpected demand, though some stagnation was expected as summer ended and unemployment benefits ceased.

title: The Home Depot Announces Second Quarter Results; Declares Quarterly Dividend of $1.50 Per Share
summary: The Home Depot reported strong second-quarter fiscal 2020 results, with sales increasing 23.4% to $38.1 billion and net earnings rising to $4.3 billion. The company also declared a quarterly cash dividend of $1.50 per share. These results underscore the effectiveness of their "One Home Depot" investment strategy and their ability to adapt to current market demands, including significant investments in associate benefits.

title: Home Depot and Walmart Are Stay-at-Home Winners
summary: The article highlights Home Depot and Walmart as beneficiaries of the COVID-19 pandemic, with both companies reporting strong quarterly results. This success is attributed to people spending more time at home and consequently increasing their spending on home-related purchases.

title: America goes online to resupply and sales at Walmart.com boom
summary: Walmart's online sales nearly doubled in the second quarter as Americans relied on online shopping during the pandemic, and U.S. in-store sales also jumped 9.3%. Despite strong performance and exceeding Wall Street expectations, the company faced increased COVID-19 related costs and investor concern over the cessation of government stimulus packages. This raises questions about sustained consumer activity in the absence of further economic relief.

title: Pandemic-inspired home reno boom pushes B.C. lumber to record highs
summary: B.C. lumber prices have soared to record highs due to producers cutting production too deeply at the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, coupled with a strong U.S. housing market and unprecedented home renovation boom. This created a significant supply-and-demand imbalance, with lumber inventories running very low and order files stretching into the fall. While the high prices offer temporary financial relief, they do not resolve underlying issues like shrinking timber supplies and labor shortages in the B.C. forestry sector.

title: Assurant Acquires Fixt Onsite Mobile Device, Smartphone, Tablet Repair Company
summary: Assurant ($AIZ) has acquired Fixt, an on-demand mobile device support and repair services provider for smartphones and tablet computers. Financial terms were not disclosed for this M&A deal. Fixt's platform allows consumers to schedule local, onsite repairs and manages logistics for employee devices, with a network of over 1,500 repair technicians.

title: Lowe’s targets pros, DIY market with new tool-rental program
summary: Lowe's is launching a new tool-rental program, starting with its first location in South End, to attract both professional contractors and DIY customers. The company expects these tool rental stores to expand nationwide within the next few years. This initiative aims to meet customer demand and broaden its service offerings to a wider market.

title: Big-Box Retailers’ Profits Surge as Pandemic Marches On (Published 2020)
summary: Walmart, Target, and other big-box retailers experienced a significant surge in profits during the COVID-19 pandemic, driven by their one-stop shopping convenience and e-commerce growth. Target reported its greatest quarterly sales increase in company history, while Walmart doubled its e-commerce sales and Home Depot saw sales rise over 23 percent. This success stands in contrast to many other retail sectors that faced bankruptcies during the same period.

title: Target expands same-day pickup to 1,500 stores, as curbside drives sales for them, Walmart and others
summary: Target is expanding its same-day pickup service, including fresh and frozen grocery items, to 1,500 stores, following a 730% growth in its Drive Up curbside pickup service in Q2 2020. This expansion reflects a broader trend among retailers like Walmart, Best Buy, and Macy's, where curbside and online shopping have surged due to the coronavirus pandemic. The convenience of these services is driving significant sales growth, with Target's digital sales increasing by 195% and Walmart's by 97% in the second quarter.

title: Supplier Spotlight: BlueFletch, Coded for Success
summary: BlueFletch, an Atlanta-based software and mobile application services provider, has been a key partner for The Home Depot since 2011. During the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, BlueFletch rapidly developed two critical mobile apps within two weeks. These apps enabled The Home Depot to implement curbside pickup and efficiently count in-store customers, demonstrating BlueFletch's agility and problem-solving capabilities in a time of crisis.

title: Lowe’s targets professionals, and its main competitor Home Depot, with new services
summary: Lowe's is reportedly gaining market share, particularly among professionals, a group traditionally favoring Home Depot. The company announced strong second-quarter results, beating expectations for profit and sales, and reported a significant U.S. same-store sales growth of 35.1%. This growth is attributed to new services targeting professionals and increased consumer spending on home improvement during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Home Decor Sales Are Booming at Target and HomeGoods Amid the Pandemic
summary: Home decor and improvement sales have surged during the pandemic as people adapt their homes for remote work, schooling, and fitness. Retailers like Target and TJX Companies (HomeGoods, TJ Maxx) reported significant year-over-year growth in home-related categories, alongside traditional home improvement stores like Lowe's and Home Depot. This trend is expected to continue as more people work from home, indicating a lasting shift in consumer spending habits.

title: This Retail ETF Strategy Is Crushing it this Year
summary: The article highlights the success of the ProShares Long Online/Short Stores ETF (CLIX), which has achieved an over 87% year-to-date gain by capitalizing on both the growth of e-commerce and the decline of brick-and-mortar retail. The strategy benefits from increased online sales and widespread store closures and bankruptcies among traditional retailers. Recent data indicate a significant surge in e-commerce sales, underscoring the fund's continued potential.

title: The Home Depot Mobilizes to Support Communities Facing Hurricane Laura
summary: The Home Depot is activating its virtual Hurricane Command Center to support communities in Texas and Louisiana bracing for Hurricane Laura, coordinating the movement of over 230 trucks with emergency supplies. The Home Depot Foundation is also working with non-profit partners to provide immediate assistance and is ready to process grants for associates affected by the storm through The Homer Fund.

title: Atlanta developer closes on land, secures $44M construction loan for Home Depot's new Hillsborough warehouse
summary: An Atlanta developer has successfully closed on the land and secured a $44 million construction loan for Home Depot's new warehouse in Hillsborough County, Florida. This development signifies the progress of Home Depot's Gibsonton warehouse project, with the same developer also constructing a warehouse for Amazon in Temple Terrace.

title: Is Headline CPI Inflation "Fake News"?
summary: The article discusses the Federal Reserve's adjusted monetary policy to allow inflation to average 2 percent over time, suggesting interest rates will remain near zero. It questions the accuracy of the official Consumer Price Index (CPI) by comparing it to alternative inflation data from ShadowStats, which indicates a much higher inflation rate. The author suggests that gold could be a good hedge against inflation, noting that institutional investors are beginning to add gold to their portfolios.

title: Apple stock drop makes history with $179B loss
summary: Apple experienced the largest single-day market cap drop for a U.S. listed company, losing over $179.92 billion (8%) in value on Thursday. This significant decline followed a period where Apple had recently become the first U.S. company to reach a $2 trillion valuation. Despite the drop, its market cap remains at the $2 trillion level, and analysts largely maintain a "strong buy" rating as the company prepares to release a 5G iPhone.

title: Supplier Spotlight: D-Unique Tools Builds Business into Global Supplier
summary: D-Unique Tools, founded by Mike Hunter in 1991, grew from a small local supplier to a global business thanks to a partnership with The Home Depot and the innovative Universal Square tool. Led by Mike and his daughter Nanette, the company overcame early challenges and leveraged The Home Depot's Supplier Diversity Program to expand its reach to over 2,000 stores across North America and the UK. The family-owned business continues to thrive, with Nanette as president and her father as chairman, offering a product line of about 20 unique items.

title: Grand Rounds Secures $175 Million Investment, Led by The Carlyle Group, to Accelerate Clinical Navigation and Virtual Primary Care
summary: Grand Rounds, a leader in healthcare quality and clinical navigation, announced a $175 million investment led by The Carlyle Group. The funding will be used to accelerate clinical navigation and virtual primary care accessibility, helping the company scale to meet the growing needs of its six million members across 130+ employers. This investment underscores the expanding role of digital health and healthcare navigation in improving patient outcomes and reducing costs.

title: Grand Rounds lands $175M cash infusion backed by The Carlyle Group
summary: Grand Rounds, a personal healthcare assistant company, has secured a $175 million funding round led by The Carlyle Group, bringing its total funding to $270 million and valuing the company at $1.34 billion. The company plans to use the new funds to accelerate clinical navigation and virtual primary care initiatives, having seen rapid growth and increased service usage by 55% over the past year, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic. Grand Rounds uses data and algorithms to connect over 6 million workers from companies like Walmart and Home Depot with healthcare providers and services.

title: The Home Depot Expands Livestream Workshop Offerings with Hurricane & Storm Preparedness Class Starting September 14
summary: The Home Depot is launching a new Hurricane & Storm Preparedness Livestream Workshop starting September 14, in response to a predicted record-high hurricane season.
