These free digital workshops will provide essential tips and resources for families to prepare their homes for hurricanes, tornadoes, and floods. The initiative also highlights Home Depot's broader commitment to disaster relief and community support through The Home Depot Foundation.

title: Home Depot expands Black Friday deals to limit store crowding amid pandemic
summary: Home Depot announced it is expanding its Black Friday deals to start in early November and run through December to avoid store crowding during the COVID-19 pandemic. The retailer aims to reduce the "frenzied one-day shopping" experience by offering extended sales both in-store and online, along with free shipping on over 1 million items. All Home Depot stores will also be closed on Thanksgiving Day.

title: Home Depot building first new Greater Washington store in more than a decade
summary: The Home Depot is constructing its first new store in the Greater Washington area in over a decade. This new store is located in Haymarket and is part of a larger, long-planned shopping center.

title: Home Depot Changing Up Black Friday Due to Current Situations
summary: Home Depot announced changes to its Black Friday strategy for the upcoming holiday season, primarily to help control the spread of COVID-19. Instead of a single day of sales, the retailer will offer Black Friday prices throughout November and December, both in-store and online. This aims to reduce crowds and provide a less stressful shopping experience.

title: Home Depot could become marquee tenant at I-49 Industrial Center
summary: Home Depot may become the main tenant at the I-49 Industrial Center in south Kansas City, occupying a 297,600-square-foot distribution facility. This move is projected to create at least 48 new jobs for the area. The potential facility is referred to as "Project Rhino."

title: J&J Snack Foods names Walmart, Coca Cola, Home Depot veteran Ken Plunk as CFO
summary: J&J Snack Foods Corp. has appointed Ken Plunk as senior vice president and CFO, effective September 21, 2020. Plunk brings extensive corporate and operational finance experience from leadership roles at Walmart, Home Depot, and Coca-Cola, having previously overseen financial planning and analysis for Walmart's international portfolio. He also served as CFO for Walmart China and held senior finance positions for Sam's Club and U.S. finance.

title: Home Depot Is Selling A 12-Foot Skeleton Just In Time For Spooky Season And People Are Obsessed
summary: Home Depot's 12-foot skeleton is a highly sought-after Halloween decoration, captivating customers despite its massive size and assembly challenges. The article highlights the social media frenzy around this $300 item, with many declaring it a must-have for the 2020 spooky season. Although currently sold out, its popularity underscores a collective desire for lighthearted fun during a challenging year.

title: About 3,500 US Companies Sue Over Trump-Imposed Chinese Tariffs
summary: Around 3,500 U.S. companies, including major firms like Tesla, Ford, and Target, have filed lawsuits against the Trump administration for imposing tariffs on over $300 billion in Chinese goods. These lawsuits allege that the administration failed to impose tariffs within the required 12-month period and did not comply with administrative procedures, challenging the "unbounded and unlimited trade war" with China. This legal action comes after the World Trade Organization found the U.S. breached global trading rules with its tariffs against China.

title: Made in America: Amid tariffs and coronavirus, domestically produced flooring may gain preference. - April 2020
summary: This article discusses how tariffs on Chinese imports and the potential impact of the coronavirus on the supply chain may lead to increased preference for domestically produced flooring in the U.S. It highlights the growth in U.S. manufacturing across various flooring categories including carpet, resilient, ceramic, hardwood, laminate, and rugs, identifying key domestic players and their market shares. The article suggests that these external pressures could encourage a "Made in America" trend in the flooring industry.

title: Roundup Class Action Lawsuit Claims Home Depot Failed to Warn
summary: A proposed Roundup class action lawsuit against Home Depot, filed by plaintiff James Weeks, alleges the retailer failed to warn consumers about the herbicide's cancer-causing chemicals under California's Proposition 65. The U.S. District Court judge allowed an amended complaint to clarify these claims, denying Home Depot's argument that federal law preempts the state law action regarding "point-of-sale" warnings. The lawsuit claims Home Depot knew of the risks associated with Roundup but continued to sell it without adequate warnings on shelves, despite the active ingredient glyphosate being linked to various cancers and listed as a carcinogen under Proposition 65.

title: Home Depot’s loyalty update gets mobile-first treatment
summary: Home Depot has updated its Pro Xtra loyalty program, integrating it with a mobile app to offer home-improvement professionals easier ways to earn and redeem points. The app provides a "mobile-first" experience, allowing users to track purchases and savings via a virtual ID barcode, and includes gamified features to encourage repeat business. This move reflects Home Depot's broader strategy of leveraging technology to enhance customer engagement and capitalize on strong sales growth seen during the pandemic.

title: The Home Depot Names Ted Decker President and Chief Operating Officer; Announces Additional Senior Leadership Promotions
summary: The Home Depot announced that Edward "Ted" P. Decker has been named president and chief operating officer, effective October 5, 2020. This promotion is part of several senior leadership changes aimed at strengthening the company's strategic leadership and operational efficiency. Other key promotions include Ann-Marie Campbell to EVP of U.S. stores and international operations, Jeff Kinnaird to EVP of merchandising, Michael Rowe to president of The Home Depot Canada, and Richard McPhail to additionally oversee corporate strategy.

title: The Home Depot announces five senior leadership promotions - Atlanta Business Chronicle
summary: The Home Depot has announced five senior leadership promotions, with Edward “Ted” P. Decker appointed as president and COO, effective October 5. CEO Craig Menear stated that these promotions aim to strengthen leadership and operational efficiency, allowing him to focus on the company's long-term growth and strategic positioning.

title: Berkshire Crossing Shopping Center sold to subsidiary of Michigan-based real estate investment trust
summary: The Berkshire Crossing Shopping Center in Pittsfield was sold for $16.8 million to Agree Stores LLC, a subsidiary of Michigan-based Agree Realty Corp. The 14.9-acre property, which houses 16 stores including Walmart and Home Depot, was acquired from Brixmor Property Group. Agree Realty, founded in 1971, specializes in acquiring and developing properties leased to industry-leading retail tenants, owning 936 properties in 46 states as of June 30.

title: Shaking Up Aging in Place
summary: The Home Depot has launched a new "Independent Living" program in partnership with National Seating & Mobility (NSM) to cater to the growing senior market wishing to age in place. The program offers in-home consultations and installation services for accessibility modifications like ramps, stairlifts, and grab bars, initially rolling out in select New Jersey and Missouri stores. This initiative aims to address the significant demand for home modifications as a large percentage of the aging population prefers to remain in their current homes.

title: Industrial Distribution's 2020 Big 50 List
summary: Industrial Distribution's 2020 Big 50 List ranks industrial distributors based on their 2019 sales figures, acknowledging the unprecedented challenges faced by the industry due to the pandemic. The article provides a concise reference list of the top 50 companies, along with methodology and additional resources such as video countdowns and editor contacts. It highlights the mixed scenarios distributors encountered, from record sales in 2019 to pandemic-induced setbacks and ongoing initiatives to gain market share.

title: The Home Depot Announces 2020 Innovation Award Winners
summary: The Home Depot announced its 2020 Innovation Award winners, recognizing top product innovations in various categories. The Overall Winner, the Frigidaire Air Fry Range, and First Runner Up, the Masterbuilt Gravity-Fed Grill/Smoker, highlighted breakthroughs in cooking technology. The company also honored several other finalists and presented additional supplier awards for environmental impact, interconnected customer experience, marketing innovation, and supplier diversity.

title: Business Is Good If You’re a Builder, but Will It Last?
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has unexpectedly fueled a booming business for new-home builders as Americans seek more comfortable and spacious living arrangements. However, this momentum faces challenges from supply chain disruptions, soaring lumber prices, and persistent labor shortages. The article explores how builders are adapting to these issues and future uncertainties while highlighting the shift in housing demand towards suburbs and the increased reliance on virtual operations in the home-buying process.

title: ETF of the Week: iShares U.S. Home Construction ETF (ITB)
summary: This article discusses the iShares U.S. Home Construction ETF (ITB), highlighting its performance and the factors driving the homebuilding sector's resilience during the COVID-19 pandemic. It notes that the ETF offers exposure to U.S. homebuilding and related industries, featuring strong returns compared to the S&P 500. The piece attributes this growth to a shift in living preferences and low-interest rates, creating a strong market for homebuilders.

title: Best Work-Life Balance 2020
summary: Comparably has released its lists for the Top 100 highest-rated companies for Work-Life Balance in 2020, based on anonymous employee feedback. The lists are divided into Large Companies (over 500 employees) and Small/Mid-Size Companies (500 employees or fewer). The methodology involved sentiment ratings from employees over a 12-month period, with specific criteria for company inclusion based on employee participation.

title: The Home Depot Expands Pro Xtra Loyalty Program
summary: The Home Depot has expanded its Pro Xtra loyalty program, introducing new benefits and rewards for its Pro customers. Members can now earn rewards for in-store purchases and redeem perks like Tool Rental Perks and Pro Xtra Dollars via the Home Depot mobile app. The program's new mobile-first design, informed by customer feedback, aims to offer a more personalized experience, helping Pros save time and money.

title: The Most Important Question You Can Ask Your Employees, According to Home Depot's Co-Founder
summary: Arthur Blank, co-founder of Home Depot, emphasizes the importance of a strong corporate culture in his new book, "Good Company." He shares insights from his career, including experiences at Home Depot and his subsequent ventures, highlighting the impact of values-driven leadership and employee empowerment. Blank suggests that the ultimate measure of a company's culture is whether employees believe the organization is "worthy of your life."

title: Motel 6, Home Depot Fire Dallas Ad Agency Over Founder's Racially Insensitive Remarks
summary: Motel 6 and The Home Depot severed ties with their long-time ad agency, Dallas-based The Richards Group, after the agency's founder, Stan Richards, made racially insensitive comments during an internal meeting. Richards admitted to saying "It's too Black" when reviewing a proposed multicultural campaign for Motel 6. Both companies cited their zero-tolerance policies for discrimination and quickly terminated their contracts, with Cracker Barrel also withdrawing consideration of The Richards Group for their advertising business.

title: The Home Depot Rental Opens New Rental Centers, Operations Facilities
summary: The Home Depot Rental has announced the opening of 10 new rental centers and rental operations facilities, expanding its services for both customers and professional contractors. These new locations and facilities aim to enhance the rental experience, provide a wider assortment of large equipment, and improve fleet management efficiency. The company is strategically mapping these new centers to meet growing market demands and plans for further expansion.

title: Port KC could issue bonds for Home Depot facility, Platform Ventures spec soon
summary: Port KC is considering authorizing $70 million in bonds to fund 664,200 square feet of new industrial construction at the I-49 Industrial Center. This includes a possible 297,600-square-foot rail-served distribution center for The Home Depot Inc. and a speculative project by Platform Ventures. The Home Depot facility is currently undergoing due diligence.

title: Home Depot, Motel 6 Drop Richards Group Ad Agency Over Founder's Racist Remark
summary: Home Depot and Motel 6 have severed ties with advertising agency Richards Group following reports that its founder, Stan Richards, made a racist comment about a proposed ad campaign. Richards allegedly stated that a Motel 6 ad was "too Black" and would not resonate with the chain's "significant White supremacist constituents" during an internal agency meeting. The incident has led to a number of consumer companies cutting their relationships with the agency.

title: Motel 6 and Home Depot Drop Ad Agency After Its Founder Calls Ad ‘Too Black’ (Published 2020)
summary: Motel 6, Home Depot, and Keurig Dr Pepper have terminated their relationships with The Richards Group advertising agency. This decision followed reports that the agency's 87-year-old founder, Stan Richards, made racist remarks, describing a proposed Motel 6 ad as "too Black" and referencing "white supremacist constituents" during an internal meeting. The companies cited outrage and immediately began seeking new advertising partners.

title: Friend Tire enters Florida market, leases industrial space
summary: Friend Tire Company, a subsidiary of Yokohama Rubber, has expanded into the Florida market by leasing a 46,020-square-foot industrial space in Four Corners Business Park in Davenport. The new facility will serve as a regional distribution center for the wholesale tire company, aiming to enhance its supply chain in the Southeast. Colliers International facilitated the lease transaction, highlighting the strategic location with excellent access to major interstates and key markets like Orlando and Tampa.

title: Sam's Club expands autonomous floor-sweeping robots to all U.S. stores
summary: Sam's Club is expanding its partnership with Brain Corp to deploy autonomous floor-scrubbing robots to all its U.S. stores, totaling around 600 locations. This initiative builds on Walmart's earlier collaboration with Brain Corp and also includes an expanded shelf analytics pilot with cleaning company Tennant to improve pricing accuracy and product availability. The move highlights a growing trend of robotics in big box retail to enhance efficiency and promote contactless environments.

title: WD-40 CEO reveals 3 of the craziest ways his lubricating spray has been used
summary: WD-40's CEO, Garry Ridge, highlights some unconventional uses for the company's famous lubricating spray, including deterring squirrels from bird feeders and freeing a burglar from an air conditioning duct. The article also notes the company's strong sales growth during the COVID-19 pandemic, attributed to increased home renovation activities. WD-40's fourth fiscal quarter saw a 5% increase in sales year-over-year, with significant surges in the Americas and EMEA regions.

title: The Home Depot Expands At-Home Learning Resources for Kids with Virtual Field Trips
summary: The Home Depot has expanded its educational resources for children by launching a new "Virtual Field Trips" video series, providing behind-the-scenes tours from suppliers. This initiative aims to support families and teachers with free, interactive online educational projects, building on its existing Science Fair Central platform and monthly kids' workshops. The program kicks off with features on Bonnie Plants and Back to the Roots, offering engaging content and accompanying DIY projects.

title: Home Depot Won a Lot of Customers During the Pandemic. The Trick Is Keeping Them.
summary: Home Depot unexpectedly saw a surge in customer traffic to both its online and physical stores during the pandemic, despite initially preparing for a drop. This increase was driven by people spending stay-at-home savings and stimulus checks on home-improvement projects. As a result, the company reported its strongest quarterly sales growth in nearly 20 years, with May-to-July revenue up 23% to $38.1 billion compared to the previous year.

title: STREETWISE: Home Depot thrives during the pandemic
summary: Home Depot has successfully navigated the COVID-19 pandemic by leveraging its "One Home Depot" strategy, focusing on omnichannel capabilities and an interconnected shopping experience. The company has seen significant growth in sales and earnings, partly due to strategic investments in its online platform and in-store technologies like automated lockers and digital price labels. These initiatives, coupled with its ability to negotiate low prices with suppliers, have allowed Home Depot to thrive despite challenges faced by other retailers.

title: Home Depot won a lot of customers during the pandemic. The trick is keeping them.
summary: Home Depot saw a significant surge in sales during the COVID-19 pandemic as customers invested in home improvement projects. The company credits its robust digital technology and cloud infrastructure for handling the increased demand, enabling services like curbside pickup and efficient online order fulfillment. Home Depot is focused on retaining these new customers by continuing to invest in diverse shopping capabilities and supporting both novice and experienced DIYers.

title: 20 Minutes With: Home Depot Co-Founder Arthur Blank
summary: Home Depot co-founder Arthur Blank discusses his philosophy of "good capitalism," emphasizing balancing profitability with social responsibility. He shares insights on personalizing large companies, addressing societal cynicism towards corporations, and navigating public health concerns in his diverse businesses. Blank also comments on Black Lives Matter protests in the NFL and the importance of supporting social activism.

title: Home Depot debuts virtual field trips for kids
summary: Home Depot has launched a new series of "Virtual Field Trips" catering to children, expanding its existing DIY workshop initiatives. These digital tours, featuring the retailer's suppliers, aim to educate kids on how products reach store shelves. This effort, in collaboration with Discovery Education, also plans to introduce more online resources and projects to the Science Fair Central platform in Spring 2021, aligning with the growing need for remote learning and entertainment during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Home Depot Canada exposes private customer data following systems error
summary: Home Depot Canada has experienced a data leak where customer information, including names, email addresses, order numbers, and the last four digits of payment cards, was accidentally sent to other customers due to a systems error. While the company stated only a "very small number of customers" were affected, some individuals reported receiving hundreds of unsolicited emails. Security experts warn that this leaked data could be leveraged by malicious actors for sophisticated phishing attacks, urging Home Depot to guide customers on how to identify and avoid such scams.

title: Lowe’s Is Said to Be in Talks to Acquire HD Supply
summary: Lowe's Cos. (LOW) is reportedly in preliminary discussions to acquire building products distributor HD Supply Holdings Inc. (HDS). While discussions have occurred with advisers, no final decision has been made, and Lowe's does not currently plan to proceed with a deal despite recent approaches. HD Supply was previously owned by Lowe's competitor, Home Depot.

title: Owner of Vans and The North Face buys Supreme for $2.1 billion in big streetwear bet
summary: VF Corp, owner of Vans and The North Face, acquired streetwear brand Supreme for $2.1 billion in a strategic move to bolster its presence in the booming streetwear market. This acquisition aims to grow Supreme's revenue from $500 million to over $1 billion within a few years, leveraging VF Corp's expertise in rehabilitating brands and Supreme's strong direct-to-consumer sales model and rapid product release cycle. The deal, which saw VF Corp shares rise 14%, maintains Supreme's independent management and creative control.

title: Newmark Completes Sale of Off-Market Home Depot-Occupied Property for $34 Million
summary: Newmark successfully brokered the sale of an off-market retail property in Paterson, New Jersey, occupied by Home Depot, for $34 million. The 120,000-square-foot building sits on 10 acres and features a long-term ground lease. This transaction highlights the strong demand for properties with investment-grade tenants and long-term triple-net leases, especially for essential businesses during the pandemic.

title: Here are the businesses closing their doors on Thanksgiving
summary: Many major retailers and businesses are opting to close their doors on Thanksgiving this year, a shift from previous years. This decision allows their employees and customers to spend time with family, with some companies also citing safety concerns due to the coronavirus pandemic. As a result, Black Friday sales are largely expected to begin online or in stores on Friday morning, bringing back a more traditional start to the holiday shopping season.

title: Building Material Consolidation Kicks Into High Gear
summary: The building material sector is experiencing a significant surge in M&A activity, particularly driven by private equity investments, following a slowdown earlier in the year due to COVID-19. Numerous high-profile deals involving major distributors like US LBM, Foundation Building Materials, HD Supply, and PrimeSource have been announced, indicating a "fever pitch" in consolidation. This increased activity suggests a substantial shake-up in the market, despite ongoing challenges in commercial construction and potential shifts in the residential sector.

title: $8B deal as Home Depot reunites with HD Supply
summary: Home Depot is set to acquire its former subsidiary, HD Supply, in an $8 billion deal. This acquisition will bolster Home Depot's presence in the contractor and professional markets, which have seen significant growth during the pandemic. HD Supply specializes in maintenance, repair, and operations products for the multifamily and hospitality sectors.

title: Reuniting: Home Depot Buying HD Supply in $8B Deal
summary: The Home Depot is reacquiring HD Supply for approximately $8 billion, 13 years after divesting the industrial products distributor. This deal positions Home Depot to expand its presence in the fragmented $55 billion Maintenance, Repair, and Operations (MRO) marketplace, building on its existing MRO business and recent acquisition of Interline Brands. The transaction is expected to close in Home Depot's fiscal fourth quarter, by January 31, 2021.

title: Home Depot reunites with HD Supply
summary: The Home Depot is reacquiring HD Supply Holdings, Inc. in an $8 billion deal, thirteen years after selling it off. This acquisition aims to strengthen Home Depot's position in the maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) market, complementing its existing MRO business with HD Supply's product offerings and distribution network. The transaction is expected to close in Home Depot's fourth quarter.

title: HD Supply Holdings, Inc. Announces Agreement to be Acquired by The Home Depot, Inc.
summary: HD Supply Holdings, Inc. announced its definitive agreement to be acquired by The Home Depot, Inc. for $56 per share in cash. The all-cash tender offer has been unanimously approved by the Boards of Directors of both companies and is expected to close during The Home Depot's fiscal fourth quarter, ending January 31, 2021. This acquisition aims to benefit customers, associates, and shareholders, strengthening the living space maintenance professional segment.

title: Home Depot Reunites With HD Supply in Deal Catering to Pros
summary: Home Depot Inc. has agreed to acquire building products distributor HD Supply Holdings Inc. for approximately $8.7 billion, reuniting the companies over a decade after their split. This acquisition aims to strengthen Home Depot's position in the professional contractor market, which has seen increased demand during the pandemic. The deal is expected to contribute to Home Depot's earnings and was announced shortly after rival Lowe's Cos. was also reported to be in preliminary talks with HD Supply.

title: Home Depot to buy back HD Supply in $8 bln deal
summary: Home Depot announced its acquisition of HD Supply Holdings Inc. for approximately $8 billion, aiming to regain control over the industrial materials wholesaler it spun off over a decade ago. The deal, offering $56 per share, seeks to expand Home Depot's reach into building utility and maintenance products, with the company expecting the acquisition to be accretive to earnings in 2021.

title: Home Depot Bets $9 Billion on Life After Covid-19
summary: Home Depot's decision to acquire HD Supply for $8.7 billion is seen as a strong indicator of confidence in a post-pandemic economic recovery, particularly for industries like hospitality. HD Supply, which Home Depot previously owned, generates a significant portion of its revenue from supplying maintenance products to hotels and resorts, an industry heavily impacted by the pandemic. This acquisition represents a strategic bet by Home Depot on future growth as the world emerges from the Covid-19 crisis.

title: The Home Depot Announces Agreement to Acquire HD Supply Holdings, Inc.
summary: The Home Depot announced its agreement to acquire HD Supply Holdings, Inc. for approximately $8 billion in cash. This acquisition aims to accelerate sales growth by positioning The Home Depot as a premier provider in the MRO marketplace, serving multifamily and hospitality end markets. The transaction is expected to be accretive to earnings per share in fiscal 2021 and is anticipated to close during The Home Depot's fiscal fourth quarter, which ends January 31, 2021.

title: Home Depot (HD) Buying HD Supply (HDS) In $8 Billion Deal
summary: Home Depot (HD) announced it is reacquiring HD Supply Holdings Inc (HDS) in an $8 billion deal, paying $56 per share. HD Supply, a national distributor of maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) products, was spun out of Home Depot over a decade ago. The acquisition is expected to close in Q4 of Home Depot’s fiscal year and will be funded through cash on hand and debt, with projections for the deal to be accretive to earnings in fiscal 2021.

title: Home Depot to Acquire HD Supply Holdings for $8.7 Billion
summary: The Home Depot Inc. is acquiring HD Supply Holdings Inc. for $8.7 billion, or $56 per share, returning HD Supply to its former owner. This all-cash tender offer is expected to close in Home Depot's fiscal fourth quarter, pending regulatory approval. Both companies' boards have approved the deal, which Home Depot anticipates will accelerate sales growth in the highly fragmented $55 billion MRO market.

title: Home Depot to acquire HD Supply for about $8 billion
summary: The Home Depot announced an agreement to acquire HD Supply Holdings, Inc. for approximately $8 billion, purchasing all outstanding shares for $56 per share. This acquisition is expected to make Home Depot a leader in the MRO market, accelerating sales growth by better serving customers in the fragmented $55 billion marketplace. The sale is subject to regulatory approvals and is expected to be completed by January 1, 2021, funded by cash on hand and debt.

title: The Home Depot Announces Third Quarter Results; Plans to Invest Approximately $1 Billion in Annualized Permanent Compensation Enhancements for Frontline, Hourly Associates
summary: The Home Depot reported strong third-quarter 2020 results, with sales increasing by 23.2% to $33.5 billion and net earnings rising to $3.4 billion. The company announced plans to invest approximately $1 billion in annualized permanent compensation enhancements for frontline, hourly associates, transitioning from temporary COVID-19 related bonuses. This investment reflects continued outsized demand for home improvement projects and the company's commitment to its associates.

title: Home Depot boosts staff pay by $1 bln after uninterrupted sales surge
summary: Home Depot announced it will spend an additional $1 billion annually on employee wages, transitioning some pandemic-era benefits to permanent pay increases for frontline hourly staff. This move follows a sustained surge in demand for home improvement products due to the COVID-19 pandemic and a strengthening housing market, even as the company's stock experienced a slight dip despite beating quarterly sales and profit estimates.

title: Home Depot Plans Workforce Investment as Pandemic Brings Another Strong Quarter
summary: Home Depot reported strong sales growth in its latest quarter, driven by increased home-improvement projects during the pandemic. The company's revenue exceeded expectations, reaching $33.54 billion, with same-store sales growing 24% year-over-year. In response to its strong performance, Home Depot also announced a permanent increase in compensation for its front-line workers, a program estimated to cost around $1 billion annually.

title: A COVID Shadow Gives Black Friday Retail New Meaning
summary: This article discusses the unique challenges and opportunities for retail during Black Friday 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. It suggests that while the virus casts a shadow, there's potential for revenue boosts, particularly highlighted by the Direxion Daily Retail Bull 3X ETF (RETL B+). The article also touches upon the "K-shaped" recovery and the resilience of U.S. consumers, noting strong spending in certain sectors like home goods.

title: Home Depot seeks MRO dominance with HD Supply acquisition
summary: The Home Depot announced its acquisition of HD Supply Holdings Inc., a distributor of MRO products, for approximately $8 billion. This strategic move aims to accelerate Home Depot's sales growth by enhancing its MRO business and expanding its reach in the fragmented $55-billion marketplace. The acquisition is expected to benefit customers, associates, and shareholders of both companies, strengthening Home Depot's position in the MRO sector.

title: Home Depot Founder Arthur Blank Talks Big New Gifts and His Philanthropic Legacy
summary: Arthur Blank, co-founder of Home Depot and a signatory of the Giving Pledge, discusses his recent significant philanthropic contributions, including $200 million to Children's Healthcare of Atlanta and $20 million to the University of Texas at Austin for stuttering research. He shares how his personal experiences, family values, and new memoir, "Good Company," have shaped his approach to giving, emphasizing investing in children and leveling the playing field for all. His family foundation, which includes his children, continues to support various causes, ensuring his philanthropic legacy will endure.

title: College student fired from Sherwin-Williams after his paint-mixing TikTok videos go viral
summary: A college student, Tony Piloseno, was fired from Sherwin-Williams after his paint-mixing TikTok videos went viral, accumulating over 1.4 million followers. Despite his efforts to propose his TikTok presence as a marketing strategy to the company, he was terminated in July for "gross misconduct," including using company property and embarrassing the company, following a customer complaint about experimental paint mixing. Piloseno maintained he purchased the paint used for videos made outside of customer orders, though he admitted to filming some early videos during work hours.

title: Home Depot reaches $17.5 mln settlement over 2014 data breach
summary: Home Depot has agreed to a $17.5 million settlement with 46 U.S. states and Washington, D.C., concerning a 2014 data breach that exposed payment card data of 40 million customers. The retailer, which had previously incurred $198 million in pre-tax expenses and settled other related litigation, did not admit liability but committed to security upgrades and hiring a chief information security officer. The breach occurred when hackers used a vendor's credentials to access the company's network and deploy custom malware.

title: Attorney General Becerra Announces $17.5 Million Settlement Against Home Depot Over Credit Card Data Breach
summary: California Attorney General Xavier Becerra announced a $17.5 million multistate settlement with The Home Depot, Inc. regarding a 2014 data breach that compromised approximately 40 million customer payment cards. California will receive over $1.8 million from the settlement, which also mandates significant security improvements for Home Depot to prevent future breaches. This settlement reinforces the Attorney General's commitment to holding companies accountable for protecting consumer information, following similar actions against Anthem, Equifax, and Target.

title: Home Depot Agrees to Pay $17.5 Million in Multistate Settlement Following 2014 Data Breach
summary: Home Depot has agreed to pay $17.5 million in a multistate settlement after its 2014 data breach compromised 56 million payment card numbers. The settlement, divided among 46 states and D.C., also mandates that the company implement comprehensive data security practices, including appointing a chief information security officer, providing security training, and enhancing safeguards like encryption and penetration testing. This follows a previous settlement in 2017 with financial institutions affected by the breach.

title: Harley Goes Solar With Over 8,000 Panels Atop Pilgrim Road Plant
summary: Harley-Davidson has installed nearly 8,400 solar panels at its Pilgrim Road Powertrain Operations facility in partnership with WEC Energy Group. This solar farm will generate 2.25 megawatts of power, enough to supply around 400 homes, with the energy being funneled into the grid by We Energies. This initiative is part of Harley-Davidson's commitment to green energy under Jochen Zeits' leadership, although the direct implications for electric motorcycle production like the LiveWire remain uncertain.

title: Is Black Friday canceled this year? How COVID is changing Black Friday 2020
summary: COVID-19 has significantly altered Black Friday 2020, leading many major retailers like Walmart and Target to close on Thanksgiving Day. Retailers are also spreading out deals over several weeks or months to reduce crowds and encouraging online shopping. Additionally, mask requirements are in place, and some stores are enhancing free delivery options.

title: Home Depot Deal Raises Buildings Materials M&A to Record Height
summary: The acquisition of HD Supply Holdings Inc. by Home Depot Inc. for $8.7 billion has pushed North American building materials mergers and acquisitions to a record high of $15.2 billion. This surge in M&A activity is attributed to increased home remodeling during the Covid-19 pandemic and stay-at-home orders. The current deals have surpassed the previous record set in 2007.

title: DICK’S Sporting Goods and Rite Aid Join Coalition to Combat Sale of Fraudulent Goods
summary: DICK'S Sporting Goods, Rite Aid, HP Inc., and OpSec Security have joined the Buy Safe America Coalition to combat the sale of fraudulent goods, urging Congress to pass the INFORM Consumers Act. This act would require online marketplaces to verify seller information, aiming to protect consumers and employees from organized retail crime and counterfeit products, especially with the surge in online holiday shopping.

title: The Home Depot to Open Two New Distribution Centers in Newark Area
summary: The Home Depot announced plans to open two new distribution centers in Perth Amboy, New Jersey, over the next 12 months, creating over 400 new jobs in the tri-state area. This expansion is part of a $1.2 billion investment in its supply chain network to improve flexible customer delivery options for both DIY and Pro customers. The new facilities will enhance same-day and next-day delivery capabilities for bulk, oversized, and appliance orders.

title: 3 out of 4 Americans Built Up Their Home Improvement Skills in 2020, CRAFTSMAN® Built@Home Survey Finds
summary: A new CRAFTSMAN survey found that 78% of Americans honed their home improvement skills during the COVID-19 pandemic, with most wishing for more renovation know-how. The survey detailed top projects, the increase in power tool usage, and a shift towards more advanced renovations in 2021. CRAFTSMAN is also donating $500,000 to Rebuilding Together and Feeding America to support communities impacted by COVID-19.

title: Data Breaches Can Cost $$ – Plus Ongoing Obligations (ask Home Depot): Lessons and Takeaways
summary: This article details the costly settlement Home Depot reached with 46 states and D.C. following its 2014 data breach, which exposed 40 million customer payment cards. Beyond a $17.5 million monetary payment, the settlement mandates extensive security overhauls and ongoing oversight, in addition to over $180 million already paid in litigation. The piece highlights a valuable list of specific information security requirements that businesses can learn from to protect sensitive data and avoid similar penalties.

title: Kroger, other retailers see 'eye-popping profits' as workers reap little benefit
summary: A new report by the Brookings Institution reveals that supermarket chains and other food retailers saw their profits soar by an average of 39% in the first half of the year due to the pandemic, with Kroger's profits jumping 90%. Despite these "eye-popping profits," front-line workers largely reaped little benefit, as many retailers quickly ended "hero pay" and replaced it with less generous bonuses. The report highlights inequalities between worker compensation and company financial performance, prompting unions to press for the reinstatement of hazard pay amidst rising COVID-19 cases.

title: Large retailers’ pandemic earnings continue to soar long after hazard pay ends
summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, large retailers have experienced soaring profits and stock prices, while compensation for their low-wage front-line workers has not seen a proportional increase. Many essential businesses initially offered hazard pay, but most discontinued it by June, even as the pandemic worsened. This disparity is exemplified by ongoing contract disputes between Kroger's Houston division and its union, UFCW Local 455, over reinstating hazard pay and changes to health care and pension plans, despite the company's significant profit growth.

title: Home Depot Credit Card — Financing With No Interest For a Certain Period
summary: The Home Depot credit card offers consumers financing options with no interest for certain periods, depending on purchase amounts. There are two types of consumer cards: the Home Depot Consumer Credit Card and the Home Depot Project Loan Card, neither of which has an annual fee. While store cards don't offer cash-back rewards, Home Depot frequently provides promotional discounts and allows extended return periods for cardholders.

title: Home Depot to pay $20M fine for lead paint violations
summary: Home Depot has agreed to pay a $20.75 million settlement for lead paint violations across the country, marking the highest civil penalty under the Toxic Substances Control Act. The settlement, reached with the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the Justice Department, addresses issues where the company's subcontractors failed to adhere to lead paint regulations in homes built before 1978. Home Depot will also make system-wide changes to ensure contractors are EPA-certified and follow lead-safe practices.

title: Home Depot to Pay $21 Million Penalty for Alleged Lead-Safety Violations
summary: Home Depot Inc. has agreed to pay a $20.75 million penalty in a settlement with U.S. regulators for alleged lead safety violations. The Environmental Protection Agency investigated five customer complaints and found that Home Depot sent uncertified firms to conduct renovations that required certified firms, and that subcontracted firms in some cases failed to follow lead-safe work practices or maintain proper records.

title: Home Depot in trouble after Black Lives Matter dispute with worker
summary: The National Labor Relations Board (NLRB) has ruled that a Minnesota Home Depot store violated federal law by telling an employee to remove a "BLM" marking from their work apron and constructively discharging them when they refused. The NLRB found that the employee's refusal was "protected concerted activity" under the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA) and ordered Home Depot to offer reinstatement and back pay. A dissent argued that the BLM display was not directly related to workplace discrimination.

title: The Home Depot Completes Acquisition of HD Supply
summary: The Home Depot has completed its acquisition of HD Supply Holdings, Inc. for approximately $8 billion, as announced on November 16, 2020. This strategic move aims to enhance Home Depot's services for MRO customers and position it as a premier provider in the $55 billion MRO marketplace. HD Supply, a national distributor of maintenance, repair, and operations products, will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of The Home Depot.

title: The Home Depot Completes Acquisition of HD Supply
summary: The Home Depot has completed its acquisition of HD Supply Holdings, Inc. for approximately $8 billion, aiming to enhance its position in the maintenance, repair, and operations (MRO) marketplace. This acquisition is expected to better serve existing and new MRO customers by combining HD Supply's robust product offering and distribution network with The Home Depot's MRO business. The tender offer resulted in approximately 82.9% of HD Supply's outstanding shares being validly tendered.

title: Atlanta-Based The Home Depot Acquires Key Competitor for $8 Billion
summary: The Home Depot has finalized its acquisition of HD Supply Holdings, Inc. for approximately $8 billion, a deal first announced in mid-November. This acquisition aims to enhance Home Depot's ability to serve MRO customers by integrating HD Supply's distribution network and MRO product offerings. The transaction is expected to be accretive to Home Depot's earnings in fiscal year 2021.

title: More Than 190,000 Ceiling Fans Are Recalled After Blades Detach (Published 2020)
summary: More than 190,000 Hampton Bay 54-inch Mara Indoor/Outdoor ceiling fans, sold through Home Depot, have been recalled because their blades can detach while spinning. The Consumer Product Safety Commission reported 47 incidents of detached blades, with two instances of blades hitting people and four reports of property damage. King of Fans, the distributor, attributed the issue to an "isolated manufacturing defect" and is offering free replacements to affected consumers.

title: Home Depot recalls nearly 200K ceiling fans after reports of blades detaching, injuring people
summary: Home Depot is recalling almost 200,000 "Hampton Bay 54 in. Mara Indoor/Outdoor" ceiling fans after receiving 47 reports of blades detaching, with two incidents causing injuries and four leading to property damage. The recall was issued in conjunction with King of Fans, Inc. due to a manufacturing defect. Buyers are advised to stop using the fans and contact King of Fans for a free replacement.

title: Ceiling fans sold at Home Depot recalled over blades that can fly off
summary: Home Depot has recalled Hampton Bay 54-inch Mara Indoor/Outdoor ceiling fans due to blades detaching, posing an injury risk. Approximately 182,000 units were sold between April and October for about $150. There have been 47 reports of blade detachments, including two minor injuries and four property damage incidents.

title: Ceiling fans sold at Home Depot recalled after blades detach
summary: Over 190,000 Hampton Bay 54-inch Mara Indoor/Outdoor ceiling fans sold exclusively at Home Depot have been recalled due to blades detaching during use, causing injuries and property damage. The recall was voluntarily initiated by King of Fans in cooperation with the CPSC after 47 reports of blade detachment. Consumers are advised to immediately stop using the fans and contact King of Fans for a free replacement if they observe any blade movement issues.

title: Ceiling Fans Sold at Home Depot Recalled After Blades Fly Off
summary: Home Depot has recalled over 190,000 Hampton Bay Mara ceiling fans after reports of blades detaching, causing injuries and property damage. The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission received 47 reports of blades falling off. Owners are advised to stop using the fans immediately and inspect them, with King of Fans offering free replacements for faulty units.

title: Hampton Bay ceiling fans sold at Home Depot recalled
summary: King of Fans has recalled over 190,000 Hampton Bay 54-inch Mara indoor/outdoor ceiling fans sold at Home Depot due to blades detaching during use, causing injuries and property damage. The malfunction is attributed to a manufacturing defect in the fan blade's locking clip assembly. Consumers are advised to stop using the fans, inspect them, and contact King of Fans for a free replacement if issues are found.

title: Atlanta-area Home Depot distribution center bought for $97M
summary: Monmouth Real Estate Investment Corp. acquired a 657,518-square-foot Home Depot distribution center in Locust Grove, Ga., for $97 million. This purchase highlights ongoing investment in logistics and e-commerce infrastructure.

title: The Home Depot Completes Acquisition of HD Supply
summary: The Home Depot has finalized its acquisition of HD Supply Holdings Inc. for $8 billion, bringing the distribution arm back into the company after selling it in 2007. This move is expected to enhance service for both existing and new MRO customers. Home Depot's chairman and CEO, Craig Menear, expressed enthusiasm for the value this acquisition will bring to associates, customers, and shareholders.

title: Ceiling fans sold at Home Depot recalled because blades may spin off
summary: More than 190,000 Hampton Bay 54-inch Mara Indoor/Outdoor ceiling fans sold at Home Depot are being recalled due to the risk of blades detaching during use, potentially causing injury or property damage. King of Fans, the distributor, has received 47 reports of blades detaching, with some causing minor injuries and property damage. Consumers are advised to stop using the fans immediately, check for defects, and contact King of Fans for a free replacement if issues are found.

title: Corpus Christi: 23-Acre Retail Development Planned in Calallen
summary: A Dallas developer, Identity Capital LLC, is planning a 23.4-acre retail development named Nemec Towne Center in Calallen, Corpus Christi. The project, located north of County Road 52 and with frontage on Interstate 69, will proceed in five phases and include privately owned streets. The Nemec family, local landowners, is also involved, and the development is expected to attract various retail chains.

title: 5 stories that will dominate home retail in the year ahead
summary: The article discusses five major events in 2020 that are predicted to profoundly impact home furnishings retail in 2021 and beyond. These include the rise of RH, increased focus on decor from Home Depot and Lowe's, market share gains by Walmart and Target, Wayfair's profitability, and the beginning of a turnaround for Bed Bath & Beyond. The author emphasizes that the pandemic accelerated changes in the retail landscape and more shifts are expected.

title: Grand Opening
summary: The Home Depot opened a new 118,000-square-foot store in Maspeth, Queens, on January 7, 2021, driven by area growth and customer base expansion. This new location features an optimized checkout, specialty showroom, and new storage for Buy Online, Pickup In-Store orders, reflecting a multi-year investment by the company to enhance customer experience. The store currently employs 245 associates, with expectations for future growth.

title: CarMax plans to bring two used-car dealerships to Long Island
summary: CarMax, the largest used-car retailer in the country, is expanding its presence to Long Island with two new dealerships in East Meadow and Smithtown. These locations will serve the New York City area, marking CarMax's entry into the downstate market after years of strategic expansion. The move is well-timed given increased demand for used cars due to economic uncertainty during the COVID-19 pandemic and a shift in new car production.

title: Big-box brands like Home Depot, Target driving Manhattan retail leasing, CBRE report says
summary: A new report by CBRE indicates that big-box brands such as Home Depot and Target are significantly contributing to retail leasing activity in Manhattan. The article highlights a rendering of a new Home Depot store planned for East 61st Street and mentions reviewing the top Q4 retail leases in Manhattan as per the CBRE report.

title: Investors Push Home Depot and Omnicom to Steer Ads From Misinformation (Published 2021)
summary: Shareholders in Home Depot and Omnicom have filed resolutions urging the companies to investigate whether their advertising spending contributes to the spread of hate speech and misinformation. Coordinated by Open MIC, the resolutions highlight concerns that ad dollars inadvertently finance harmful online content. This comes in the wake of the U.S. Capitol siege, which was fueled by debunked conspiracy theories about election fraud spread through online platforms.

title: You Can Buy a Tiny House at Home Depot for Less than $13,000
summary: Home Depot sells Tuff Shed Tiny Houses for under $13,000, presenting an affordable housing alternative, especially in expensive areas like New Jersey. The author, while intrigued by the tiny house movement from shows like "Tiny House Hunters," acknowledges the challenge of downsizing but sees the financial benefits.

title: Home Depot pays nearly $36M for prime site in Tysons
summary: The Home Depot has acquired a prime piece of property in Tysons, Virginia, for nearly $36 million. The retailer has not yet disclosed its plans for the newly acquired site. This purchase follows news of Home Depot building its first new store in the D.C. area in over a decade.

title: 40% off during Home Depot’s bath event of the year
summary: Home Depot's "biggest bath event of the year" offers up to 40% off select bath products and free shipping on vanities, running through January 31. The article highlights several vanity and faucet deals, such as the Merryfield bath vanity, Rubicon bathroom faucet, and Pegasus medicine cabinet, to help consumers upgrade their bathrooms during quarantine. These deals aim to refresh home spaces after prolonged periods spent indoors.

title: Agency Brief: Leo Burnett and BBDO are finalists in Home Depot creative review
summary: Leo Burnett and BBDO have been named as finalists in the creative review for Home Depot's advertising account. This development indicates a competitive process for the retail giant's marketing efforts. The final decision will determine which agency secures the significant creative mandate.

title: Glimmers of hope for Daytona's ISB corridor even as retailers flock to city's LPGA area
summary: Despite a major retail exodus from Daytona's International Speedway Boulevard (ISB) corridor to the fast-growing LPGA area, a handful of new businesses are opening on ISB, offering a glimmer of hope. Many national chains have relocated to the LPGA area's newer shopping centers due to available land and higher traffic counts, while some ISB closures are attributed to chains' financial struggles or poor store performance. However, landlords investing in property improvements and the area's strong foundation of hospitals, universities, and the Speedway suggest ISB can still thrive, particularly by focusing on entertainment and dining, and attracting local businesses.

title: The Home Depot and Allstate Launch New Best-in-Class Extended Protection Plan
summary: The Home Depot has partnered with Allstate to introduce a new extended protection plan, offering expanded benefits and faster repair services for customers. This plan covers major appliances, outdoor power equipment, home electronics, and other products, featuring a speed of service guarantee, shorter appointment windows, advanced troubleshooting, and an industry-leading "No Lemon" policy for replacements. The collaboration aims to instill confidence in purchases by providing efficient and reliable support for product issues.

title: The Home Depot Bringing 1,500 New Jobs to Dallas-Fort Worth Metro with New Distribution Center
summary: The Home Depot has opened a new 1.5 million square-foot distribution center in Dallas, dedicated to fulfilling online and in-store orders, including large appliance delivery and installation. This facility is part of a $1.2 billion investment to expand its national distribution network and is expected to create 1,500 new jobs in the Dallas-Fort Worth area, increasing the company's regional supply chain footprint to 4.5 million square feet. The investment aims to enhance the customer shopping experience by offering same-day and next-day delivery to 90% of the U.S. population.

title: Home Depot's DFW campus now expected to employ 1,500 people, company says
summary: Home Depot's distribution campus in West Dallas is now projected to create 1,500 new jobs by the end of 2021, an increase from the originally anticipated 800 jobs. This expansion highlights significant job growth in the Dallas-Fort Worth area. The article was published by the Dallas Business Journal.

title: Global Garden and Lawn Tools Market is Expected to Reach $ 2.91 Billion by 2024 - Latest Market Research Report by Technavio
summary: The global garden and lawn tools market is projected to grow by USD 2.91 billion during 2020-2024, driven by the increasing adoption of smart gardening technologies and product innovations. North America is expected to contribute 53% of this growth, with the US being a key market. COVID-19 is anticipated to have a negative impact on the market in the short term, but vendors are continually launching new products and focusing on advanced features like automation in lawnmowers.

title: The Home Depot opens multi-channel fulfillment center in Dallas
summary: The Home Depot has opened a 1.5 million square-foot multi-channel fulfillment center in Dallas, part of a larger $1.2 billion investment to expand its nationwide distribution and delivery network. This new facility aims to improve online and in-store pickup orders, enabling same- and next-day delivery to 90% of the U.S. population. It features advanced automation, sustainability initiatives, and is expected to create 1,500 new jobs in the Dallas-Fort Worth area.

title: Home Depot opens automated Dallas fulfillment center with hydrogen-powered forklifts
summary: Home Depot has opened a new 1.5 million-square-foot fulfillment center in Dallas, part of its $1.2 billion supply chain investment, featuring hydrogen-powered forklifts for zero-emission operations. The facility will handle store and online orders, large appliance delivery, and is a key hub for achieving same-day and next-day delivery for 90% of the U.S. population. This development reflects Home Depot's focus on automation, sustainability, and omnichannel capabilities, following increased online demand during the pandemic.

title: Global Furniture Market to Grow by $ 113.61 Billion During 2020-2024 | APAC to Emerge as Key Growing Region | Technavio
summary: The global furniture market is projected to grow by $113.61 billion at a CAGR of almost 4% between 2020 and 2024, driven primarily by increasing residential/commercial construction. The APAC region is expected to be a key growth area, contributing 47% of the overall market expansion due to urbanization and rising disposable incomes. Home furniture dominated the market in 2019, supported by government initiatives and demand for multifunctional items, with key players including Ashley Furniture Industries Inc., Inter IKEA Holding BV, and Steelcase Inc.

title: Agree Realty Sees Accelerated Growth by Investing in Top-Tier Net Lease Retail Assets
summary: Agree Realty has achieved accelerated growth by focusing on acquiring and developing net-leased properties with industry-leading retail tenants, resulting in a highly resilient portfolio, even during the COVID-19 pandemic. The company recorded record investment activity in 2020 and is strategically expanding its ground lease portfolio and partnering with top retailers. Analysts project continued strong FFO growth due to Agree Realty's robust balance sheet, cost of capital, and strategic execution.

title: Home Depot: State-of-the-Art E-Commerce Distribution Center Developed on an Aggressive Schedule
summary: Home Depot partnered with Prologis to develop a state-of-the-art, over 1 million square foot e-commerce distribution center in Atlanta to support its rapidly growing online business. The project was completed on an aggressive 12-month timeline, which was critical for Home Depot to quickly meet increasing customer demands for online shopping. This facility is Home Depot's first ground-up e-commerce center designed exclusively for conveyable goods.

title: The Home Depot to Donate $1 Million to Support Campus Improvements at Historically Black Colleges and Universities
summary: The Home Depot announced a $1 million grant program through its annual Retool Your School initiative to support campus improvements at Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs). This commitment doubles the previous year's funding, providing grants ranging from $20,000 to $75,000 to 30 schools. Voting for favorite HBCUs for these grants is open to students, alumni, and advocates until March 15, 2021.

title: Supplier Spotlight: Diversant
summary: This article highlights Diversant, the largest African American-owned IT staffing firm in the U.S. and a preferred partner for The Home Depot. Founded by Gene Waddy out of necessity, Diversant has grown significantly, partly due to its strong relationship with The Home Depot and its commitment to diversity and community involvement, including programs for military veterans. The company operates as a certified Minority Owned Business Enterprise (MBE) and focuses on recruiting a diverse and agile workforce.

title: Serial shoplifters arrested after Home Depot theft in Selma, police say
summary: Two serial shoplifters, Mia Delarosa and Brittany Zaragosa, were arrested in Selma after stealing from Home Depot. Delarosa, previously banned from the store for past thefts, entered the store while Zaragosa waited in a car. After a brief pursuit, both were apprehended and found with stolen items from Home Depot and other nearby stores, facing multiple charges.

title: Toro Recalls Power Max Snowthrowers Due to Amputation Hazard
summary: Toro has recalled approximately 6,700 Power Max snowthrowers in the U.S. and Canada due to an amputation hazard. The recall follows five reports where the auger failed to disengage when the control lever was released, although no injuries have been reported. Consumers are advised to stop using the affected snowthrowers and contact a Toro dealer for a free repair.

title: Toro Snow Blower Recall Issued Due to Amputation Risk
summary: Toro has issued a recall for approximately 6,700 of its Power Max 826 OHAE Snowthrowers due to a defect where the auger blades can continue spinning after the control lever is released, posing an amputation risk. While no injuries have been reported, the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) advises owners to immediately stop using the recalled snow blowers and contact Toro for a free repair. The recalled units were sold at The Home Depot and Ace Hardware stores between November 2020 and January 2021.

title: Toro recalls snowblowers due to amputation hazard
summary: Toro is recalling more than 7,400 snowblowers in the U.S. and Canada due to an amputation hazard. The recall involves 2021 Toro Power Max 826 OHAE Snowthrowers where the auger may fail to disengage, allowing it to spin at full speed continuously. No injuries have been reported, but consumers are urged to stop using the product and contact Toro for a free repair.

title: Toro Recalls Power Max Snowthrowers Due to Amputation Hazard
summary: Toro has issued a recall for over 6,700 Model Year 2021 Power Max 826 OHAE Snowthrowers (Model Number 37802) sold in the U.S. and Canada. The recall is due to a potential amputation hazard, as the snowthrowers were sold with a problem that needs repair. Consumers who purchased these units between November 2020 and January 2021 for approximately $1,200 are advised to check Toro's website for serial numbers and product safety information.

title: The Home Depot Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2020 Results; Increases Quarterly Dividend by 10 Percent
summary: The Home Depot reported strong fourth quarter and fiscal 2020 results, with sales reaching $32.3 billion and $132.1 billion respectively, driven by significant comparable sales growth. The company's board of directors approved a 10% increase in its quarterly dividend to $1.65 per share. Due to ongoing uncertainty related to the COVID-19 pandemic, Home Depot is not providing formal guidance for fiscal 2021, but expects flat to slightly positive comparable sales growth if the demand environment persists.

title: Home Depot casts doubt on further room for improvement after blow-out 2020
summary: Home Depot's shares fell 5% despite beating fourth-quarter sales estimates, as the company expressed uncertainty about maintaining its pandemic-driven sales growth into 2021. Due to the unpredictable nature of the pandemic, vaccine distribution, and fiscal policy, Home Depot's CFO stated they are limited in forecasting demand for the year, suggesting "flat to slightly positive comparable sales growth" if current trends continue. This cautious outlook, including flat operating margins, disappointed analysts and may raise expectations for rival Lowe's.

title: After 2020 Boom, Home Depot Says Sales May Be Flat This Year
summary: Home Depot Inc. experienced a significant stock drop despite strong demand, as investors are concerned about difficult comparisons and narrowing profitability due to higher costs in 2021. The company reported a 25% rise in U.S. same-store sales for the quarter ended Jan. 31, surpassing estimates, but anticipates "flat to slightly positive" revenue by that measure for 2021 as it laps the previous year's gains.

title: Prices lurch higher as Home Depot, other importers battle surging cargo, commodity costs
summary: Home Depot and other major U.S. retailers are facing escalating costs for goods and transportation, worsened by tariffs, as they cope with surging consumer demand during the COVID-19 pandemic. These companies are passing on increased expenses to consumers for items like appliances and furniture, with cargo costs from Asia to the U.S. rising significantly, creating bottlenecks that are expected to last for several months. Additionally, companies like Peloton, Spectrum Brands, Kia Motors, and La-Z-Boy are grappling with production issues, including parts shortages and increased shipping expenses, leading to higher prices and operational challenges.

title: Home Depot, Macy’s Expect Pandemic Trends to Continue, for Now
summary: Home Depot and Macy's executives expect pandemic-fueled shopping trends to persist into 2021, driving demand for home improvements and home goods. While Home Depot saw a 20% revenue increase due to increased home spending, Macy's experienced a nearly 30% sales tumble as consumers reduced apparel purchases. Both retailers acknowledge that consumer spending could shift in the latter half of the year as vaccine rollouts progress.

title: Home Depot turning to Tweel to solve downtime issues in rental business
summary: Home Depot is retrofitting its rental zero-turn mowers with non-pneumatic Michelin X Tweel Turf tires to reduce service calls and customer complaints related to tire issues, which previously accounted for over 40% of downtime. This conversion has eliminated tire-related service calls, downtime, and negative customer experiences for the retrofitted mowers, saving hundreds of labor hours and tens of thousands of dollars in parts costs. The success of this trial has prompted a full-scale conversion and further collaboration between Home Depot and Michelin to explore additional product opportunities.

title: Home Depot turning to Tweel to solve downtime issues in rental business
summary: Home Depot's rental business is adopting Michelin X Tweel Turf tires to reduce equipment downtime. The report, published by Tire Business Staff, indicates this initiative is aimed at improving efficiency in their rental operations.

title: Toro recalls snow blowers due to amputation risk
summary: Toro has recalled approximately 6,700 Power Max 826 OHAE 252cc Two-Stage Electric Start Gas Snow Blowers due to an amputation hazard, as the auger may not disengage when the control lever is released. There have been five reported incidents of this malfunction. Consumers are advised to stop using the snow blowers and return them to an authorized Toro dealer for repair.

title: Leadership Advice for CEOs and Entry Level Professionals from Hal Lawton ‘96, President & CEO of Tractor Supply Co.
summary: Hal Lawton, President and CEO of Tractor Supply Company, shared leadership advice for CEOs and entry-level professionals during the Wells Fargo Executive Leadership Series. He emphasized servant leadership, prioritizing emotional and decency quotients, applying mentor lessons, considering boss leadership styles in job searches, and developing work-life harmony. Lawton, an NC State alumnus, highlighted key insights from his extensive career, including roles at Macy's, eBay, and Home Depot.

title: Carol Tomé on becoming CEO of UPS: ‘This was my calling’
summary: Carol Tomé reflects on her unexpected journey to becoming CEO of UPS, making her the first woman and first outsider to lead the company. She discusses breaking barriers, her initiatives to change UPS's business model and culture, and her focus on employee development and diversity, drawing parallels to her experience at Home Depot. Tomé also shares her personal motivation and future goals for UPS, including sustainability and philanthropic efforts.

title: The Home Depot Pasadena Store Is Opening March 11, 2021
summary: The new Home Depot Pasadena store, located at 2881 East Walnut Street, is set to open on March 11, 2021. This 113,500 square foot store is part of The Home Depot, Inc.'s $11 billion investment in its stores, featuring customer enhancements like flexible checkout, a specialty showroom, and improved storage for Buy Online Pickup In Store orders. The store will employ 275-300 associates and operate from 6:00 am to 9:00 pm Monday-Saturday and 7:00 am to 8:00 pm on Sundays.

title: Gap Inc. Bets on Yeezy, Loyalty Programs and New Categories in 2021
summary: Gap Inc. is focusing on a "startup mindset" for 2021, emphasizing aggressive marketing, loyalty programs, and expansion into new apparel categories across its brands like Gap, Banana Republic, Old Navy, and Athleta. Key initiatives include a unified loyalty program, significant digital growth, the highly anticipated Yeezy collaboration, and inclusive sizing expansions. The company also plans strategic store closures for Gap and Banana Republic while opening new Athleta and Old Navy locations.

title: The Home Depot Expands Environmentally Friendly Outdoor Power Lineup
summary: The Home Depot is expanding its lineup of cordless outdoor power equipment, featuring brands like Ryobi, DeWalt, Makita, and Milwaukee. These new battery-operated tools offer the convenience and environmental benefits of cordless technology with performance comparable to gas equipment, including longer runtimes and interchangeable batteries across various tools. The initiative aims to provide customers with easier-to-use, eco-friendly, and powerful options for their outdoor projects.

title: 4 Key Steps to Profitable Store-Based Fulfillment
summary: A report by Incisiv, commissioned by Manhattan Associates Inc., reveals that while ecommerce surged due to the pandemic, order fulfillment from stores has significantly reduced profit margins for retailers. The article outlines four key steps for retailers to make store-based fulfillment more profitable: addressing inefficiencies, equipping associates with digital tools, streamlining returns, and improving in-store inventory accuracy. These steps are crucial for retailers to adapt to the evolving landscape and meet customer expectations in a post-pandemic world.

title: Furniture retailers face ‘unprecedented’ delays but business is booming, Corridor stores say
summary: Furniture retailers in the Corridor are experiencing "unprecedented" delays in their supply chains due to high demand, manufacturing disruptions from COVID-19, and material shortages caused by weather events. Despite these challenges, business is booming, with increased sales driven by work-from-home trends and a renewed focus on home improvement. Local businesses are adapting by stocking more items, adding suppliers, and offering "quick ship" options while appreciating increased local support from customers.

title: Home Depot hiring more than 2,600 positions in Chicago area
summary: Home Depot is looking to hire over 2,600 new employees for positions across the Chicago area. These roles include both part-time and full-time in-store positions focusing on customer service, online order fulfillment, and merchandising. Additionally, the company is seeking over 1,500 associates for its distribution centers nationwide to help with store replenishment and order shipping.

title: Home Depot hiring more than 2.6K jobs in Chicago area
summary: The Home Depot is seeking to fill over 2,600 positions in the Chicago area. These roles include full-time and part-time opportunities in customer service, online order fulfillment, overnight freight handling, and merchandising. Interested individuals can find more information and apply online through careers.homedepot.com/hiring.

title: Old Golf Courses Are Being Turned Into E-Commerce Warehouses
summary: Driven by a surge in online shopping and the need for more e-commerce fulfillment centers, developers are acquiring old golf courses and converting them into warehouses. This trend is fueled by the overbuilding of golf courses in the early 2000s and a subsequent decline in their popularity, making these large undeveloped tracts of land ideal for logistics conversion.

title: As Home Improvement Surges, Capitalize with the RTH ETF
summary: The article discusses how the surge in home improvement spending in 2020, driven by social distancing, presents an opportunity for investors through the VanEck Vectors Retail ETF (RTH). RTH, with a significant holding in Home Depot, offers exposure to leading retail companies benefiting from this trend. Future predictions suggest continued, albeit moderating, growth in home repair spending, further supporting RTH's investment potential.

title: Supplier Spotlight: Brinly-Hardy's Fifth Generation CEO Talks Partnerships & Horse-Drawn Plows
summary: The article features Jane Hardy, the fifth-generation CEO of Brinly-Hardy Co., a family-owned business established in 1839 that has evolved from making horse-drawn plows to modern lawn and garden equipment. Hardy discusses the company's nearly 200-year history, its innovative spirit, and its long-standing partnership with The Home Depot, which started almost from the retailer's inception. She highlights Brinly-Hardy's commitment to making better products and innovating through collaborations with The Home Depot's merchants.

title: As Home Improvement Surges, Capitalize with the RTH ETF
summary: The article highlights how the surge in home improvement spending in 2020, driven by social distancing, presents an opportunity for investors through the VanEck Vectors Retail ETF (RTH). RTH, with a significant allocation to Home Depot, serves as an indirect play on this booming sub-sector, which saw product sales spike by 8.7%. Future spending on home repair is also predicted to continue, further benefiting retailers like Lowe's, Ace Hardware, and Home Depot.

title: The Home Depot Partners with Habitat for Humanity to Help Communities "Bring On Spring"
summary: The Home Depot announced a partnership with Habitat for Humanity International to support spring DIY projects and neighborhood revitalization across the U.S., providing over $200,000 in products. This initiative builds on their decade-long collaboration, with a significant focus on helping veterans, including the first project at a Female Veterans Village in Florida. The program aims to encourage community involvement in home improvement after a challenging year.

title: Home Depot Rental Opens New Operations Facilities in Houston, Nashville
summary: The Home Depot Rental has opened new rental operations facilities (ROFs) in Houston and Nashville, adding to existing locations in New Orleans and Los Angeles. These facilities aim to streamline the supply chain and delivery of larger equipment to jobsites, expanding Home Depot Rental's capacity to serve Pro customers with a broader assortment of heavy equipment. The company plans further expansion with new ROF locations expected in Atlanta and Dallas later this year, alongside additional rental centers nationwide.

title: Home Depot, Lowe’s build on supply chain foundations to make quick work of omnichannel
summary: Home Depot and Lowe's rapidly adapted their supply chain strategies during the pandemic by leveraging prior investments in technology and fulfillment networks. Both retailers quickly implemented curbside pickup, optimized their store-based fulfillment, and refined their market delivery systems for bulky items. This agility allowed them to meet surging online demand and maintain strong sales growth, demonstrating the critical role of supply chain visibility and adaptability in an omnichannel retail environment.

title: Celebrating the Wins
summary: Tanya Hairston-Whitner '95 and Katie Lampley '96, two Bentley alums, initially met in 1992 and forged a lifelong friendship rooted in their shared West Indian heritage and commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI). Both have significantly contributed to Bentley University's DEI efforts, with Hairston-Whitner serving on the Board of Trustees and chairing its new DEI committee, and Lampley becoming the first Chief Diversity and Inclusion Officer. They emphasize the importance of continuous effort, leading by example, and bravery in fostering inclusive environments.

title: U.S. Supreme Court weighs TransUnion bid to nix 'terrorist list' lawsuit
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court is considering narrowing a class-action lawsuit against TransUnion, where thousands sought damages after being incorrectly flagged as matching names on a government list of suspected terrorists and drug traffickers. The credit reporting company is appealing a lower court's ruling which upheld a $40 million jury verdict. Justices questioned whether all class members suffered a "concrete injury," a requirement for such lawsuits, particularly for those whose information was not publicly disclosed.

title: Chipotle Names Matt Carey and Mauricio Gutierrez to its Board of Directors
summary: Chipotle Mexican Grill announced the appointment of Matt Carey and Mauricio Gutierrez to its board of directors, expanding the board to 11 members, with 10 being independent. Carey, an expert in IT and cybersecurity, will join the Audit and Risk Committee, while Gutierrez, with executive and transformational leadership experience, will serve on the Compensation Committee. These appointments aim to bring diverse perspectives and expertise to support Chipotle's strategic objectives.

title: Chipotle names Matt Carey and Mauricio Gutierrez to its board
summary: Chipotle Mexican Grill has appointed Matt Carey, CTO of Home Depot, and Mauricio Gutierrez, CEO of NRG Energy, to its board of directors. These additions bring diverse experience in technology, cybersecurity, and executive leadership to Chipotle's 11-member board, aiding the company in achieving its strategic objectives. Carey will serve on the audit and risk committee, while Gutierrez will join the compensation committee.

title: Syracuse man arrested for creating fake barcodes at Home Depot; stealing thousands
summary: A 37-year-old Syracuse man, Jeffrey G. Gordon, was arrested for allegedly stealing thousands of dollars from Home Depot stores by using fake barcodes to pay lower prices at self-checkout. Police state Gordon orchestrated this scheme 28 times between November 2020 and February 2021 across multiple Home Depot locations in New York, accumulating approximately $10,000 in theft. He faces multiple charges including Grand Larceny and Petit Larceny and has been released on an appearance ticket.

title: Pay for Home Depot's top five executives jumps 43% for 2020
summary: The combined compensation for Home Depot's top five executives rose by 43% in 2020, totaling $35 million. This increase follows a nearly 20% revenue growth for the company in the same year, along with promotions for several key executives.

title: Today In Retail: PriceSmart’s Revenues Increase 3.4 Pct; Handy Collaborates With Gotham Properties
summary: PriceSmart reported a 3.4 percent increase in total revenues for the second quarter of fiscal 2021, and Handy partnered with Gotham Properties to offer home services to tenants. Additionally, Levi Strauss plans to open new stores and expects a 25 percent rise in first-half sales, while UPS is acquiring electric vertical takeoff aircraft to enhance delivery efficiency and reduce emissions.

title: QVC complex in West Hempfield sold for $15M; future tenant could create up to 1,000 jobs
summary: A New York-based real estate investment firm, Saadia Group, has purchased the QVC distribution center in West Hempfield for $15.5 million. Saadia Group is negotiating a lease with an unidentified tenant expected to create 300 to 1,000 jobs, largely replacing the 1,100 jobs lost due to QVC's wind-down. The tenant is slated to begin operations by the end of the year in the 765,000-square-foot complex.

title: Sarasota's Earth's Ally brings organic products to home gardeners
summary: Earth's Ally, a Sarasota-based company founded in 2018, offers organic gardening products for home gardeners, initially sourcing solutions used by large organic farms.
