The company, led by CEO Scott Allshouse, has developed its own nontoxic weed killer and other plant care products, emphasizing safety for pollinators, pets, and children. Earth's Ally recently secured a nationwide distribution deal with Lowe's and aims to combat the misconception that natural products are ineffective.

title: The Home Depot Opens Three New Florida Distribution Centers
summary: The Home Depot announced the opening of three new distribution centers in Florida, located in West Palm Beach, Miami, and Fort Myers. These facilities aim to provide faster delivery options to customers in South Florida, with plans for two more Miami distribution centers to open in 2022. The expansion is expected to create over 150 new jobs and is part of the company's broader $1.2 billion investment in its supply chain network.

title: Wilberforce University to receive Home Depot school improvement grant
summary: Wilberforce University has been awarded a $20,000 "Retool Your School" grant from The Home Depot for campus improvements and student learning enhancements. This year, the program is distributing over $1 million to 30 Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU). Students at Wilberforce will advise the school administration on the specific projects that will benefit from the grant.

title: The Home Depot Announces Winners of Retool Your School Historically Black Colleges and Universities Grant Program
summary: The Home Depot announced the winners of its 12th annual Retool Your School program, awarding $1 million across 30 Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) for campus improvement projects. Tougaloo College received the Campaign of the Year award along with its cluster prize, totaling $120,000. Since 2009, the program has provided over $4 million in funding to 87% of the nation's HBCUs.

title: The Home Depot names BBDO its new agency of record
summary: The Home Depot has appointed BBDO as its new agency of record. This decision comes after a strong performance year for Home Depot, with sales increasing by 20% in 2020. The article highlights other creative and marketing industry news, including AI's role in recent campaigns.

title: Amazon plans furniture assembly service to catch Wayfair
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is testing a new premium service offering immediate furniture and appliance assembly upon delivery, aiming to better compete with rivals like Wayfair, Best Buy, Home Depot, and Lowe’s. This service, anticipated to launch in Virginia and two other markets, would involve drivers assembling items, removing packaging, and handling immediate returns for dissatisfied customers. The initiative seeks to make delivery of large items more convenient and efficient, building on the increased online sales of furniture and housewares observed during the pandemic, although Amazon has struggled to match Wayfair's dominance in the online home-goods market.

title: Expansion of Home Depot on 19400 SW 106 Avenue in South Miami Heights, Florida
summary: Home Depot USA Inc. is planning a significant expansion at its South Miami Heights, Florida location, adding a 17,250 square foot building and a 3,000 square foot lumber canopy. The project will also increase parking density, with a meeting scheduled for April 29, 2021, to discuss development specifics. The store, adjacent to the Ronald Reagan Turnpike, will remain open during the expansion.

title: Your Outdoor Oasis Is One Afternoon Project Away: OLYMPIC Stains by PPG Selects Light Oak as Its First-Ever 2021 Stain Color of the Year
summary: OLYMPIC Stains by PPG has named Light Oak as its first-ever 2021 Stain Color of the Year, responding to the increased interest in DIY home improvement and outdoor living driven by the pandemic. Light Oak is a soft, semi-transparent tan stain designed to add a refined Scandinavian-inspired look to outdoor spaces, allowing the wood's natural characteristics to show through. This versatile color is ideal for decks, patios, pergolas, fencing, and siding, helping homeowners create relaxing outdoor oases.

title: Top Trends Driving Propane Cylinder Sales
summary: The propane cylinder market is experiencing strong demand driven by increased outdoor living investments, generator use during power outages, and industrial applications favoring propane for efficiency and environmental benefits. Despite steel shortages and price increases, both new and refurbished cylinder sales are robust, with a growing interest in lighter composite cylinders. Companies are adapting to these trends by emphasizing planning, innovative products, and efficient delivery processes.

title: Georgia religious leaders call for boycott of Home Depot over silence on voting laws
summary: A group of prominent Georgia clergy members is calling for a nationwide boycott of Home Depot. They criticize the company for its silence on the state's new voting restrictions and its refusal to meet with activists, contrasting its stance with other Georgia-based companies like Delta and Coca-Cola. The religious leaders are urging Home Depot to speak out against the new voting laws and meet with them to discuss changes.

title: Home Depot to face boycott over Georgia voting curbs
summary: Religious leaders in Georgia are calling for a boycott of Home Depot due to the company's silence on the state's new voting restrictions. Activists argue that the new laws make it harder for Black people and other racial minorities to vote, and Home Depot has not joined other corporations in opposing the measures. Home Depot stated its belief that "all elections should be accessible, fair and secure and support broad voter participation."

title: Church leaders call for Home Depot boycott over Georgia voting curbs
summary: Black religious leaders in Georgia are calling for a boycott of Home Depot, accusing the company of not taking a strong stance against the state's new restrictive voting law. While other Georgia-based corporations like Delta and Coca-Cola have engaged with activists and opposed the law, Home Depot has stated it supports accessible, fair, and secure elections but has not denounced the legislation. The leaders warn that the boycott will escalate if Home Depot does not forcefully speak out against the law.

title: Georgia Faith Leaders Urge Boycott of Home Depot Over Voting Law (Published 2021)
summary: A coalition of Black faith leaders in Georgia, representing over 1,000 churches, has called for a boycott of Home Depot. They argue that the company failed to oppose the state's new voting law, which they believe limits voting access. This boycott is seen as a "warning shot" to other states considering similar voting restrictions and aims to apply economic pressure on corporations to take a stand on voting rights.

title: These 3 dividend ETFs are a retiree's best friend
summary: This article recommends three dividend ETFs — SPDR S&P Dividend ETF, Vanguard High Dividend Yield ETF, and Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF — as excellent options for retirees seeking a steady stream of passive income. It highlights the importance of diversification in retirement investing and details the characteristics, holdings, and expense ratios of each ETF, emphasizing their potential to provide income that keeps pace with inflation while managing risk. The author advises investors to look beyond just the yield and focus on the sustainability of dividends.

title: Turning Home Depot Sheds Into Tiny Houses: Everything You Need to Know
summary: Home Depot has partnered with Tuff Shed to offer customizable sheds that can be transformed into tiny homes. While these sheds provide a base structure with various customization options like specific colors, roof styles, and materials, they lack essential features like foundations, electricity, and plumbing. Converting a Tuff Shed into a livable tiny home requires significant additional work, research, and financial investment beyond the initial purchase price, but offers a path to a more sustainable lifestyle.

title: The Home Depot Announces New and Enhanced Disaster Preparedness Resources
summary: The Home Depot has introduced new and enhanced resources for disaster preparedness, coinciding with National Hurricane Preparedness Week and National Wildfire Preparedness Month in May. These resources include a new Weather Center Hub with supply checklists and government agency information, free online workshops for hurricane and wildfire preparedness, and step-by-step guides and videos. The Home Depot Foundation also continues its commitment to disaster response and long-term recovery efforts, having dedicated $4.1 million to disaster relief in 2021.

title: Police arrest man accused of using counterfeit bills at local Home Depot stores
summary: Police in Boardman, Ohio, arrested Marcus Shelton of New York City for attempting to use counterfeit bills at a Home Depot. Shelton and another suspect had allegedly been using fake money at several Home Depot stores in the area for months, including purchasing about $400 worth of power tools with counterfeit hundred-dollar bills earlier that day in Salem. Shelton faces charges of theft by deception and counterfeiting, and the investigation involves Boardman police, Home Depot loss prevention, and the U.S. Secret Service.

title: Tractor Supply board picks Macy’s exec to be next CEO
summary: Tractor Supply has appointed Hal Lawton, formerly president of Macy's, as its new president and CEO, effective January 13. He will succeed Greg Sandfort, who will transition out of the role and advise Lawton until August. Lawton's background includes leadership positions at eBay and Home Depot, bringing extensive omnichannel retail experience to Tractor Supply.

title: Supplier Spotlight: Klein Tools, Powering America's Tradespeople Since 1857
summary: The article highlights Klein Tools, a family-owned business founded in 1857 by Mathias Klein, emphasizing its enduring commitment to quality and craftsmanship, which has made its tools a standard for tradespeople. It details Klein Tools' exclusive partnership with The Home Depot formed in 2009, which significantly boosted both companies' market presence and sales. The partnership has led to multiple Supplier Partner of the Year awards for Klein Tools and includes sponsorship of the SkillsUSA National Signing Day.

title: Home Depot Regional Distribution Center being built at Conroe’s remediated superfund site
summary: A 600,000-square-foot Home Depot Regional Distribution Center is under construction at a remediated superfund site in Conroe, Texas, formerly the Conroe Cresoting Co. This project, despite the site's history of environmental contamination, is reactivating a rail spur and enabling a long-awaited road extension project. While the company name was initially withheld due to a nondisclosure agreement, city officials confirmed it would be a Home Depot facility, scheduled for completion in July and opening in the fall.

title: The Home Depot Foundation Grants $30,000 in Scholarships to SkillsUSA Students
summary: The Home Depot Foundation has granted $30,000 in scholarships to six SkillsUSA students entering the skilled trades, as part of its Path to Pro program. This initiative supported SkillsUSA's National Signing Day 2021 by recognizing high school and college students pursuing careers in building and construction. The Home Depot Foundation continues to advance its trades training program, which has exposed over 15,000 individuals to the skilled trades and certified more than 5,000 participants.

title: With car rentals impossible to find, travelers are resorting to U-Hauls for their vacation
summary: Due to soaring car rental prices and limited availability, travelers are turning to unconventional solutions like U-Haul vans and Home Depot trucks for their transportation needs. This trend, dubbed "carmageddon," highlights the struggle many face in securing affordable vehicles for their trips. The article shares several anecdotes and offers tips for finding alternative transportation, including using car-sharing services like Turo or extending rental bookings.

title: Home Depot vs. Lowe’s — should you buy either stock now?
summary: This article compares the performance of Home Depot Inc. and Lowe's Cos. Inc., especially concerning their sales growth during the coronavirus pandemic. It notes that while Lowe's has grown more quickly, Home Depot boasts better margins and a history of dividend increases. The article aims to provide investors with insights into which home-improvement retailer might be a better investment.

title: Corporate Counsel Awards: Salmon Laguerre a true rising star
summary: The article announces that Salmon Laguerre, corporate counsel for The Home Depot Inc., has been named the Rising Star in the 2021 Corporate Counsel Awards. These awards are presented by Atlanta Business Chronicle in partnership with the Association of Corporate Counsel Georgia Chapter.

title: Home Depot hiring for nearly 700 positions at Maine stores
summary: Home Depot is looking to fill almost 700 positions across its stores in the metro Portland-Auburn area of Maine. The company is hiring for full-time and part-time roles in customer service, online order fulfillment, freight unpacking, and merchandising. Interested individuals can apply online or by texting "JOBS" to 52270.

title: American Woodmark Shines in Product Innovation
summary: American Woodmark, one of the world's largest cabinet makers, boasts a long history of innovation, stemming from its origins in 1951 as "Formed Laminates" and its partnership with The Home Depot since 1980. The company was recognized for its Sedgewood Bath Vanities and lauded by Women on Boards for its diverse board of directors, illustrating its commitment to both product innovation and diversity.

title: Home Depot
summary: The Home Depot implemented IBM Blockchain technology to improve communication and resolution of transaction disputes with its vendors. This technology provides real-time visibility into the supply chain, enabling faster identification and resolution of discrepancies, fostering stronger relationships, and increasing overall efficiency. The initiative has significantly reduced the time and manual intervention previously required to address vendor disputes.

title: Home Depot charged four times more for some lumber products this year
summary: Home Depot significantly increased prices for some lumber products, with inflation from skyrocketing lumber prices impacting its fiscal first-quarter results. Over a third of the increase in the average customer ticket was due to commodity inflation, as the company passed higher costs onto consumers amid "unprecedented demand" for home improvement projects.

title: Home Depot removes face mask requirement for vaccinated shoppers
summary: Home Depot has updated its mask policy, removing the requirement for vaccinated shoppers. This decision by Atlanta's largest public company follows new guidance from the CDC. The company had initially implemented its mask policy in July 2020 to mitigate the spread of Covid-19.

title: Quarterly Earnings 2021
summary: The Home Depot's investor relations page provides access to quarterly earnings reports for 2021 and other years. Users can find press releases, 10Q/10K filings, webcast transcripts, and supplemental materials for each quarter. The page also offers email alerts for financial information and contact details for investor relations.

title: Big retailers like Walmart, Macy’s see shoppers back in stores
summary: Major retailers like Walmart, Macy's, and Home Depot are reporting increased in-store shopping and exceeding sales estimates as COVID-19 restrictions ease across the U.S. Government stimulus checks and higher vaccination rates are contributing to a return to pre-pandemic consumer behaviors, with foot traffic significantly up at these stores. This trend suggests a strong recovery for brick-and-mortar retail as consumers resume activities outside their homes.

title: Home Depot outpaces Lowe’s in Q1
summary: In Q1, Home Depot significantly outperformed Lowe's, with net sales increasing 32.7% to $37.5 billion compared to Lowe's 24.1% rise to $24.4 billion. Home Depot saw robust demand from both DIY and Pro customers, with all its top 40 markets achieving double-digit comps growth. While Lowe's also reported double-digit gains, its growth showed signs of slowing, and it lost market share to its larger competitor.

title: Masks optional: Kroger stores lift mask requirement for vaccinated customers
summary: Kroger announced it is lifting its mask mandate for vaccinated customers and most vaccinated associates starting May 20, aligning with CDC guidance. Non-vaccinated individuals and pharmacy/clinic employees will still be required to wear masks. Other major retailers like Walmart, Target, Home Depot, and Aldi are also making masks optional for vaccinated customers, while some, like Jungle Jim's and Whole Foods, continue to require them.

title: The Home Depot to Present at RBC Global Consumer & Retail Virtual Conference
summary: The Home Depot announced that its president & chief operating officer, Ted Decker, and executive vice president of merchandising, Jeff Kinnaird, will present at the RBC Global Consumer & Retail Virtual Conference on June 2, 2021, at 10:00 a.m. ET. The presentation will be webcast live and archived on the company's investor relations website. The company also provided an overview of its operations, fiscal 2020 sales and earnings, and stock exchange information.

title: The Home Depot Declares First Quarter Dividend of $1.65 and Announces $20 Billion Share Repurchase Authorization
summary: The Home Depot announced that its board of directors declared a first-quarter cash dividend of $1.65 per share, payable on June 17, 2021, to shareholders of record on June 3, 2021. This marks the 137th consecutive quarter the company has paid a cash dividend. Additionally, the board authorized a new $20 billion share repurchase program, replacing the previous authorization.

title: The Home Depot Foundation Expands Trades Training Initiatives with Path to Pro Scholarship Program
summary: The Home Depot Foundation has launched the Path to Pro scholarship program, committing $250,000 in financial assistance to high school seniors and graduates pursuing building construction trades. This initiative aims to address the growing labor shortage in the construction industry and support the training of future skilled tradespeople. The scholarships will be administered by the SkillPointe Foundation, further expanding The Home Depot Foundation's existing $50 million investment in trades training.

title: Home Depot’s ‘One Supply Chain’ is taking shape with massive 2021 growth
summary: Home Depot reported strong Q1 2021 results, with continued high demand for home improvement from both DIY and Pro customers. The company's "One Supply Chain" initiative, a $1.2 billion investment, is progressing well, expanding its logistical facilities like Flatbed Delivery Centers, Market Delivery Operations, and Market Delivery Centers to enhance delivery speed and cater to broader product categories. Home Depot's strategy of investing in both physical and digital supply chains and its omnichannel fulfillment, particularly high store fulfillment for online orders, is proving successful in meeting customer demand for bulky items.

title: Declining future lumber prices are an early indicator of inflation
summary: This article discusses how declining future lumber prices may signal an early moderation of inflation, which saw prices increase over 410% from January 2020 to May 2021. The increase in lumber prices added a significant cost to new homes and is partially blamed for reduced housing starts. The author also touches on rising labor costs and the hope that inflation will abate within the next 24 months.

title: Home Depot Wiretapped Shoppers, Class Action Lawsuit Claims
summary: A class action lawsuit alleges that Home Depot uses Quantum Metric session replay tools to secretly monitor and record customer activity on its website, homedepot.com, violating Florida's Security of Communications Act. The lawsuit claims these tools record clicks, mouse movements, and information input, leaving users vulnerable to data leaks. Plaintiff Michael Fridman is seeking damages and a jury trial for anyone in Florida whose screen session was recorded without consent.

title: Police: Theft ring involving officer targeted Home Depot stores
summary: A Las Vegas police officer, Samuelito Quijano, and five others were arrested in connection with a retail theft ring primarily targeting Home Depot stores. The ring allegedly accumulated thousands of dollars in thefts from at least 28 stores since March. Police recovered stolen or fraudulently purchased property after serving search warrants, and several co-defendants confessed to their involvement.

title: Luxury Goods Sales Projected to Recover to 2019 Levels This Year
summary: A new report from Bain & Company projects global luxury goods sales to fully recover to 2019 levels this year, with a 30% probability of exceeding $340 billion. This optimistic forecast is driven by strong economic rebounds in China and the United States, propelled by swift vaccine distribution and increased disposable income. The article highlights the U.S. Global Investors' Global Luxury Goods Fund (USLUX) as an attractive way to capitalize on this recovery, benefiting from the spending habits of affluent consumers, particularly in Asia.

title: Announcing the 2021 Adobe Experience Maker Awards Finalists
summary: Adobe has announced the finalists for its 2021 Experience Maker Awards, recognizing customers who have innovated using Adobe Experience Cloud solutions amid challenging times. The awards also include the Lion Awards for Workfront customers, celebrating advancements in work management. Finalists in 12 global categories and several regional "Experience Maker" categories were selected from a record number of submissions, and winners will be announced at virtual galas in June.

title: Alberta sets sights on expanding forest products harvest as high prices drive returns
summary: Alberta is looking to significantly increase its forest product harvest as record-high lumber prices boost provincial revenues. This expansion includes allocating new harvesting rights to First Nations, such as the Bigstone Cree Nation, and other forestry companies. While the increase in timber dues and levies is benefiting the province's treasury, the initiative faces criticism regarding environmental impact and Indigenous consultation.

title: Target is reopening fitting rooms after keeping them closed more than a year amid COVID-19
summary: Target has started reopening its fitting rooms across all stores, with most expected to be operational by Tuesday after being closed for over a year due to the coronavirus pandemic. This decision follows updated CDC guidelines on masks for vaccinated individuals and comes as other retailers, like Kohl's, also reopen their dressing rooms to improve the shopping experience. Target assures customers that frequent disinfection and cleaning protocols will remain in place, with a small number of fitting rooms potentially still used for vaccinations.

title: Carpentersville shopping center sells for $3.95 million
summary: Hanley Investment Group Real Estate Advisors facilitated the sale of a 100%-occupied, 11,035-square-foot multi-tenant retail property in Carpentersville, Illinois, for $3.95 million. The property, shadow-anchored by a Home Depot, attracted 13 offers and was purchased by a San Diego-based investor. Tenants include Panda Express, ATI Physical Therapy, Game Stop, and T-Mobile, with most leases extending beyond 2025.

title: The Home Depot Foundation and Home Builders Institute Partner with 100 Black Men of America, Inc. to Provide Skilled Trades Training Opportunities for Youth in Underserved Communities
summary: The Home Depot Foundation and Home Builders Institute are partnering with 100 Black Men of America, Inc. to launch a skilled trades training program for Black youth in underserved communities. This initiative aims to address the underrepresentation of Black individuals in skilled labor industries by offering skill-building workshops, internships, and industry-recognized certifications. The Foundation is also supporting the Russell Innovation Center for Entrepreneurs with construction aid for an outdoor creativity space.

title: The Home Depot Foundation Partners With 100 Black Men of America Inc. to Provide Skilled Trades Training for Underserved Youth
summary: The Home Depot Foundation, in partnership with Home Builders Institute (HBI) and 100 Black Men of America Inc., is launching a new program to provide skilled trades training to underserved Black youth. The initiative aims to increase opportunities in the trades through workshops, internships, and certifications, with pilot programs starting in Atlanta, Philadelphia, and San Francisco. Additionally, The Home Depot Foundation introduced a $250,000 Path to Pro scholarship program, reinforcing its commitment to investing $50 million in training the next generation of skilled tradespeople.

title: CMS Energy sells EnerBank USA to fund renewables, grid reliability
summary: CMS Energy is selling EnerBank USA, a non-core business, to Regions Bank for $960 million to fund investments in renewable energy and grid reliability in Michigan. The sale provides capital for Consumers Energy's Clean Energy Plan and infrastructure projects, avoiding rate increases for customers. The deal is expected to close in Q4 and will not impact CMS's long-term adjusted earnings-per-share growth guidance.

title: The Home Depot Foundation Partners with Girl Scouts of the USA to Launch Skilled Trades Training Program for Young Women
summary: The Home Depot Foundation announced a new strategic partnership with Girl Scouts of the USA to launch a skilled trades training program for young women. This pilot program, starting in Fall 2021 in Atlanta, Denver, and Houston, will offer hands-on experience in carpentry and other building construction trades, led by female industry professionals. The initiative aims to address the underrepresentation of women in the construction industry and includes scholarship opportunities for high school senior Girl Scouts through the Foundation's Path to Pro program.

title: Home Depot and Lowe's have 30% share of a home improvement market that's heading toward $1 trillion
summary: Home Depot and Lowe's together hold approximately 30% of the U.S. home improvement market, which is projected to grow significantly towards $1 trillion. Despite their market dominance, the industry remains fragmented. Analysts suggest that increased home improvement spending, spurred by factors like COVID-19, is likely to continue.

title: Sam's Club getting into home improvement business, competing with Home Depot, Lowe's
summary: Sam's Club is entering the home improvement market with a new service called "Sam’s Club Home Install Experts by Service Finance," aiming to compete with giants like Home Depot and Lowe's. The service will connect members with local contractors for various renovation projects and offer additional discounts and financing options. This move capitalizes on the booming home improvement market, which saw significant growth in 2020.

title: HR Excellence Awards: Home Depot CEO Craig Menear: 'As a team we're trying to win together'
summary: Home Depot CEO Craig Menear emphasized that the company's long-term focus on its people was instrumental in its success during a challenging year for brick-and-mortar retailers. The home improvement giant managed to move an additional $22 billion worth of product through its network in 2020, attributing this achievement to its people-first approach. This strategy highlights the importance of human resources in navigating difficult economic landscapes and achieving business goals.

title: Home Depot charters in own box ship
summary: Home Depot has chartered its own containership to mitigate severe shipping delays affecting its supply chain. This measure is part of broader efforts by the company to cope with global disruptions, which have also included using air freight for high-value items. The retail giant, a major importer, faces challenges similar to other businesses due to port congestion, labor shortages, and increased demand.

title: Only 4.8% of designers are Black. Herman Miller, Adobe, and Gap unveil a plan to change that
summary: A new collective called the Diversity in Design (DID) Collaborative, launched by nearly two dozen companies including Herman Miller, Adobe, and Gap, aims to increase Black representation in the design profession. The collaborative plans to promote design in high schools, work with historically Black colleges to develop design curricula, and host a design fair to offer mentorship and internships. This initiative seeks to address systemic inequalities by investing in the talent pipeline for Black designers, moving beyond superficial efforts to create tangible change through specific programs and transparent metrics.

title: Home Depot secures its first-ever ship, as global supply chain crisis deepens
summary: Home Depot has secured its first dedicated ship to address the deepening global supply chain crisis, making it one of the largest importers in the U.S. This new shipping capability will be "100% dedicated to Home Depot" starting in July, aiming to ensure smoother operations amidst logistical challenges. The move highlights the company's proactive steps to manage its supply chain and maintain product availability.

title: Genuine Parts Company Announces Technology And Digital Leader
summary: Genuine Parts Company (GPC) announced that Naveen Krishna has joined the company as Executive Vice President and Chief Information & Digital Officer. In this role, Mr. Krishna will lead the strategy for all technology and digital initiatives, aligning them with GPC's strategic roadmap. He brings over 25 years of technology experience from various retail and consumer products industries, including Macy's and The Home Depot.

title: Twenty years of Reflexis, illustrated by three major retailer rollouts
summary: This article celebrates twenty years of Reflexis, a cloud-based workforce and task management solutions vendor now part of Zebra Technologies, by detailing its long-standing partnerships with three major retailers: Staples, AutoZone, and Vera Bradley. It highlights how Reflexis's technology has helped these companies streamline operations, improve workforce management, and adapt to evolving retail demands, from task management to real-time scheduling and inventory solutions. The piece underscores the significant ROI and operational efficiencies achieved through these implementations.

title: The Home Depot Foundation Increases Investment to More than $100 Million in Support of Veterans Experiencing Homelessness
summary: The Home Depot Foundation announced an additional $6.4 million investment to combat veteran homelessness, bringing its total contribution to over $100 million since 2011. These grants will impact nearly 4,000 veterans and provide over 600 housing units across the U.S. The Foundation aims to reverse the rise in veteran homelessness, collaborating with partners like Community Solutions and U.S.VETS to offer transitional and permanent supportive housing, and has pledged to invest $500 million in veteran causes by 2025.

title: Weyerhaeuser's Devin Stockfish on the Housing Boom, Inflation and Climate Change
summary: Devin Stockfish, CEO of Weyerhaeuser, discusses the surge in lumber prices driven by the housing boom and underbuilding in the U.S., along with the impact of inflation and labor shortages on the industry. He also details Weyerhaeuser's strategic positioning in the emerging carbon sequestration market, highlighting forests' role in climate change mitigation and the potential for a "natural climate solutions business." The interview covers the company's international reach, particularly with Douglas Fir exports to Japan, and its involvement in renewable energy projects like wind and solar farms on its extensive land holdings.

title: The Home Depot Launches Online Rental Reservations; Opens New Rental Locations
summary: The Home Depot has launched new "Rent Online, Pick-up In Store" technology at its 1,300 rental locations to enhance the customer experience. This allows Pro and DIY customers to reserve equipment online up to 30 days in advance, saving time and trips to the store. Additionally, The Home Depot has expanded its equipment rental network by opening eight new Rental Centers since January across North America.

title: The Home Depot Launches Online Rental Reservations, Opens New Rental Locations
summary: The Home Depot has introduced a new "Rent Online, Pick-up In Store" reservation system for its 1,300 rental locations across North America, allowing customers to reserve equipment up to 30 days in advance. This initiative aims to save time for both Pro and DIY customers by enabling them to check availability and reserve tools online. Additionally, the company has opened eight new Rental Centers since January to expand its service offerings.

title: VIDEO: Fire burns Home Depot roof in Hamilton, NJ
summary: A fire broke out on the roof of a Home Depot in Hamilton, NJ, on Wednesday morning, initially sending thick black smoke into the air. Firefighters quickly managed to control the blaze, which occurred at the store on Route 130 and involved solar panels on the roof. The cause of the fire was not immediately detailed, as Hamilton police did not respond to requests for information.

title: Latest U.S. and Canadian Housing Starts in 10 Graphs
summary: This article analyzes the latest housing starts data for the U.S. and Canada through May 2021, highlighting new home building booms in both countries driven by low mortgage rates and pandemic-related lifestyle changes. It presents 10 graphs to illustrate trends, noting Canada's more outstanding growth in starts and differences in single-family versus multi-family construction between the two nations, alongside regional insights and future outlooks.

title: Amazon has spent billions to get within a 1-hour delivery distance of many U.S. customers, but Walmart and Target are still winning that race
summary: Despite Amazon investing $35 billion in 2020 to build out its delivery infrastructure, Walmart and Target, with their extensive network of brick-and-mortar stores, remain closer to more U.S. customers for swift delivery. This suggests that the physical presence of traditional retailers still provides a competitive edge in rapid fulfillment, even against Amazon's substantial e-commerce investments.

title: These stores will be open on the Fourth of July
summary: This article lists various retail and grocery stores that will be open or closed on the Fourth of July, along with their operating hours. It serves as a guide for shoppers and those running errands during the holiday. The information is relevant for anyone planning activities that involve shopping on Independence Day.

title: We Love These Air-Powered Half-Inch Drive Impact Wrenches
summary: This article highlights the enduring power and utility of air-powered half-inch drive impact wrenches, despite the rise of cordless electric tools. It recommends several top models from brands like Ingersoll Rand, Aircat, and Campbell Hausfeld, detailing their key features such as torque, weight, and suggested use cases. The article emphasizes that pneumatic impact wrenches remain superior for raw nut-busting torque, making them essential tools for professional and serious DIY mechanics.

title: Third Conviction Concludes StaMedia Fraud Saga
summary: The StaMedia fraud saga has concluded with the third and final conviction, sending three Texas con men to prison for defrauding investors of millions. Richard Gregory Tilford received 40 years, Bobby Guess received 12 years, and former pastor Timothy Lloyd Booth, who stole $23 million primarily from elderly individuals, was sentenced to 68 years. The scam involved false claims of advertising contracts with AT&T and The Home Depot, promising high returns that never materialized.

title: Home Depot, Lowe's amp up focus on home pros, as consumers swap DIY projects for parties, travel
summary: Home Depot and Lowe's are shifting their growth strategy to focus on home professionals, as consumers are increasingly opting for travel and social activities over DIY projects post-pandemic. Both retailers are investing in services, supply chain improvements, and loyalty programs to attract and retain professional contractors, who represent a significant and growing revenue stream. While Home Depot historically has a larger pro business, Lowe's is aggressively expanding its share in this lucrative market.

title: Mistakes Everyone Makes When Shopping At Home Depot
summary: This article highlights common mistakes shoppers make at Home Depot and provides tips to save money and improve the shopping experience. It covers strategies such as renting tools instead of buying, checking for rebates, utilizing "oops" paint, monitoring daily deals, leveraging the Low Price Guarantee, understanding price tag hacks, using coupons, keeping receipts, joining the Garden Club, shopping holiday sales, securing free shipping, and signing up for the Pro Xtra loyalty program.

title: European pension managers go big for indoor ag as Equilibrium closes $1.1bn CEA fund
summary: Equilibrium Capital has successfully closed its second indoor agriculture fund, Controlled Environment Foods Fund II (CEFF II), at over $1 billion, significantly exceeding its $500 million target. The fund attracted substantial investment from institutional investors, primarily European pension funds like Sweden's AP4 and two large UK pension managers, highlighting a growing demand for sustainable real assets in agriculture. CEFF II will focus on investing in high-tech greenhouses, vertical farms, and other controlled environment agriculture facilities across North America, with specific interest in crops like tomatoes, peppers, cucumbers, leafy greens, and berries.

title: Preparing for Disaster Season with Canter Power Systems
summary: Canter Power Systems, established in 1948, is the largest residential generator installer in the U.S. and a trusted service provider for The Home Depot. The company specializes in handling high demand for generators during disaster seasons, scaling inventory and services to meet needs, and successfully adapted to virtual sales during the COVID-19 pandemic. Canter Power provides personalized customer service with factory-certified technicians and 24/7 technical support, offering a seamless experience for homeowners seeking automatic standby generators.

title: Developers, major retailers keep betting on the Southside for logistics
summary: Major retailers and developers continue to invest in Atlanta's Southside for logistics due to its strategic location. Companies like Home Depot, Kroger, and Cummins Inc. benefit from its proximity to the airport, rail, and interstate highway system for national distribution. The area is experiencing significant development activity and demand for distribution centers.

title: "At Home" Store Coming to Washington Township's The Dump Location (Leasing Company Site).
summary: A new "At Home" home decor store is confirmed to be coming to the former The Dump location on Route 42 in Washington Township, according to the website of leasing company Urban Edge Properties. This move signifies a significant retail development for the area, as At Home stores are massive, typically 90,000-120,000 square feet, and are expected to draw shoppers from a wide distance. The existing The Dump store will eventually vacate the premises to make way for the new establishment.

title: 10,000 new homes planned in Reunion community northwest of Fort Worth
summary: A new massive residential community called Reunion is planned northwest of Fort Worth, targeting 10,000 single-family homes at buildout, making it one of North Texas's largest. The project is expected to add significantly to the region's housing landscape.

title: The Home Depot and Google Cloud Expand Partnership to Enhance the Interconnected Shopping Experience
summary: The Home Depot and Google Cloud have extended their multi-year partnership to enhance the retailer's digital transformation and improve customer shopping experiences in physical and digital environments. Building on Google Cloud's expertise since 2015, The Home Depot leverages AI, ML, and data analytics for features like "Rent Online, Pick Up In Store," predictive inventory management, and voice search. The collaboration aims to provide scalability and personalized experiences for customers and associates.

title: Home Depot plans to foil shoplifters with power tools that won't work if they're stolen
summary: Home Depot is implementing a new anti-theft measure for power tools that renders them non-functional unless properly activated at the register via Bluetooth. This initiative targets organized retail crime, which costs retailers significantly, without negatively impacting legitimate customers with excessive physical deterrents like locked cases. The company plans to roll out this technology across its 1,988 US stores after successful testing.

title: Websites back up after brief global outage linked to Akamai
summary: Many websites experienced a global outage for about an hour due to a glitch in Akamai Technologies Inc.'s systems, specifically a bug in its domain name system (DNS) service triggered during a software update. Akamai quickly implemented a fix by rolling back the update, confirming the disruption was not a cyberattack. This incident marked the second significant disruption linked to Akamai in approximately a month, affecting major sites including Delta Air Lines, Costco, American Express, and Home Depot.

title: Home Depot Extends Google Cloud Deal
summary: Home Depot Inc. has announced it is extending its multiyear cloud-services deal with Google Cloud. This decision comes after a period of explosive online sales during the pandemic, with the home-improvement chain attributing the cloud's capabilities to helping it respond quickly to changing market trends. The partnership aims to expand the digital tools that supported rocketing demand from DIY customers and professional contractors.

title: Amazon, Airbnb, UPS among major firms to face brief outage; Akamai says issues fixed | World News
summary: Major companies including Amazon, Airbnb, and UPS experienced a brief service outage due to a disruption from Akamai Technologies, a web content delivery provider. Akamai quickly implemented a fix, and services rapidly resumed normal operations. The disruption also affected Indian companies like Zomato and Paytm.

title: Home Depot uses Bluetooth to prevent stolen items from working and combat organized retail crime
summary: Home Depot is implementing Bluetooth technology in select stores to combat organized retail crime. This system will activate purchased power tools at the point of sale, rendering stolen items inoperable. This initiative aims to deter theft and resale of stolen merchandise.

title: The Home Depot Reduced Carbon Emissions by More Than 127,000 Metric Tons in 2020; Commits to 100 Percent Renewable Electricity for Facilities by 2030
summary: The Home Depot reduced its Scope 1 and 2 carbon emissions by over 127,000 metric tons in 2020, achieving a 22 percent reduction in carbon intensity. The company has set a new goal to achieve 100 percent renewable electricity for its facilities by 2030 and has partnered with the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) to establish further emissions reduction targets. These commitments were detailed in their 2021 ESG Report, which also highlighted their social and governance initiatives.

title: Traeger, Weber battle it out in barbecue IPO mini-boom as consumers spend billions on outdoor cooking
summary: The pandemic-driven surge in at-home grilling has led to a mini-boom in barbecue company IPOs, with Traeger and Weber leading the charge. Traeger priced its IPO at $18, valuing it at $2 billion, while rival Weber is also planning to go public with an expected valuation between $4 billion and $6 billion. Other companies like BBQGuys are also entering the public market, capitalizing on consumers spending billions on outdoor cooking equipment.

title: Berlin Raceway ready to celebrate big contest victory with the community
summary: Berlin Raceway in Marne, Michigan, is hosting a celebration night to commemorate its win of the Advance Auto Parts 'Advance My Track' challenge, which awarded them $50,000. The event will feature a pre-race concert, a full night of racing, and fireworks. The prize money will be used to refurbish the concession stand and turn two-deck, as well as establish a non-profit to bring disadvantaged children to the racetrack.

title: A breakdown of US value ETFs
summary: This article analyzes five US value ETFs, highlighting that only three of them outperformed Vanguard's S&P 500 ETF despite 2021 being anticipated as a strong year for value factor resurgence. It details the methodologies, holdings, and performance of each ETF (iShares Edge MSCI USA Value Factor UCITS ETF, Ossiam Shiller Barclays Cape US Sector Value UCITS ETF, UBS ETF Factor MSCI USA Value UCITS ETF, UBS ETF Factor MSCI USA Prime Value UCITS ETF, and SPDR MSCI USA Value Weighted UCITS ETF) and discusses the importance of index design and Total Expense Ratios (TERs) in their relative performance.

title: Coronavirus: Starbucks, McDonald’s, Home Depot to require workers wear masks inside all locations
summary: Starbucks, McDonald’s, and Home Depot are reinstating indoor mask mandates for their employees due to the surge in COVID-19 infections caused by the delta variant. McDonald's and Target will specifically enforce these measures in high-risk transmission areas as identified by the CDC. These policy changes align with the CDC's updated recommendations urging vaccinated individuals to resume wearing masks indoors in certain settings.

title: Coca-Cola latest to delay Atlanta office returns; Invesco sets mandate
summary: Coca-Cola has delayed the return of its employees to its Atlanta headquarters until mid-October at the earliest due to the surge of the COVID-19 delta variant. Atlanta-based Invesco has also set a vaccine mandate for nearly 1,000 U.S. employees, requiring proof of vaccination for office returns. Other major local companies have been adjusting their return-to-office plans amid the ongoing pandemic.

title: The Home Depot Creates Nearly 500 New Jobs in Baltimore with New Distribution Centers
summary: The Home Depot has opened three new distribution centers in Baltimore, creating nearly 500 new full- and part-time jobs. These facilities, part of a $1.2 billion investment in its supply chain, will enhance delivery options for customers in the region, including same-day and next-day delivery goals. The expansion aims to improve the shopping experience for both Pro and DIY customers by offering faster access to a broader range of products.

title: The C.T. and Octavia Vivian Museum and Archives, Inc. and The Home Depot Foundation Partner to Launch Curriculum Focused on the Life and Teachings of Dr. C.T. Vivian
summary: The C.T. and Octavia Vivian Museum and Archives, Inc. and The Home Depot Foundation have partnered to introduce a new 16-week collegiate curriculum focused on the life and teachings of civil rights leader Dr. C.T. Vivian. The course, "It’s In The Action," will be offered at several universities this fall, including Emory University and Morehouse College, providing students with a comprehensive study of Vivian's advocacy for equality through nonviolent strategies. This initiative aligns with The Home Depot Foundation's commitment to social equity through education and workforce development.

title: Home Depot punished staff for BLM activism, U.S. labor board alleges
summary: The U.S. labor board has filed a complaint alleging that Home Depot punished staff for Black Lives Matter activism, including forcing out a worker who wore a "BLM" apron. The complaint states that Home Depot selectively enforced its dress code and threatened employees to prevent protests against racial harassment. Home Depot denies the allegations, stating that the labor board "misrepresents the relevant facts" and that the company does not tolerate workplace harassment.

title: Sherwin-Williams Co. stock rises Monday, outperforms market
summary: Sherwin-Williams Co. stock (SHW) rose 0.69% on Monday, outperforming the broader market indices like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average. The company also reached a new 52-week high, surpassing its previous peak from August 13th. While some competitors also saw gains, Sherwin-Williams' trading volume was slightly below its 50-day average.

title: Home improvement boom’s next phase favors Home Depot
summary: Wall Street's predictions of a fizzling pandemic-fueled home improvement boom have not materialized, with growth potentially entering a new phase. Home Depot is expected to benefit more in this next phase, as the "pro" business, where Home Depot has a larger share, is now recovering and outpacing DIY sales, which historically favored Lowe's. The article highlights both the continued growth drivers, such as surging home prices leading to bigger renovations, and potential headwinds including travel rebounds and consumer confidence dips.

title: Ulta Beauty at Target Opens First 52 Doors
summary: Ulta Beauty at Target has opened its first 52 doors, out of an anticipated 100 this year, launching shops-in-shop featuring over 50 prestige beauty brands like MAC Cosmetics and Clinique. The partnership aims to provide Target customers with a curated selection of prestige beauty products and drive Ulta customers to its full-line stores or website. This collaboration follows other store-in-store concepts and leverages the loyalty programs of both retailers.

title: The Home Depot, Inc. Announces Rise In Q2 Profit, Beats estimates
summary: The Home Depot, Inc. (HD) reported a significant increase in its second-quarter profit, with earnings rising to $4.81 billion, or $4.53 per share, surpassing analyst expectations of $4.43 per share. The company's revenue also saw an 8.1% increase, reaching $41.12 billion for the quarter. These results indicate strong financial performance for Home Depot in Q2.

title: The Home Depot Announces Second Quarter 2021 Results
summary: The Home Depot reported strong second-quarter 2021 results, with sales reaching $41.1 billion, an 8.1% increase from the previous year, marking the first time quarterly sales exceeded $40 billion. Comparable sales rose by 4.5% overall and 3.4% in the U.S., while net earnings increased by 12.7% to $4.8 billion, or $4.53 per diluted share. The company credited these achievements to the dedication of its associates and robust customer service.

title: Home Depot Sales Climb, but Remodeling Frenzy May Be Cooling
summary: Home Depot reported a surge in sales for the three months ended August 1st, exceeding analyst expectations and surpassing $40 billion for the first time quarterly. However, same-store sales growth slowed compared to previous periods, and customer traffic decreased, indicating a potential cooling of the pandemic-driven home remodeling boom. The company's shares fell, and no full-year forecast was provided.

title: Procter & Gamble has a brand problem
summary: A survey by Fortune and Civis Analytics reveals that Procter & Gamble has a significant generational favorability gap, with only 36% of 18–34 year olds having a favorable view compared to 87% of those over 65. This gap is largely attributed to younger Americans not having heard of P&G, despite the company's efforts in environmental sustainability and its massive advertising budget for individual brands like Tide and Crest. While P&G has the largest net favorability gap, its overall net favorability score remains high at +50 points.

title: Walmart Merchants Charter Ships to Get Inventory to US Stores
summary: Walmart is chartering its own ships to transport merchandise to its U.S. stores in an effort to manage ongoing supply chain challenges and inventory levels. The retail giant, like many others, has been impacted by port delays and import surges but believes these proactive steps will position them well for the busy third and fourth quarters. This strategy mirrors actions taken by other large retailers like Home Depot, while smaller businesses continue to struggle with shipping capacity.

title: The Home Depot Declares Second Quarter Dividend of $1.65
summary: The Home Depot announced that its board of directors declared a second quarter cash dividend of $1.65 per share. The dividend is payable on September 16, 2021, to shareholders of record on September 2, 2021. This marks the 138th consecutive quarter the company has paid a cash dividend.

title: Big retailers book pricey private cargo ships in holiday scramble
summary: Major retailers like Walmart, Home Depot, and Ikea are chartering private cargo ships and buying their own containers to bypass supply chain disruptions ahead of the holiday season. These unprecedented and costly measures are being taken to ensure shelves remain stocked amid surging consumer demand and port congestion. This strategy gives larger retailers a competitive advantage over smaller businesses facing inventory shortages.

title: Home Depot Robocall Class Action Settlement
summary: Home Depot and Atlantic Water and Air agreed to a $4.35 million settlement to resolve a class action lawsuit over unwanted robocalls. The settlement benefits consumers who received automated calls between October 16, 2013, and June 1, 2015, with estimated payouts of $110 per Class Member, capped at $5,000. The lawsuit alleged violations of the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) after consumers' information, obtained from free water tests, was used for unsolicited sales calls.

title: The Home Depot to open Northwest Jacksonville delivery center
summary: The Home Depot plans to open a new market delivery operations (MDO) center in Northwest Jacksonville, located in the Perimeter West Industrial Park. This facility, which is a strategic investment in their supply chain network, aims to offer same-day and next-day delivery to 90% of the United States. The city is currently reviewing a permit application for FCL Builders Inc. to build out the 66,990-square-foot space, with a projected construction cost of $1.67 million.

title: News Taiwan’s TSMC to charter boxship to deliver semiconductor components to US
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co (TSMC) is reportedly in discussions with Wan Hai to charter a containership to transport components for its new Phoenix, Arizona plant from Kaohsiung to the US. This decision follows similar actions by Home Depot and Walmart, with unconfirmed reports suggesting TSMC's chairman has approved chartering an entire vessel for an estimated cost of at least $107 million. The Phoenix plant is expected to begin producing 5-nanometer chips in 2024, as TSMC invests $100 billion over three years to expand its semiconductor fabrication capacity.

title: Home Depot improves inventory depth with focus on high-velocity SKUs
summary: Home Depot is enhancing its inventory by focusing on high-demand products and chartering its own ships to navigate supply chain disruptions. This strategy, prioritizing "highest velocity SKUs" like electrical and plumbing fixtures, has led to a 24% increase in customer transactions over $1,000, despite an overall 6% drop in transactions. The company's efforts, including working closely with suppliers to narrow product focus, resulted in a 26% year-over-year inventory value increase and an 8% net sales increase in Q2.

title: TSMC May Charter its Own Boxship to Transport Chip-Making Equipment
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC) is reportedly considering chartering its own container ship to transport manufacturing equipment to its new facility in Phoenix, Arizona. This strategic move aims to significantly reduce the high costs associated with conventional containerized freight given current market rates. The first plant, costing $12 billion, is expected to begin mass production in 2024, with the first batch of containers anticipated to depart in October.

title: The Home Depot to Present at Goldman Sachs 28th Annual Global Retailing Virtual Conference
summary: The Home Depot announced that its chairman and CEO, Craig Menear, and president & COO, Ted Decker, would present at the Goldman Sachs 28th Annual Global Retailing Virtual Conference. The presentation was scheduled for September 10, 2021, and was to be webcast live. The company also provided an overview of its operations, noting its status as the world's largest home improvement retailer.

title: Home Depot launches Path to Pro program in Houston area to help people find skilled trade jobs
summary: Home Depot has launched a "Path to Pro" program in Houston to help people find skilled trade jobs in fields like HVAC, carpentry, electrical, and plumbing. The free online program, which takes about 10 hours to complete, connects graduates with employers. Additionally, the Houston Gulf Coast Building and Construction Trades Council offers an apprenticeship readiness program for those interested in union-supported construction careers.

title: REAL ESTATE BRIEFS: Home sales booming this year in North River Ranch
summary: Home sales in North River Ranch, a master-planned community by Neal Land & Neighborhoods, have significantly exceeded expectations in the first half of 2021. The community sold 234 homes, over 42% above its goal, with an average sale price of $369,000, which is nearly $40,000 less than other Manatee County neighborhoods. Additional homesites are planned for the Brightwood neighborhood, with prices ranging from the $300,000s to over $800,000.

title: Looking for work? The Home Depot supply-chain offers positions in Luzerne County
summary: The Home Depot is actively hiring for over 300 part-time and full-time supply chain positions across three facilities in Pittston, Luzerne County, Pennsylvania. These warehouse associate roles involve fulfilling online orders and replenishing store inventory, offering competitive pay, consistent schedules, and opportunities for career advancement. Interested job seekers can apply online or by texting "WAREHOUSE" to 52270 for more information.

title: Lowe's says inventory in better position in months amid supply-chain snafu
summary: Lowe's has proactively brought holiday products into its stores and warehouses earlier than planned, anticipating supply chain disruptions. Despite broader industry challenges with inventory due to COVID-19-led factory closures and port congestion, Lowe's Chief Financial Officer David Denton stated the company's inventory position and supply chain are in a better state compared to several months ago. Lowe's has also placed larger orders for high-demand items to ensure product availability during the crucial holiday season.

title: Bargains coming to Del Rio, Ollie's Celebrates Grand Opening this coming week
summary: Ollie's Bargain Outlet is celebrating the grand opening of its newest store in Del Rio, Texas, on September 15th, offering brand name closeouts at up to 70% off. This marks their 21st store in Texas and is expected to create 50-60 new jobs for the local community. Ollie's is known for its wide selection of discounted merchandise across various categories.

title: Lawsuit: Home Depot doesn’t give workers enough breaks
summary: A class-action lawsuit filed in Snohomish County Superior Court alleges that Home Depot stores in Washington state fail to provide their hourly employees with legally required meal and rest breaks. The suit, which could involve at least 10,000 workers across 45 locations, claims chronic understaffing prevents employees from taking mandated breaks. While some employees support the claims of missed breaks, others have stated they rarely, if ever, missed them.

title: Ross Dress For Less to move into other half of former Hen House at Merriam Town Center
summary: Ross Dress for Less is set to occupy half of the former Hen House Market space at Merriam Town Center, sharing the renovated building with Bob’s Discount Furniture. The discount department store's arrival is welcomed by city officials, who anticipate the store could be complete within 45 to 60 days, though an official opening date has not been set. The move resolves a long-standing vacancy since the Hen House closed in 2018, bringing a nationally recognized retailer to the shopping center.

title: Mike Amend | Canada | English
summary: This article provides a biography of Mike Amend, Chief Enterprise Technology Officer at Ford. It details his role in leading Ford's Enterprise Technology Organization, including Information Technology and Global Data Insight and Analytics, and his focus on leveraging data, software, and technology for growth. The article also highlights his previous experience at Lowe's, JCPenney, The Home Depot, Dell Technologies, BEA Systems, and Sprint, and his board directorships at Canada Life and Ford Motor Credit Company.

title: Ford hires former Lowe's, Home Depot executive as chief digital and information officer
summary: Ford Motor Co. has appointed Mike Amend, formerly of Lowe's Companies Inc., as its new chief digital and information officer to lead the company's technology and software platforms. This strategic hire aligns with CEO Jim Farley's vision to transform Ford through electrification and advanced technologies, leveraging Amend's experience in e-commerce and digital growth from his previous roles at Lowe's, JCPenney, and Home Depot. Amend will work alongside Hau Thai-Tang and recent hire Doug Field to drive Ford's technological initiatives and develop new software solutions.

title: Kroger Joins Buy Safe America Coalition
summary: Kroger has joined the Buy Safe America Coalition, a group dedicated to combating organized retail crime and protecting consumers from counterfeit and stolen goods. This move reinforces Kroger's commitment to fighting the billions of dollars lost annually to such crimes, often facilitated by online marketplaces with minimal seller verification. The grocer supports the INFORM Consumers Act and has its own dedicated crime unit, having initiated over 2,000 organized retail crime cases.

title: Home Depot Inc. stock falls Monday, still outperforms market
summary: Shares of Home Depot Inc. (HD) fell 1.33% on Monday to $331.21, despite a broader market decline where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also fell. The stock closed $14.48 short of its 52-week high and demonstrated a mixed performance compared to competitors like Lowe's Cos. and Kingfisher PLC ADR. Trading volume for Home Depot exceeded its 50-day average.

title: Target to expand Pr. George's distribution center into what may be region's largest
summary: Target plans to expand its former Safeway warehouse campus in Upper Marlboro, Prince George's County, potentially making it the largest distribution center in the region. The retail giant acquired the campus in December.

title: For Home Depot, tackling capacity crunch key in pandemic strategy
summary: During the pandemic, Home Depot faced significant supply chain capacity challenges due to a 20% increase in volume. To address this, the retailer charted its own ships and utilized freight visibility tools to strategically manage container entry points. UPS also experienced unexpected demand surges, leading them to optimize existing capacity, automate facilities, and expedite hiring to mitigate daily package volume shortfalls.

title: How Back to the Roots is Helping Children Garden and Grow
summary: Back to the Roots, founded by Alejandro Vélez and Nikhil Arora, creates indoor gardening kits with a mission to enable the next generation to grow food regardless of space constraints or gardening experience. The company, which became a diverse supplier for The Home Depot in 2012, donates grow kits to underfunded schools through its #GrowOneGiveOne program, providing hands-on products and STEM curriculum. This initiative aims to integrate gardening, nutrition, and food education into children's learning.

title: Retail’s new fad? Charter ships to ensure sales, even if it’s costly.
summary: Amid soaring container ship charter rates and limited capacity, retailers like Home Depot, Ikea, Walmart, and Dollar Tree are chartering their own ships to secure product deliveries for the holidays and beyond. This costly measure is seen as necessary to avoid even greater losses from unsold goods due to shipping delays. Experts suggest this trend will continue due to depleted inventories and persistent demand.

title: Home Depot expanding operations across SC, including in North Charleston
summary: Home Depot announced plans to expand its operations across South Carolina, creating nearly 100 new jobs. This expansion aims to enhance distribution capabilities to meet growing demand and provide faster delivery to customers in the region. The new positions will be located in North Charleston, Greenville, Jasper, and Lexington Counties.

title: SICO Paint by PPG Unveils 2022 Colour of the Year: Cool Current
summary: SICO Paint by PPG has announced Cool Current (6199-42), a sophisticated grey-green, as its 2022 Colour of the Year, reflecting Canadians' desire for authenticity, nature, and meaningful human interaction after a year of lockdowns. This choice signifies a shift in consumer preferences towards more saturated hues and away from neutral palettes, influenced by post-pandemic optimism and a return to more defined living spaces. PPG's annual Global Colour Forecasting Workshop determined this trend, seeing inspiration from historical design eras and emphasizing resilience, connection, and nature.

title: Jamaican Ann-Marie Campbell Started as a Cashier at Home Depot and is now Executive VP Overseeing Over 2,000 Stores
summary: Ann-Marie Campbell, born in Kingston, Jamaica, began her career at Home Depot as a cashier in 1985 and has since risen to the position of Executive VP, overseeing 2,200 stores and international operations for Canada and Mexico. She is recognized for her leadership, appearing on Fortune's Most Powerful Women in Business list, and actively contributes to her community through various board memberships and the Ann-Marie Campbell Scholarship at Georgia State University. Her journey highlights her determination and impact in a male-dominated industry.

title: The Home Depot Canada Foundation launches TradeWorx to help youth experiencing homelessness establish careers in skilled trades
summary: The Home Depot Canada Foundation has launched TradeWorx, a new initiative with an initial $1 million commitment to help youth experiencing homelessness build careers in skilled trades. The program will provide training and social support to one hundred Canadian youth, addressing both youth homelessness and the high demand for skilled labor in the construction industry. This builds on the Foundation's previous investments of over $42 million in combating youth homelessness since 2009.

title: Sources: Dick's Sporting Goods scouting for satellite office in the city
summary: Dick's Sporting Goods, headquartered in Coraopolis, is reportedly seeking a satellite office in Pittsburgh. Sources indicate the company has hired a local firm for the search, with the Terminal in the Strip District potentially being a top contender. This move suggests an expansion of the retailer's corporate presence within the city.

title: The Home Depot Commits $10 Million to Venture Capital Funds Focused on Diversity and Innovation
summary: The Home Depot announced a $10 million investment in venture capital funds focused on promoting diversity, technology, and entrepreneurship. These investments include Base10 Partners Advancement Initiative, L'ATTITUDE VENTURES, and Plexo Capital, aiming to support minority-owned companies, HBCUs, and diverse founders. This initiative is part of The Home Depot's broader commitment to social equity, building on previous investments and programs.

title: Do it Best names Vendors of the Year at fall market
summary: Do it Best announced its Vendors of the Year at its annual fall market in Indianapolis. Awards were given for overall sales growth, supply chain excellence, outstanding products and services, and lumber and building materials excellence, along with specific departmental awards. Stanley Black & Decker, Global Harvest Foods, Scotts Miracle-Gro Company, and Metal Sales were among the top honorees.

title: Pharr to Get One of Five Tractor Supply Stores Breaking Ground Soon
summary: Tractor Supply Company plans to open five new stores in Texas, including one in Pharr, with construction starting in early 2022. Other stores will break ground in Lucas, Midland, Borger, and Stephenville, with estimated costs ranging from $2.1 million to $3 million per location. Oxford Architecture and HBC Interests LLC are among the firms involved in the design and development of these new retail outlets.

title: 13 Really Cool Tiles We Found at The Home Depot
summary: This article highlights 13 unique and stylish tile options available at Home Depot, suitable for kitchen and bathroom makeovers. It showcases various designs, from mosaic and patterned to bold colors and geometric shapes, demonstrating how tiles can enhance any space without requiring a splurge. The selections aim to inspire creativity beyond standard subway tiles, offering diverse aesthetic choices for different interior styles.

title: Ring and The Home Depot Announce Ring Jobsite Security, A New Way to Secure Job Sites
summary: Ring and The Home Depot have partnered to launch Ring Jobsite Security, an exclusive offering designed to protect construction sites. This system leverages the new Ring Alarm Pro, providing professional monitoring, cellular connectivity, and battery backup, making Ring's home security products adaptable for job site needs. It offers customizable solutions with various Ring devices, aiming to provide affordable security that was previously only accessible to large-scale builders.

title: Home Depot’s insanely popular 12-foot skeleton—key marketing stats and facts
summary: This article discusses the marketing phenomenon surrounding Home Depot's immensely popular 12-foot skeleton decoration. It highlights the significant attention and engagement generated by this product, making it a key case study in effective seasonal retail marketing. The piece provides an overview of its impact and popularity just as the Halloween season begins.

title: The Home Depot’s 2021 Innovation Awards
summary: The Home Depot announced its 2021 Innovation Awards, with the Milwaukee M18 FUEL Cordless Framing Nailer taking the top honor. Hubspace smart home technology by Afero and Pergo Defense+ waterproof, antimicrobial flooring by Mohawk Industries were recognized as the first and second runners-up, respectively. The awards celebrate suppliers providing innovative and exclusive products that make home improvement easier, safer, and more enjoyable for customers.

title: Home Depot, Loadsmart take aim at empty flatbed miles
summary: Home Depot and Loadsmart have partnered to launch Flatbed Messenger, a marketplace designed to reduce empty miles for flatbed truck carriers. The platform utilizes algorithms to match available trucks and backhaul capacity with shipper loads, aiming to decrease deadheads for carriers and improve overall efficiency in the fragmented flatbed industry. This initiative also seeks to address sustainability concerns by optimizing routes and lowering emissions, aligning with growing pressure for greener logistics.

title: Walmart, Target, Home Depot and other large retailers are chartering ships to bypass supply chain problems. Will the strategy save Christmas?
summary: Large retailers like Walmart, Target, and Home Depot are chartering their own ships to mitigate severe supply chain disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. This strategy is an attempt to ensure they have enough inventory for the crucial holiday shopping season, bypassing bottlenecks at ports and other transportation challenges. Retailers are facing unprecedented logistic issues, highlighting the lengths they must go to maintain their supply lines.

title: The Home Depot Announces 2021 Innovation Award Winners
summary: The Home Depot announced its 2021 Innovation Award winners, recognizing suppliers who developed innovative products that enhance DIY and Pro projects. The Milwaukee M18 FUEL Cordless Framing Nailer won the overall award, with Hubspace and Pergo Defense+ taking first and second runner-up honors. The company also honored suppliers for environmental, interconnected, marketing, and diversity innovations.

title: Developers Diversified PR returns to local retail market to operate 9 shopping centers
summary: Developers Diversified PR has re-entered the Puerto Rico retail market after a 15-year absence, acquiring nine shopping centers formerly owned by Retail Value Inc. Developer Scott Wolstein, who previously founded the original Developers Diversified Realty, will oversee the portfolio with the aim of restoring its performance to pre-Hurricane María levels. The company believes there are "tailwinds" in the market, including the influx of wealthy Americans and potential manufacturing shifts to the hemisphere, despite significant economic challenges.

title: Walmart lands Home Depot as its first fast-delivery customer
summary: Walmart has secured Home Depot as the first major client for its new GoLocal fast delivery service. This partnership will focus on same-day and next-day delivery of smaller items for Home Depot, starting in select states before expanding. The collaboration highlights a growing trend of retailers working together, even competitors, to enhance e-commerce and delivery capabilities.

title: Home Depot teams up with Walmart’s GoLocal for speedy delivery service
summary: Home Depot has partnered with Walmart's GoLocal service to offer same-day and next-day delivery to its customers. This collaboration aims to help Home Depot achieve its goal of providing fast delivery to 90% of the U.S. and highlights a growing trend of rival companies partnering on fulfillment services.

title: Home Depot Partners With Walmart for Local Deliveries
summary: The Home Depot has partnered with Walmart to expand its same-day and next-day delivery services across the U.S. through Walmart GoLocal. This collaboration makes Home Depot the first retail client for Walmart GoLocal, which launched in August. The initiative aims to enhance delivery options for a wide range of products, capitalizing on Home Depot's significant digital sales growth in the past year.

title: Ordering a power tool from Home Depot? Walmart may be the one delivering it to you
summary: Walmart has launched a new service called GoLocal, which will deliver goods from other businesses' websites to customers, with Home Depot being the first customer. This initiative allows Walmart to expand beyond its core retail business and leverage its logistics network for same-day or next-day deliveries, particularly in underserved markets. By partnering with businesses like Home Depot, Walmart aims to lower delivery costs and increase work for its Spark platform drivers, despite facing stiff competition in the last-mile delivery sector.

title: Idaho Falls OfficeMax to close
summary: The OfficeMax store on Northgate Mile in Idaho Falls is scheduled to close permanently on November 13, 2021, reflecting broader retail trends and shifts in the city's commercial landscape. This closure is part of ODP Corporation's strategy to reduce its retail footprint and spin off its retail operations. The area around the store, once a bustling retail hub, has seen significant changes as businesses moved to other parts of Idaho Falls and into commercial/light industrial uses.

title: The Home Depot Teams Up with Walmart GoLocal to Enhance Local Delivery Capabilities
summary: The Home Depot is partnering with Walmart GoLocal to expand its same-day and next-day delivery capabilities for home improvement customers across the U.S. This collaboration makes The Home Depot the first retail client for Walmart's new white-label delivery service, aiming to offer fast and reliable delivery to 90 percent of the U.S. population. The service will initially roll out in select markets with plans for national expansion by year-end, covering a variety of products from tools to paint.

title: Coca-Cola thinks ‘outside the box,’ books bulk vessels to ship supplies
summary: Coca-Cola is utilizing bulk vessels to transport materials, a non-traditional approach to navigate limited vessel space and keep production lines running globally. This strategy, adopted by other retailers facing supply chain congestion, involves carrying over 60,000 tons of material to non-congested ports to avoid delays and high demurrage fees. While individual company actions may not shift market dynamics, this move highlights the significant impact and overstretched state of current logistics.

title: Lowe’s taps Mike Shady to lead online business as it eyes continued growth
summary: Lowe's has appointed Mike Shady to lead its online business as Senior Vice President. Shady aims to boost online traffic and support the company's omnichannel strategy amidst strong competition. This move comes as the home-improvement retailer plans for continued growth in its digital operations.

title: 1099C Language in Collection Letters: Third Circuit District Court Grants Defendants’ Motion for Summary Judgment in FDCPA Case
summary: A Third Circuit district court granted summary judgment to defendants in an FDCPA case concerning 1099C language in collection letters. The court ruled that including language about potential IRS reporting for debt settlements of $600 or more is not false, deceptive, or misleading if there is a possibility that such reporting would be required. This decision reinforces that such language is permissible when the debt amount allows for potential IRS reporting, even under the "least sophisticated debtor" standard.

title: Home Depot delivery center approved for Northwest Jacksonville
summary: The city of Jacksonville has approved a permit for FCL Builders LLC to construct a $1.67 million Home Depot delivery center in the Perimeter West Industrial Park. This 66,990-square-foot facility is part of Home Depot's strategy to expand its supply chain network for same-day/next-day delivery services. The center will be located at 4345 Perimeter Industrial Parkway, with nearly 90,000 square feet remaining available for lease in the same building.

title: Home Depot Inc. stock underperforms Friday when compared to competitors
summary: Home Depot Inc. (HD) stock declined by 0.93% on Friday, closing at $334.34, in a generally poor trading session for the stock market. This underperformance was observed relative to its competitors, with Lowe's Cos. (LOW) also falling but Kingfisher PLC ADR (KGFHY) rising. The stock's fall ended a three-day winning streak and it closed below its 52-week high.

title: Greenville’s Everett Sports Marketing serves exclusive client list, delivers huge results
