summary: Everett Sports Marketing (ESM), founded by Dan Everett, has grown from a side-gig into one of the nation's premier NFL player marketing firms, based in Greenville. The company specializes in securing significant endorsement deals for a selective list of NFL athletes, including Jalen Hurts and Nick Chubb. ESM attributes its success to maintaining a small client roster with a robust staff, enabling them to deliver personalized service and record-breaking marketing arrangements.

title: Merriam city council candidates on the issues: The future of Merriam Town Center
summary: Merriam city council candidates discuss the future of the Merriam Town Center, which has seen major tenants leave, including the city's only grocery store. Candidates provided diverse opinions on potential redevelopment into a mixed-use area with housing and green space, addressing concerns about blight, economic incentives, and creating a vibrant draw for residents. The discussion highlights differing views on the timing and necessity of a comprehensive redevelopment versus more immediate, cost-effective revitalization strategies.

title: Ken’s Krew: Championing Ability and Enabling Success
summary: Ken's Krew, supported by Home Depot co-founder Ken Langone, provides job placement, training, and support for individuals with neurodevelopmental disabilities. The Home Depot has partnered with Ken’s Krew since 1997, employing 450 Krew members across 162 stores with significantly higher retention rates than the industry standard. The program tailors training and offers ongoing support, fostering personal and professional growth for its members.

title: LaserShip taps top Home Depot supply chain executive as CEO
summary: Regional parcel delivery carrier LaserShip has named Mark Holifield, the architect of Home Depot's modern-day supply chain operation, as its new CEO, effective November 8th. Holifield's appointment signals a serious effort by LaserShip's owner, American Securities LLC, to build a national delivery network, especially following reports of LaserShip's acquisition of OnTrac. His extensive experience in supply chain and e-commerce logistics from Home Depot is expected to be crucial as the parcel sector faces an unprecedented holiday delivery season and aims for national expansion.

title: Long-time Home Depot exec Mark Holifield leaving to be delivery firm's CEO
summary: Mark Holifield, a veteran executive at Home Depot, is departing the company to become the CEO of a delivery firm. Holifield joined Home Depot in 2006 and was instrumental in transforming the home improvement giant's supply chain. This move marks a significant leadership change for Home Depot's logistics operations.

title: Amazon Bulks Up Shipping Capacity to Battle Holiday Season Snarls
summary: Amazon announced it has doubled its container processing capacity and secured more shipping storage from ocean freight carriers to mitigate supply chain issues ahead of the holiday shopping season. The company also plans to hire 150,000 seasonal workers and has increased its ports of entry by 50%. This move comes as other major retailers like Walmart and Target are also chartering ships to cope with pandemic-driven supply chain disruptions.

title: West Fraser To Acquire Georgia Pacific OSB Mill In South Carolina
summary: West Fraser Timber Co. Ltd. is set to acquire Georgia Pacific's oriented strand board (OSB) mill near Allendale, S.C., for approximately $280 million. The company plans to invest an additional $70 million to upgrade and optimize the facility, which has been idle since late 2019, expecting it to employ about 135 people and become one of its lowest-cost OSB mills. This acquisition leverages West Fraser's expertise in restarting idled mills and aims to enhance its OSB portfolio in the U.S. South, allowing for greater flexibility to meet customer demand.

title: Semiconductor shortage has Philip Morris shifting sales strategy for its heated-tobacco devices
summary: Philip Morris International is re-prioritizing its sales strategy for heated tobacco products, focusing on existing users due to device component constraints caused by the global semiconductor shortage. This shift is limiting product availability and forcing missed sales in certain markets, as demand for its IQOS device continues to grow but supply cannot keep up. The company aims for smoke-free products to comprise the majority of its sales by 2025, but achieving this goal will require an increase in semiconductor chip supply for device manufacturing.

title: Tasty! When is Chipotle Opening In Forked River, NJ?
summary: The article discusses the upcoming opening of a Chipotle restaurant in the Home Depot Plaza in Lacey Township (Forked River), NJ, which has been highly anticipated by locals. The author expresses excitement for the new establishment, highlighting Chipotle's menu and its commitment to real ingredients and sustainable practices. Despite a nearby Taco Bell, the author believes Chipotle will be a success in the area, which has also seen recent additions like Starbucks.

title: Mike Amend
summary: Mike Amend is the Chief Enterprise Technology Officer at Ford, reporting to Jim Farley. In this role, he leads Ford's Enterprise Technology Organization, focusing on data, software, and technology to drive growth and value. Amend previously held significant roles at Lowe's, JCPenney, and The Home Depot, where he was instrumental in growing their online businesses.

title: Monmouth REIT shareholder revolt leads to $4B sale, $600M better than before
summary: Monmouth Real Estate Investment Corp. has agreed to be acquired by Industrial Logistics Properties Trust for $4 billion after shareholders rejected an earlier, lower bid from Sam Zell's Equity Commonwealth. The all-cash deal, valued at $21 per share, is approximately $600 million higher than the previous offer and has been welcomed by activist investor Blackwells Capital. This acquisition will significantly expand Industrial Logistics Property Trust's mainland portfolio, building on Monmouth REIT's success in industrial properties.

title: From groundskeeper to CEO, Matt Missad leads UFP Industries on a profitable hunt for growth
summary: Matt Missad, CEO of UFP Industries, has led the company on an aggressive M&A strategy, completing 31 acquisitions in the past five years. UFP Industries, a wood products manufacturer with global operations, prioritizes M&A over organic growth and has developed an effective in-house M&A team. The company's diversification and unique approach to acquisitions have helped it navigate challenging markets, including the volatile lumber industry during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Sunbelt Investment Buys 205,000-Square-Foot Home Depot Superstore in Metro Los Angeles
summary: Sunbelt Investment Holdings has acquired a 205,000-square-foot Home Depot Superstore in Anaheim Hills, California. This flagship store, located on 18 acres near Interstate 91, is the largest Home Depot on the West Coast and the second largest in the nation. The purchase price was not disclosed.

title: Largest Home Depot on West Coast sells for $53 million
summary: Sunbelt Investment Holdings has acquired the Home Depot Superstore in Anaheim Hills, California, for $53 million. This particular Home Depot is noted as the largest on the West Coast and the second largest nationwide. With this purchase, Sunbelt Investment Holdings now owns a total of four Home Depot locations.

title: Robots check inventory at Busy Beaver store
summary: Busy Beaver Building Centers has launched a pilot program with Badger Technologies to deploy autonomous robots for inventory management at its Irwin, Pennsylvania store. These robots will monitor on-shelf product availability and verify prices for over 30,000 SKUs, freeing up associates to assist customers and improving efficiency. The initiative aims to enhance customer service and combat revenue loss due to inventory and pricing inaccuracies, building on other technology deployments by Busy Beaver.

title: Fire erupts at Home Depot in Park City, chemicals a concern
summary: A fire broke out at a Home Depot holding facility in Park City, Utah, prompting a response from fire crews who had concerns about chemicals on site. The blaze was quickly contained to the facility, and luckily, no injuries or major traffic disruptions were reported. Authorities are currently investigating the cause of the fire while cleanup efforts are underway.

title: Fire at Home Depot in Park City under investigation
summary: A fire broke out on the roof of a Home Depot in Park City, Utah, early Monday morning. Flames were visible around 4:30 a.m. and were extinguished by 6:30 a.m. The cause of the fire is currently under investigation, and no injuries were reported.

title: Home Depot Sales Gain Shows Americans Keep Fixing Up Houses
summary: Home Depot Inc. reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter results, with comparable-store sales increasing by 6.1%, significantly surpassing analyst estimates. This performance indicates sustained consumer spending on home improvement, driven by the strong U.S. housing market and the company's ability to navigate supply chain issues and inflation by passing costs to consumers. While sales transactions were down, a higher average ticket size, likely due to increased professional spending, contributed to the revenue gain.

title: Home Depot sales increase, signaling company could avoid effects of supply chain issues
summary: Home Depot reported better-than-expected earnings for its latest quarter, with comparable store sales increasing by 6.1% from July to October. The company's total sales reached $36.82 billion, up 9.8% year over year, demonstrating its ability to navigate supply-chain challenges by chartering its own container ships. Despite a slowdown in growth compared to earlier in the pandemic, strengthened by consumer spending on home improvements and stimulus checks, Home Depot's profits rose significantly, surpassing Wall Street analyst forecasts.

title: Walmart says it's ready for holidays — but hasn't yet seen huge wave of early shoppers
summary: Walmart CFO Brett Biggs stated that while the company is prepared for the holiday season with increased inventory, it has not yet observed a significant surge of early holiday shoppers, unlike competitors Amazon and Target who began promotions in October. Walmart strategically delayed its major holiday sales until November, focusing on strong grocery sales in Q3. Analysts believe Walmart's robust inventory and large store footprint position it well to navigate supply chain issues and meet customer demand during the holiday shopping period.

title: Home Depot Sales Rise, Continuing Pandemic Streak
summary: Home Depot reported better-than-expected quarterly results, with sales rising 9.8% year over year, demonstrating continued strong consumer demand for home-improvement products. The retailer has managed to improve profits despite supply-chain disruptions and rising input prices, showcasing resilience in challenging economic conditions. This performance indicates that some retailers are successfully navigating the current supply-chain issues impacting the economy.

title: Target CEO Brian Cornell’s Net Worth, Family, and Political Beliefs
summary: This article details the net worth, family life, and political beliefs of Target's Chairman and CEO, Brian Cornell. It highlights his professional career, including his turnaround efforts at Target, and mentions his estimated net worth of $80 million and his 2020 compensation of $19.8 million. The piece also touches on his liberal views and his advocacy for diversity and inclusion, particularly after George Floyd's murder.

title: Thanksgiving, Black Friday store hours: What's open, closed in Twin Cities
summary: This article provides a list of store hours for Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday in the Twin Cities, detailing which retailers will be open or closed. Due to the ongoing pandemic, many retailers have adjusted their hours, and the list includes specific opening and closing times for various stores on both days. The information is compiled to help shoppers plan their trips during the holiday season.

title: The Home Depot to Hold Virtual Career Day with Hundreds of Corporate and Technology Positions Available
summary: The Home Depot is hosting its first-ever virtual Corporate Career Day on Tuesday, Nov. 30, from 1 to 4:30 p.m. ET, to fill hundreds of corporate and technology positions. The event will offer jobseekers insights into various open roles, discussions with leaders on topics like retail technology and company culture, and networking opportunities with hiring teams. The Home Depot aims to highlight its long-lasting career potential, competitive culture, and comprehensive benefits package.

title: The Home Depot Declares Third Quarter Dividend of $1.65
summary: The Home Depot announced that its board of directors declared a third-quarter cash dividend of $1.65 per share. This dividend is payable on December 16, 2021, to shareholders of record as of December 2, 2021, marking the company's 139th consecutive quarterly cash dividend payment. The Home Depot operates 2,317 retail stores globally and reported sales of $132.1 billion and earnings of $12.9 billion in fiscal 2020.

title: Best Buy shares tumble on theft, supply constraints
summary: Best Buy's shares dropped significantly after the company reported a decline in gross profit margin for the fiscal third quarter, attributing it to organized theft and increased promotions. The consumer electronics chain also provided a subdued sales forecast for the crucial holiday fourth quarter, citing ongoing supply constraints. Despite beating Wall Street's overall third-quarter estimates, the issues of rising retail crime, especially in areas like San Francisco, and a slowdown in computing sales negatively impacted investor confidence.

title: Four Arrests in Beverly Hills May Be Related to Lakewood Home Depot Theft
summary: Four individuals were arrested in Beverly Hills, suspected of being involved in a "flash mob" theft of over $400 in merchandise from a Home Depot in Lakewood. The police are investigating to confirm the suspects' involvement and explore links to other recent smash-and-grab robberies across Los Angeles County. This incident is part of a growing trend of retail crimes in the region, particularly leading up to the holiday shopping season.

title: Get 25% off appliances during The Home Depot’s Black Friday sale of 2021
summary: The Home Depot's Black Friday 2021 sale offers up to 25% off appliances and savings up to $750, running until December 1st. The article highlights 20 specific deals across refrigerators, ranges, wall ovens, and microwaves, featuring brands like Samsung, LG, Frigidaire, and more. This sale presents an opportunity for customers to upgrade their home appliances at a discount.

title: The Home Depot Canada Foundation kick starts The Orange Door Project fundraising campaign on Giving Tuesday with more than $400,000 donation
summary: The Home Depot Canada Foundation launched its annual Orange Door Project holiday fundraising campaign on Giving Tuesday with a donation of over $400,000. Customer donations will support 124 Canadian charities focused on preventing and ending youth homelessness, with 100% of proceeds staying in local communities. The campaign runs until December 19th and highlights the urgent need to address youth homelessness exacerbated by the pandemic.

title: Stores Like Home Depot and Best Buy Bolster Security After ‘Flash Mob’ Robberies
summary: Retailers like Home Depot and Best Buy are increasing security measures due to a surge in "flash mob" robberies, particularly during the holiday shopping season. These incidents, involving large groups stealing merchandise, have seen a significant increase in intensity and organization during the pandemic. Law enforcement and retailers are collaborating to combat these organized crime activities across the country.

title: Burlington Stores, Five Below accelerate growth plans despite supply chain issues
summary: Burlington Stores and Five Below are accelerating their growth plans despite ongoing global supply chain issues. Both retailers have reported strong sales and demonstrated an ability to effectively manage the challenges posed by supply chain disruptions. This indicates their resilience and strategic planning in a challenging economic environment.

title: 3 arrested in Tigard in multi-state Home Depot theft ring
summary: Police in Tigard, Oregon, arrested three men suspected of being part of a multi-state retail theft ring targeting Home Depot stores. The men, Toni Rivera, Fredi Rivera, and Efrain Martin Jr., are believed to have stolen approximately $100,000 worth of goods, including electrical wire and tools, from stores in California, Oregon, and Washington. They were charged with aggravated theft and felon in possession of a weapon after being found with three guns, suspected narcotics, and about $40,000 in stolen property.

title: 3 arrested in Beaverton, accused in string of Home Depot thefts
summary: Three people have been arrested in Beaverton, accused of being part of an organized retail theft ring targeting Home Depot stores along the West Coast. The suspects are believed to be responsible for approximately $100,000 in losses in California and additional thefts in Washington. During the arrest, police recovered three guns, suspected narcotics, and an estimated $40,000 in stolen property, with all three facing charges of aggravated theft and felon in possession of a weapon.

title: Walgreens, CVS, Home Depot among 20 major companies urging Congress to take action on illegal retail sales online
summary: Twenty major companies, including Walgreens, CVS, and Home Depot, are urging Congress to pass the bipartisan Inform Consumers Act to combat rising retail theft. This bill aims to require online sellers to provide basic business information, making it harder for criminals to sell stolen goods. The companies believe this measure will deter organized retail crime by targeting the large syndicates profiting from stolen merchandise.

title: The Home Depot Foundation Commits Up to $1 Million to Communities Devastated by Tornado Outbreak
summary: The Home Depot Foundation is committing up to $1 million to support immediate disaster relief and long-term recovery efforts in communities affected by the recent tornado outbreak in the central United States. This new grant brings the Foundation's 2021 disaster commitment to over $7 million. The Home Depot and its Foundation are working with nonprofit partners and volunteers to distribute essential supplies, provide shelter, and offer financial support to impacted associates.

title: Western Auto Museum is a step back in time
summary: The newly established Western Auto Museum in Georgetown, Delaware, showcases the lifelong collection of Maurice Sanger, a former Western Auto store owner. The museum, located at the Nutter Marvel Carriage Museum, offers a nostalgic look at the retail chain which provided auto supplies, hardware, and various household goods before the rise of modern superstores. It features thousands of items, including rare Western Flyer merchandise, vintage auto parts, toys, and historical documents.

title: Brixton Capital Divests of Rainbow Plaza Shopping Center in Las Vegas for $63.7 Million
summary: Brixton Capital has sold the Rainbow Plaza shopping center in Las Vegas for $63.7 million to an undisclosed buyer. The 259,980-square-foot center, anchored by Albertsons and other major retailers, was 94 percent occupied at the time of sale. Rob Ippolito of Newmark represented Brixton Capital in the transaction.

title: Sebastian Home Depot Donates $1,000 to Team Success Enterprises to Help Family
summary: The Home Depot in Sebastian donated $1,000 to Team Success Enterprises to assist a local family who unexpectedly lost their father. The funds will be used to buy Christmas gifts for the family's two children, with any remaining money going to other families in need in the north county area. The initiative was prompted by the Sebastian Police Department's C.O.P.E. unit after they learned of the family's financial struggles.

title: Four traders weigh in on the homebuilder weakness after week of sell-offs
summary: The homebuilder sector experienced its worst week since October 2020, despite strong underlying housing data. While some analysts are concerned about short-term pullbacks due to technical indicators and potential Fed interest rate hikes, others remain optimistic, citing strong housing demand, low inventory, and millennial homeownership trends as counteracting factors. Traders suggest careful investment, with some favoring specific builders like Toll Brothers and major players such as Home Depot and Lowe's.

title: Former Home Depot CEO says inflation presenting a pricing, cost issue never experienced by companies
summary: Former Home Depot and Chrysler CEO Bob Nardelli stated that current inflation presents an unprecedented pricing and cost issue for companies, making 2022 look "tough." He noted that businesses are forced to pass higher costs onto consumers due to surging prices for groceries, cars, and gasoline, with the consumer price index rising 6.8% in November. Nardelli also highlighted that a shortage of workers is contributing to increased labor costs, further exacerbating the challenges for both large and small companies.

title: 2 arrested for allegedly stealing over $24K from Utah Home Depots
summary: Two men, Luis Vargas-Alfaro and Felipe Elgueta-Gasca, were arrested in Lindon, Utah, for allegedly stealing over $24,000 worth of products from multiple Home Depot locations across the state. They were caught attempting to steal electrical wire and other items from a Lindon store and admitted to police that they traveled from California to sell the stolen merchandise. Both suspects were booked into Utah County Jail facing potential charges of theft and pattern of unlawful activity.

title: Home Depot class action over retirement mismanagement dismissed
summary: A federal judge dismissed a class action lawsuit against Home Depot, which alleged that the company mismanaged employees' retirement savings through poor investments. The judge ruled there was no evidence that Home Depot's actions caused losses, also rejecting a recusal bid due to his prior role with the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. The U.S. Chamber of Commerce had supported Home Depot, arguing the claims were based on an overly expansive view of ERISA.

title: The Home Depot Expands Everyday Military Discount Benefit for All Veterans
summary: The Home Depot has expanded its military discount program to include all U.S. veterans, active service members, and their spouses, offering a 10 percent discount on in-store and online purchases after app registration. This initiative reinforces the company's commitment to the military community, building on The Home Depot Foundation's significant investments in veteran causes and housing improvements. The Home Depot also maintains its strong support for veterans and military spouses within its workforce, having been recognized as a Military Friendly® company for 19 consecutive years.

title: In Depth: The Building Envelope
summary: This article discusses the critical role of building envelope products in construction, highlighting their essential function in protecting structures from the elements. It delves into the current market trends, including sustained growth despite supply chain challenges, and emphasizes the importance of product availability, performance, and innovation. The piece also addresses how material and labor shortages are impacting the industry and stresses the need for strong communication and strategic planning between LBM dealers and manufacturers to navigate these issues successfully.

title: Nasdaq Dorsey Wright Year End Review and What to Watch for in 2022
summary: Nasdaq Dorsey Wright's Head of Research and Senior Portfolio Manager review 2021 market trends and offer insights for 2022, focusing on technical analysis, relative strength investing, and the firm's point and figure methodology. They discuss seasonal market patterns, the S&P 500's uptrend, and the Dynamic Asset Level Investing (DALI) model for asset and sector allocation. The article also examines the influence of the U.S. dollar and the fixed income market outlook.

title: The Home Depot Introduces New and Enhanced Credit Options for Pro Customers
summary: The Home Depot has introduced new and enhanced credit options for Pro Customers, including The Pro Xtra Credit Card and updates to its Commercial Account Card. Powered by Citi Retail Services, these options offer features like linking to the Pro Xtra loyalty program for faster perks, extended return periods, and online account management. The initiative aims to help Pro Customers save time and money while streamlining their shopping and billing processes.

title: Home Depot (HD) to Boost Pro Experience With New Credit Scheme
summary: Home Depot is launching a new credit scheme, The Pro Xtra Credit Card, to enhance the experience for its Pro customers. This initiative, powered by Citi Retail Services, aims to save Pro customers time and money by offering perks like faster earnings on loyalty points and a $100 credit for new card registrations. The move reinforces Home Depot's focus on its growing Pro segment, which has been a key driver of sales growth and overall company performance.

title: How retailers can meet consumers’ growing demand for sustainability and hybrid shopping experiences
summary: A new global study from IBM IBV and NRF reveals that consumer preferences have shifted significantly, with a growing demand for hybrid shopping experiences and sustainability. Retailers must adapt by offering personalized experiences, transparent supply chains, and agile operations, leveraging technologies like AI and hybrid cloud. While consumers express a willingness to pay more for sustainable products, there's still a gap between their intentions and actual purchasing behavior, which can be addressed through greater transparency.

title: The Home Depot signs on for warehouse at Charlotte industrial project
summary: The Home Depot is developing a new 403,000-square-foot, rail-served warehouse in southwest Charlotte. The facility will be built on a nearly 80-acre site on Sam Neely Road, acquired by The Keith Corp. last year for industrial development.

title: New projects light the spark of redevelopment in long-neglected area of Pinellas County
summary: Two new development projects featuring national retailers Sprouts Farmers Market, At Home, and Catapult Adventure Parks are set to revitalize a long-neglected area of Pinellas County along 66th Street N. These developments mark a significant redevelopment effort, bringing new commercial and entertainment options to the community.

title: Multiple Home Depot thieves nabbed amid wave of organized retail crime
summary: Several thieves targeting Home Depot stores have been arrested amidst a rising tide of organized retail crime. One former pawn shop owner admitted to selling over $3.2 million in stolen goods from major retailers, including Home Depot, between 2017 and 2019. In response to these incidents, Home Depot is increasing security investments and implementing new technologies like product activation to combat theft, which costs retailers an average of $719,548 per $1 billion in sales.

title: Home Depot names new CEO, Craig Menear to remain chairman
summary: Home Depot announced that Ted Decker will become its new chief executive and president, effective March 1. Decker will also join the company's board of directors. Current CEO and Chairman Craig Menear will transition to remain as chairman of the board. Home Depot's shares rose 2% in extended trading after the announcement.

title: Home Depot names Ted Decker CEO, Craig Menear to remain chairman
summary: The Home Depot Inc. has appointed Ted Decker as its new CEO. Craig Menear will continue to serve as chairman. This leadership change comes as Home Depot is experiencing a surge in business due to increased homebuilding and renovations.

title: Home Depot picks veteran Ted Decker as new CEO
summary: Home Depot has appointed Edward "Ted" Decker, a 22-year company veteran, as its new Chief Executive Officer and President, succeeding Craig Menear. Decker, who previously served as Chief Operating Officer, will assume the role on March 1. The change comes amidst a surge in demand for home improvement projects.

title: Home Depot picks veteran Ted Decker as new CEO
summary: Home Depot Inc. has appointed Edward "Ted" Decker as its new chief executive officer and president, effective March 1, 2022. Decker, a 22-year company veteran and former chief operating officer, will replace Craig Menear, who will remain as chairman. The company has recently experienced increased demand from contractors for home improvement projects previously delayed due to the COVID-19 crisis.

title: Home Depot names longtime executive as new CEO
summary: The Home Depot has appointed Edward "Ted" Decker, its chief operating officer since October 2020, as its new President and CEO, effective March 1. Current Chairman and CEO Craig Menear will remain the company's board chairman. Decker, 58, joined Home Depot in 2000 and has held various roles in finance, business development, and merchandising, with Menear expressing confidence in his leadership to guide the company's future growth.

title: Home Depot Appoints Company Veteran as CEO
summary: The Home Depot has appointed Edward “Ted” Decker as its new CEO and President, effective March 1, 2022. Decker, a 22-year veteran of the company, previously served as President and COO. Current CEO Craig Menear will transition to Chair of the Board.

title: Home Depot names Ted Decker CEO
summary: The Home Depot has appointed Ted Decker as its new CEO, effective March 1, succeeding Craig Menear who will remain chairman of the board. Decker, currently the retailer's chief operating officer, has been with Home Depot since 2000 and held various leadership roles. Analysts expect a seamless transition as Decker was integral to the company's "One Home Depot" strategy, which has seen strong sales growth.

title: 2022 Industry Pulse Report
summary: The 2022 Window + Door Industry Pulse survey reveals that the market is strong and business is booming, despite persistent supply chain and labor challenges. Key concerns include staffing, material availability, and lead times, while increased sales and a strong housing market present opportunities. Companies are prioritizing investments in operational efficiency, employee recruitment, and retention, and expect sales to continue growing.

title: Sam’s Club rolls out inventory-checking robots chainwide
summary: Sam's Club is deploying robotic inventory-analysis equipment, powered by Brain Corp software, to all nearly 600 U.S. locations. This technology, mounted on existing autonomous floor-cleaning machines, scans shelves for pricing accuracy, stock levels, and item placement, providing real-time inventory reports to store managers. The move aims to improve efficiency and free up associates for member interaction, aligning with retailers' increasing use of automation to address labor challenges.

title: Home Depot’s Menear to Transition to Chairman, Realized Nearly $200 Million
summary: The Home Depot, Inc. announced that CEO Craig A. Menear will transition to Chairman of the Board effective March 1, 2022. Mr. Menear realized nearly $200 million in total compensation between 2014 and 2020. Edward P. Decker, the current President and COO, will assume the CEO role on the same date.

title: Walmart Makes a Move to Challenge Home Depot and Lowe's
summary: Walmart is partnering with Angi to offer home improvement services online and in-store, directly challenging competitors like Home Depot and Lowe's. This collaboration allows Walmart customers to access a wide range of professional services, backed by Angi's network of over 250,000 professionals and a "Happiness Guarantee." The move aims to expand Walmart's service offerings and attract a new customer base, mirroring similar services provided by its rivals in the home improvement sector.

title: Home Depot launches training program to support construction industry
summary: Home Depot has launched a free job-training program called "Path to Pro" to address the significant labor shortage in the construction industry. The program offers self-paced training focused on basic construction skills, job site safety, and soft skills, aiming to connect qualified candidates with potential employers through its "Path to Pro network." This initiative seeks to rebuild interest in construction careers and fill the labor gap with entry-level workers.

title: Home Depot Plans to Boost Spring Hiring 25% With Quicker Job Offers
summary: Home Depot Inc. announced plans to increase its spring season hiring by 25% despite a tight labor market for retailers. To achieve this, the company has expedited its application process, aiming to make job offers within a day of receiving an application, a significant reduction from the previous five-day waiting period.

title: Home Depot stepping up spring hiring to 100,000 workers
summary: Home Depot announced plans to hire over 100,000 workers for the upcoming spring selling season, an increase from its typical 80,000 hires. This move aims to meet the anticipated peak demand for home-improvement products during this period, especially as consumers continue to invest in their homes following the COVID-19 pandemic. The company is seeking both full-time and part-time employees across various roles and will host a virtual career day.

title: Home Depot plans to hire over 100K workers ahead of spring season
summary: Home Depot announced plans to hire over 100,000 workers for the upcoming spring season, exceeding its usual 80,000 hires for the period. The roles will span customer services, sales, store support, freight, merchandising, and warehouse associates across stores and warehouses. The retailer has introduced a new hiring process allowing applicants to receive job offers within one day and will host a virtual hiring event on February 16 to connect jobseekers with opportunities and provide information on career growth.

title: The Home Depot is Hiring More Than 100,000 Associates
summary: The Home Depot is hiring over 100,000 new associates for its busy spring season, with various flexible, full-time, and part-time positions available across its stores and warehouses nationwide. The company will host a Virtual Spring Career Day on February 16, 2022, to connect jobseekers with leaders, discuss growth opportunities, and highlight benefits and upskilling programs. The Home Depot emphasizes its commitment to investing in its associates through bonuses, career development, and extensive benefits.

title: Labor shortage has Home Depot pushing 'accelerated hiring process'
summary: Home Depot has launched an "accelerated hiring process" to combat ongoing labor shortages, aiming to offer jobs within a day to prospective applicants. The company plans to hire over 100,000 associates for various positions ahead of its busy spring season, emphasizing competitive benefits and a 401(k) savings plan. This initiative comes as over 4 million Americans quit their jobs in December and job openings remain elevated.

title: Home Depot Names New CEO
summary: The Home Depot has named Edward "Ted" Decker as its new CEO and president, effective March 1, 2022. Decker, who has been with the company for 22 years and previously served as president and chief operating officer, will also join the company's board of directors. Current Chairman and CEO Craig Menear will continue as chair of the board.

title: Crunched for Workers? It’s Time to Consider Rapid Hiring
summary: During a labor shortage, companies like Home Depot are adopting rapid hiring strategies to fill numerous open roles quickly, aiming to onboard 100,000 new employees with job offers made within a day. This approach often involves leveraging AI-powered tools that streamline the application process, allowing businesses to schedule interviews and extend offers rapidly. While technology plays a key role, businesses also utilize virtual career events to support their hiring pushes.

title: Home Depot Worker Swapped $387,500 in Fake Bills for Real Ones, Officials Say (Published 2022)
summary: A Home Depot vault associate, Adrian Jean Pineda, was charged by the U.S. Secret Service for allegedly swapping $387,500 in fake "PLAYMONEY" prop bills for genuine currency over four years in a Tempe, Arizona store. The scheme was uncovered when Wells Fargo Bank identified the counterfeit bills in store deposits, leading Home Depot to contact the Secret Service in December. Pineda reportedly admitted to the scheme when confronted by a store manager.

title: Ashby: Costco in talks for new store in Natomas off I-5
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp. is reportedly planning a new store in Natomas, California, according to a Sacramento City Councilmember. The article, by Ben van der Meer, details the development without providing further specifics on the timeline or location beyond "off I-5". This news follows previous related reports concerning Costco's logistics and other store developments in the wider Sacramento area.

title: Selling out: What retail leaders need to know before striking a deal with private equity
summary: The article discusses the risks associated with private equity buyouts in the retail sector, highlighting that over 40% of such acquisitions have historically led to bankruptcy. It uses Kohl's recent consideration of bids and the case of Jones Group (Nine West) to illustrate how leveraged buyouts, often financed with significant debt, can lead to financial distress, disinvestment, and ultimately, insolvency for the acquired companies. The author stresses the importance for retail leaders to conduct thorough due diligence regarding solvency before entering private equity deals.

title: Home Depot's 48 hour return policy leads to dishwasher debacle in Cheektowaga
summary: A woman in Cheektowaga purchased a new dishwasher from Home Depot, but it never worked correctly, collecting water and not drying dishes. After attempts to fix it through the warranty and initial difficulties with Home Depot's customer service, the issue was brought to "7 Problem Solvers." As a result, Home Depot contacted the customer to offer a full refund for the defective appliance.

title: The Untold Truth Of Home Depot
summary: This article delves into various lesser-known aspects of Home Depot's history and operations, covering its consistent profitability despite market fluctuations, its unexpected viral presence on social media, past controversies including destroying hurricane relief supplies and a wrongful termination, and its founders' origins. It also highlights the company's commitment to community through its foundation's trade training programs and its unique history of employing Olympic athletes, alongside some unusual items it sells.

title: Yeti is leaving Lowe’s to focus on DTC and key wholesale accounts
summary: Yeti has ended its two-year partnership with Lowe's to prioritize direct-to-consumer (DTC) sales and key wholesale accounts, citing supply chain disruptions and an "optimization" strategy. This move aligns with Yeti's expanding DTC sales, which now account for 60% of its revenue, and its focus on strengthening relationships with core wholesale partners like Dick's, Bass Pro, and REI. Many industry commentators suggest this decision was a strategic move to improve margins and control brand perception, given Yeti's premium positioning.

title: Inside the $644 billion business of reselling returned items, from electronics to bizarre finds
summary: The liquidation market, which resells returned goods, has grown into a $644 billion industry due to the increasing volume of returns, particularly from online shopping. This sector offers a solution for retailers facing significant costs and environmental impact from returns, with companies like Liquidity Services and B-Stock Solutions specializing in reselling everything from electronics to unusual items. The boom in liquidation is also fueled by growing consumer demand for sustainable and secondhand goods, leading to the rise of direct-to-consumer liquidation stores and refurbished item marketplaces.

title: Cooling home improvement demand may pressure Home Depot, Lowe's 2022 sales
summary: Home Depot Inc and Lowe's Cos Inc are expected to forecast a slowdown in 2022 sales due to a cooling U.S. housing market, rising inflation, and easing COVID-11 fears. This comes after two years of robust pandemic-driven demand, with analysts projecting modest sales growth for both companies this fiscal year. Investors will also be watching the impact of cost inflation and supply-chain issues on profit margins.

title: Home Depot sales reach record $150 billion but shares tumble as high inflation and lower demand expected to take a toll
summary: Home Depot reported record sales of $150 billion in 2021, yet its stock fell sharply by nearly 9% on Tuesday, dragging down other home improvement stocks. While the company beat quarterly profit and sales expectations and raised its dividend, investor concerns about high inflation and an anticipated decline in demand post-pandemic are weighing on the shares.

title: Home Depot's margin warning casts shadow on solid quarter
summary: Home Depot's shares tumbled after the company warned that gross profit margins would remain under pressure through the year due to aggressive spending on supply-chain issues. Despite exceeding fourth-quarter sales and earnings estimates, the outlook for flat operating margins in 2022 and potential cooling of home improvement sales concerned investors. The company is incurring costs by chartering its own cargo ships and using air freight to mitigate supply chain disruptions.

title: The Home Depot Announces Fourth Quarter and Fiscal 2021 Results; Increases Quarterly Dividend by 15 Percent; Provides Fiscal 2022 Guidance
summary: The Home Depot announced strong financial results for the fourth quarter and fiscal year 2021, with significant increases in sales and net earnings. The company also declared a 15 percent increase in its quarterly dividend and provided fiscal 2022 guidance, anticipating slightly positive sales growth and low single-digit diluted earnings-per-share growth. These results highlight a record year for The Home Depot, exceeding $150 billion in sales.

title: Tractor Supply Co. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
summary: Tractor Supply Co. (TSCO) stock declined by 6.45% on Tuesday, closing at $200.36, amidst a broad market downturn. This performance saw the company underperform compared to major market indexes like the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average, and also in relation to some of its competitors such as Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), Home Depot Inc. (HD), and Lowe's Cos. (LOW). The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high, with trading volume exceeding its 50-day average.

title: Home Depot on South Columbus Boulevard in South Philadelphia catches fire
summary: A fire broke out at a Home Depot store in South Philadelphia on South Columbus Boulevard. Firefighters responded around 1 a.m. and brought the blaze, primarily located in the outdoor garden center, under control in 15 minutes. No injuries were reported, and the cause of the fire is currently unknown.

title: Home Depot, Lowe’s sales lap pandemic highs
summary: Home Depot and Lowe's both reported strong sales gains in the fourth quarter, outperforming pandemic highs, as consumers invested in their homes during the holidays. Home Depot's net sales increased 10.7% to $35.7 billion, while Lowe's saw a 5% increase to $21.3 billion. Analysts note Home Depot's focus on professional customers helped it gain market share against Lowe's, despite both retailers exhibiting significant growth.

title: Lowe's optimistic on home improvement demand despite rising interest rates
summary: Lowe's raised its full-year sales and profit forecasts, expressing optimism about continued home improvement demand in the United States, even as mortgage rates increase. The company believes that the ongoing trend of millennials purchasing suburban homes and extended remote work policies will sustain strong demand for home upgrade projects. This outlook comes despite a recent rise in 30-year fixed mortgage rates above 4% for the first time since 2019.

title: The Home Depot Names Paula Santilli and Caryn Seidman-Becker to its Board of Directors
summary: The Home Depot announced the appointment of Paula Santilli, CEO of PepsiCo Latin America, and Caryn Seidman-Becker, chair and CEO of CLEAR, to its board of directors, effective March 1, 2022. These additions will bring the total number of directors to 14. Both new board members bring extensive experience in retail, technology, international operations, and financial management.

title: Big Box Retailers Target Professional Business
summary: Lowe's and Home Depot, traditionally focusing on DIY consumers, are now strategically targeting professional contractors through specialized programs. Lowe's launched its MVPs Rewards and Partnership Program offering loyalty benefits and business resources, while Home Depot reacquired HD Supply Holdings Inc. to better serve professionals. This shift is driven by a consumer trend away from DIY projects and a growing demand for professional home improvement services, particularly in energy-efficient upgrades.

title: Turn your patio into a spa with up to $1,750 off hot tubs and saunas at Home Depot
summary: The Home Depot is offering significant discounts, up to $1,750 off, on hot tubs and saunas, allowing customers to transform their backyards into spa-like retreats. The sale includes various models of Lifesmart jacuzzis with features like ozone water care and LED lights, as well as Maxxus infrared saunas equipped with Bluetooth sound systems and chromotherapy. The article encourages readers to take advantage of these deals to enhance their home relaxation options.

title: The Home Depot Adds Workshops for Pros to Roster of Livestreams
summary: The Home Depot is launching a new series of free virtual workshops tailored for Pro contractors to help them manage and grow their businesses. These interactive livestreams, held every other month, will cover topics such as business cash flow management, social media for business, and industry trends. The initiative expands on Home Depot's existing workshop programs for DIYers and complements its Pro Xtra loyalty program.

title: Business Licenses – March 2022
summary: This article lists new business licenses issued in the Tri-Cities area for March 2022, categorized by city: Kennewick, Prosser, and West Richland. Each entry includes the business name, and in most cases, an address. The licenses cover a wide array of industries from construction and landscaping to retail, healthcare, and consulting services.

title: Fire Breaks Out At Home Depot In Riverhead
summary: A fire broke out at the Home Depot in Riverhead, NY, on Monday, March 21, 2022. The fire reportedly started with chairs outside the building and spread to the exterior, causing visible damage. Authorities are investigating, but the fire appears to be non-criminal, and no injuries were reported.

title: Best Composite Decking From Consumer Reports’ Tests
summary: Consumer Reports evaluated composite decking from various manufacturers like Azek, Fiberon, TimberTech, and Trex. The article highlights that composite decking offers advantages over wood, such as lower maintenance, and the price gap with natural wood has narrowed. CR's tests focused on durability, stain resistance, slip resistance, and the effects of extreme climates, finding that while most composite options resist stains well, some perform poorly in terms of slip, flexing, and sag resistance.

title: Dillard’s Said to be in Talks for Plaza Nordstrom Site
summary: Dillard's is reportedly in negotiations to take over the previously planned Nordstrom site at the Country Club Plaza in Kansas City, following two years of stalled progress on the Nordstrom development. While Nordstrom's proposed opening has been delayed multiple times, industry sources believe a Fall 2023 completion is unrealistic. Dillard's, which caters to a middle and upper-middle-class market and has financially outperformed rivals during the pandemic, would fill a department store vacancy that has existed since 2014.

title: The Home Depot Canada Foundation surpasses $50 million in support of youth experiencing homelessness
summary: The Home Depot Canada Foundation has exceeded its goal, investing over $50 million since 2013 to combat youth homelessness in Canada. This milestone was achieved through community giving campaigns, including The Orange Door Project, and additional grants to charity partners. Despite this success, the Foundation highlights the ongoing need for action as youth still represent a significant portion of Canada's homeless population and plans to announce the next phase of its investment.

title: Experts Details: Lillian Currens
summary: This page provides details about Lillian Currens, the deputy editor at Schaeffer's Investment Research. It highlights her professional background, experience in writing and editing digital content, and her role in managing Schaeffer's social media. The article also lists several of her published articles discussing stock analyses for companies like Netflix, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Nvidia, and Home Depot.

title: Home Depot Faces Class Action Alleging Failure to Pay Wages for Off the Clock Work
summary: A class-action lawsuit filed in California alleges that Home Depot failed to pay employees for all hours worked and denied appropriate meal and rest breaks. The suit claims Home Depot's policy of rounding down clock-in/out times and requiring employees to remain on premises after clocking out results in unpaid wages, violating California Labor Code. The plaintiffs seek compensation for unpaid minimum wage and overtime hours.

title: Customers, Nearby Residents Speak Out Following Massive San Jose Home Depot Fire
summary: Customers and residents in South San Jose describe their harrowing experiences during and after a massive Home Depot fire. The fire started in the lumber section, prompting a chaotic evacuation and raising questions about the store's fire suppression systems. While the fire department believes sprinklers mostly worked, the intense heat may have overwhelmed some, and investigators are still determining the exact cause.

title: Northern California Home Depot store destroyed in fire
summary: A five-alarm fire destroyed a Home Depot store in South San Jose, California, over the weekend, prompting a shelter-in-place order for nearby residents due to unhealthy air. The blaze, which reportedly started in the lumber section and fed on flammable materials, took approximately six hours to contain, with no injuries reported. Authorities are investigating the cause, and the incident occurred on the same day as another fire at the Port of Benicia.

title: Home Depot fire: San Jose crews continue to put out hot spots after massive weekend blaze destroys building
summary: Crews in San Jose are still working to extinguish flare-ups from a massive weekend fire that obliterated a Home Depot store. The blaze, which caused extensive damage to the building and merchandise, forced the evacuation of a neighboring veterinary hospital and pet campus. Nearby residents expressed devastation and gratitude towards the fire department for saving their homes from the intense inferno.

title: Pets at neighboring business Wagly rushed to safety during San Jose Home Depot fire
summary: During a five-alarm fire that destroyed a Home Depot in San Jose, pets at the neighboring Wagly veterinary hospital and pet campus were safely evacuated. Owners expressed relief and gratitude for the quick actions of the staff and first responders who ensured all animals were rescued, though some owners faced challenges in reuniting with their pets. The Wagly facility remains temporarily closed due to damage from the fire.

title: The Home Depot Foundation Teams Up With Operation Blessing to Prepare for Disaster Season
summary: The Home Depot Foundation is partnering with Operation Blessing to assemble nearly 800 disaster relief kits in anticipation of the upcoming disaster season. These kits, containing essential supplies, were put together by Team Depot volunteers and delivered to Operation Blessing's warehouse in Texas for quick deployment following severe weather events. This collaboration is part of the Foundation's ongoing commitment to disaster relief and recovery, and also contributes to their National Volunteer Month efforts.

title: Feds on the ground at San Jose Home Depot to assist in fire investigation
summary: The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) National Response Team is assisting the San Jose Fire Department in investigating the massive blaze that destroyed a Home Depot. Witnesses reported no immediate fire alarms or active sprinklers, raising questions about the store's safety systems. Despite the lack of alarms, employees are being credited for effectively evacuating all customers, with no injuries reported.

title: Home Depot or housing? Residents push back on proposal for giant Rockridge lot
summary: Residents and community groups in Rockridge are largely opposing a preliminary proposal to build a Home Depot with a large parking structure on a 15-acre vacant lot at Broadway and Pleasant Valley Avenue. Many had hoped for housing or independent shops instead, raising concerns about corporate "big-box" development, increased car traffic, and the potential impact on local hardware stores. The property's master lease, held by Terramar Retail Centers, reportedly prohibits residential development, despite community and city council interest in a mixed-use approach.

title: Suspect Identified in Massive Arson Fire at San Jose Home Depot
summary: Authorities have identified Dyllin Jaycruz Gogue, 27, as the suspect in a massive five-alarm arson fire that destroyed a San Jose Home Depot store earlier this month. Gogue was arrested and charged with felony aggravated arson and other crimes after allegedly setting the fire and attempting to steal merchandise. The incident also involved a shelter-in-place order and the evacuation of over 60 pets, with investigators looking into the cause and origin of the blaze, including the store's fire alarm and sprinkler system history.

title: Police ID Home Depot fire suspect
summary: Police have identified Dyllin Jaycruz Gogue, 27, as the suspect in connection with the April 9 Home Depot fire in San Jose. Gogue was charged with aggravated arson, grand theft, and petty theft, as he is accused of stealing from the burning store and later from an East Bay Macy’s. The fire, which destroyed the 11,000 square-foot building and caused $14 million in inventory losses, was determined to be arson, and Gogue is believed to be solely responsible.

title: The Home Depot Names Matt Carey EVP of Customer Experience; Fahim Siddiqui Named EVP and Chief Information Officer
summary: The Home Depot announced two key executive appointments: Matt Carey has been named EVP of Customer Experience, a newly created role focusing on enhancing seamless customer interactions across all platforms. Concurrently, Fahim Siddiqui has been appointed EVP and Chief Information Officer, responsible for the company's technology strategy and infrastructure. These appointments aim to further Home Depot's commitment to customer-centric technology innovation and an interconnected shopping experience.

title: San Jose Home Depot Fire: Neighbor's $5,000 backyard renovation for home daycare destroyed
summary: A San Jose neighbor, Sherrie Butts, had her recently renovated $5,000 backyard, intended for her home daycare, destroyed by the massive Home Depot fire. While grateful her home is still standing and that the fire occurred on a Saturday when children weren't present, she and others in the neighborhood are traumatized by the event. The suspect, Dyllin Jaycruz Gogue, has been charged with aggravated arson and theft, facing a potential 14 years to life in prison, as the fire was reportedly set as a diversion for stealing tools.

title: Home Depot looking to fill more than 300 positions in Columbus
summary: Home Depot is looking to hire more than 300 individuals for part-time and full-time positions in Columbus to prepare for the busy spring season. The company is offering an accelerated hiring process that can result in a job offer within a day of applying. Available positions include customer service/sales, store support, freight, merchandising, and warehouse associates.

title: Análisis Técnico de Acciones y CEDEARs
summary: This technical analysis report for April 21, 2022, identifies buying opportunities for Home Depot (NYSE: HD) and Grupo Financiero Galicia (BCBA: GGAL) based on their technical chart patterns and indicators. It also provides an in-depth analysis of the S&P Merval index in both pesos and CCL dollars, as well as the SPY ETF, highlighting key resistance, support levels, and market trends. The report offers investment recommendations for aggressive profiles, detailing price targets and stop-loss levels for featured stocks.

title: Behind the Scenes at the John Deere Horicon Works Factory
summary: Wayne Southall, a factory manager at John Deere's Horicon Works, discusses the company's journey in the riding lawn equipment market, including successes, challenges, and lessons learned over his 20-year career. The article highlights product development, such as the airless Tweel tire, the missteps with the SpinSteer mower, and how the company adapted to changes like the mass market entry and the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on supply chains. Southall emphasizes John Deere's continuous efforts to innovate and maintain flexibility in manufacturing.

title: Home Depot names company vet to CIO role
summary: Home Depot has announced the appointment of Matt Carey as the new executive vice president of customer experience and Fahim Siddiqui as the new executive vice president and chief information officer. Carey will lead strategies to enhance customer experience in stores and digital channels, while Siddiqui will manage digital strategy, infrastructure, and software development. Both promotions highlight Home Depot's focus on internal talent and technology to improve customer interaction and differentiate itself in the home improvement market.

title: Tractor Supply Makes the Case for Investing in BIPOC, LGBTQ and Women Farmers
summary: Tractor Supply Co. is increasing its focus on ESG initiatives, including reducing its carbon footprint and boosting diversity. Through its foundation, it partners with the American Farmland Trust to support small farmers, particularly women, BIPOC, and LGBTQ individuals, providing grants and aiming to improve their viability and resilience in the face of various challenges. This initiative addresses the struggles faced by these farmers, such as declining farm numbers, low-profit margins, and historical inequities.

title: The Home Depot Awards 30 HBCUs Retool Your School Campus Improvement Grants
summary: The Home Depot is investing an additional $1 million in its Retool Your School program, providing grants to 30 Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) for campus improvements. This marks the 13th year of the program, which has supported almost 70 percent of the nation's HBCUs with over 180 grants totaling more than $5 million since its launch in 2009. Alabama State University was awarded Campaign of the Year, alongside grants for the 30 winning institutions.

title: RBC, CIBC to lend Elon Musk $1.5 billion for Twitter takeover
summary: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC) have pledged a combined $1.5 billion to help finance Elon Musk's $56-billion bid to acquire Twitter. This contribution is part of a larger $32.5 billion financing package from 12 banks, with RBC providing $956.5 million and CIBC contributing $510 million. The article also touches on other recent financing deals, including increased investment by The Home Depot Canada Foundation for youth homelessness, funding for QuadFi to offer personal loans to underserved groups, and Mavrck's acquisition of Later.

title: Home Depot Canada Foundation Increases Investment To $125 Million In Support Of Youth Experiencing Homelessness
summary: The Home Depot Canada Foundation is increasing its investment to combat youth homelessness to $125 million by 2030, exceeding its initial $50 million pledge. This renewed commitment will focus on expanding stable housing, providing community support, and increasing youth employment readiness through various grants and strategic partnerships. The funding will emphasize an equity framework, significantly supporting organizations that assist underrepresented youth, and will also boost the TradeWorx program to provide skilled trades training.

title: The Home Depot Announces $150 Million Venture Capital Fund to Fuel Innovation in Retail and Home Improvement
summary: The Home Depot has launched Home Depot Ventures, a $150 million venture capital fund aimed at investing in early-stage companies to foster innovation in retail and home improvement. The fund will support technologies that enhance customer experience, improve associate efficiency, and drive operational excellence, building on the company's history of successful startup investments like Afero and Loadsmart. These investments are intended to create a seamless interconnected shopping experience and strengthen Home Depot's market position.

title: This Company’s Earnings Have Bad News for Home Depot and Lowe’s Stock
summary: Emerson Electric reported better-than-expected earnings, but its results contained a warning for investors in Home Depot and Lowe's. The industrial company's performance, coupled with higher prices, suggests potential negative impacts on retail demand for home improvement stores. This could imply a challenging outlook for Home Depot and Lowe's stock.

title: Home Depot Kids Workshops Return to Stores
summary: The Home Depot is bringing back its in-store Kids Workshops starting May 7, 2022, after shifting to virtual offerings in 2020 due to safety concerns. These workshops will occur on the first Saturday of each month, featuring seasonal-themed DIY projects like a Picket Fence Planter, and aim to foster creativity and learning in children. Participants will receive an apron, a collectible pin, and a certificate, continuing a 25-year tradition of community engagement.

title: Home Depot creates a $150M venture capital fund
summary: The Home Depot has launched Home Depot Ventures, a $150 million venture capital fund to invest in early-stage companies focused on enhancing customer experience and home improvement. The fund aims to support businesses that cater to both professional and homeowner customers, assist associates, and optimize operations through technology and data science. This initiative aligns with Home Depot's broader digital strategy, including recent leadership appointments focused on improving customer experience and digital infrastructure.

title: Neo Financial Announces $185 Million Series C Raise at a Unicorn Valuation
summary: Neo Financial, a Canadian fintech company, announced a $185 million Series C fundraising round, valuing the company at over $1 billion. This brings their total funding to $299 million. The company has grown to over 1 million customers since its 2019 inception and plans to use the new funding to expand its product offerings, including a mortgage product, and strengthen its presence across Canada.

title: Urban Edge grows food, wellness offerings with new leases at Bergen Town Center
summary: Urban Edge Properties is enhancing its Bergen Town Center property in Paramus with new leases for diverse tenants, including Kohl's, Chick’n Cone, Ani Ramen, V/O Med Spa, and Pandora Jewelry. These additions, alongside ongoing renovations to improve walkability and light, aim to provide a high-quality retail experience. Hackensack Meridian Health is also establishing an 80,000-square-foot medical office facility at the center.

title: New TA Express franchise opens today off I-45 in Fairfield, Texas
summary: TravelCenters of America Inc. has opened a new franchised TA Express travel center in Fairfield, Texas, located off Interstate 45, exit 198. The 17,000-square-foot facility offers various amenities for professional drivers and motorists, including dining options, truck parking, fueling positions, showers, and laundry facilities. This opening expands TA's nationwide network to 276 sites, strategically serving a key route between Dallas and Houston.

title: Duke Realty Rejects Nearly $24 Billion Buyout Offer From Prologis
summary: Duke Realty Corp. has rejected a nearly $24 billion buyout offer from warehousing giant Prologis Inc., deeming the unsolicited proposal insufficient. Prologis made its all-stock offer public after more than five months of private overtures. The acquisition would have significantly expanded Prologis's industrial real estate footprint, which already includes over 1 billion square feet used by major e-commerce companies.

title: Home Depot busts woman for half-dozen thefts at 4 Palm Beach County store locations
summary: A woman identified as Maria Matias was arrested after Home Depot loss prevention officers and the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office linked her to six separate thefts across four different store locations in Palm Beach County. The incidents, documented through video surveillance and fraudulent returns/purchases, involved Matias illicitly obtaining various items including door kits, ceiling fans, and seasonal decorations, often by using fake receipts or manipulating returns. Matias faces multiple charges including organized fraud and retail theft, and was released on bail after spending time in jail.

title: Home Depot's Stock Is Down, but It's Not Cheap
summary: Despite a significant drop from its December high, Home Depot's stock is still considered pricey by Morningstar analysts, trading at a premium to its fair value estimate. The retailer faces pressure from inflation, rising interest rates, and a shift in consumer spending toward travel, making its outlook challenging for 2022. Alternative home improvement stocks like Lowe's, Restoration Hardware, and Williams-Sonoma offer more compelling valuations.

title: Home Depot Sees Record First-Quarter Sales. The Stock Is Rising.
summary: Home Depot reported record first-quarter sales, exceeding expectations. This positive financial performance led to an increase in the company's stock value. The article highlights the strong sales figures for the quarter.

title: Home Depot raises profit forecast as demand holds for building materials
summary: Home Depot Inc increased its full-year profit forecast due to higher prices and sustained demand for building materials, also reporting a surprise jump in quarterly same-store sales. Despite a slowdown in DIY sales post-pandemic, demand from home-improvement professionals remains strong. The company expects comparable sales to increase about three percent in fiscal 2022, beating analyst expectations.

title: Home Depot (HD) Q1 results beat estimates; stock gains
summary: Home Depot (HD) reported higher-than-expected earnings and revenues for the first quarter of 2022, leading to a rise in the company's stock. Net income increased to $4.23 billion, or $4.09 per share, on revenues of $38.9 billion, both exceeding analyst estimates. CEO Ted Decker attributed the strong performance to associates navigating a challenging environment despite slow start to spring.

title: Home Depot raises annual profit forecast as demand holds up
summary: Home Depot Inc increased its full-year profit forecast and reported a surprise increase in quarterly same-store sales, driven by higher prices and steady demand for tools and building materials, particularly from home-improvement professionals. The company's shares rose 4% following the announcement, as it expects comparable sales to increase about 3% in fiscal 2022. This positive outlook helps allay concerns about easing consumer spending, with earnings per share also beating estimates.

title: Walmart: Profits dragged down by inflation, supply chain woes
summary: Walmart reported stronger sales in its fiscal first quarter but saw its profits decline due to surging inflation, particularly in food and fuel, and higher costs from global supply chain disruptions. The company subsequently cut its full-year earnings forecast, leading to an over 8 percent drop in shares. CEO Doug McMillon noted that inflation created more pressure on margin mix and operating costs than anticipated, despite overall sales holding up as shoppers shifted to lower-priced items and private brands.

title: After decades of producing chemicals, Westlake makes a material shift
summary: Westlake Corp., a Houston-based chemical and materials manufacturer, has undergone a significant transformation, shedding the word "chemical" from its name to reflect its expansion into material manufacturing. Following a series of nearly $4 billion in acquisitions since 2020, the company is now earning record profits, with revenue increasing by over 70 percent in the first quarter of 2022. CEO Albert Chao discusses the company's growth strategy, its move closer to consumer products in the housing and construction sectors, and its commitment to sustainability and emission reduction.

title: Home Depot raises full-year forecasts as demand stays firm
summary: Home Depot Inc. raised its annual profit and sales forecasts, easing concerns about demand despite surging inflation. The company's first-quarter comparable sales increased, driven by professional home-improvement demand and higher sales in certain categories, indicating favorable underlying housing metrics. This forecast raise was seen as "unexpected" by some analysts given the volatile economic environment.

title: After heightened demand during the pandemic, growth at Home Depot and Lowe's begins to normalize
summary: Following two years of elevated sales during the pandemic, growth in the home improvement sector is normalizing. Home Depot reported increased net sales and operating income for Q1, outperforming Lowe's, largely due to strong performance from its Pro customers. Lowe's experienced a slight decline in sales and comps, attributed to a cooler spring and its larger DIY customer base, prompting expectations of more subdued growth for the retailer.

title: Dramatic shift in sales mix leaves Target overloaded with inventory
summary: Target is grappling with an oversupply of inventory, particularly in large home goods categories like kitchen appliances and outdoor furniture, due to an unexpected shift in consumer spending habits. Following the end of federal stimulus payouts, shoppers moved away from major home makeovers and are now prioritizing smaller decor items, essentials, and experiences. To address this, Target plans to cut prices and right-size its assortments, anticipating global supply chain issues to persist until early 2023.

title: Target earnings fall short as supply chain struggles persist
summary: Target Corp. reported a significant miss on Q1 2022 earnings, with net profit more than halving despite strong comparable sales growth. The shortfall was attributed to higher-than-expected freight and transportation costs, excess inventory, and a dramatic shift in consumer spending away from discretionary goods. This mirrors similar struggles faced by competitor Walmart, highlighting the ongoing challenges for big box retailers amid supply chain disruptions and changing consumer habits.

title: Lowes vs Home Depot – Which Store is Better?
summary: This article compares Lowe's and Home Depot across various aspects like company size, customer service, power tool brands, and building materials, aiming to determine which store is "better." While acknowledging that both are strong contenders in the home improvement market, the authors provide insights based on their experience and polling, concluding that the preference often comes down to specific needs, brand loyalty, and the quality of local store employees. The comparison highlights their respective strengths and offers guidance for both Pros and DIYers.

title: Our Ultimate Stock-Pickers' Top 10 High-Conviction Purchases
summary: The article highlights the top 10 high-conviction purchases by Morningstar's Ultimate Stock-Pickers, focusing on significant additions to portfolios. Despite market volatility and inflation in early 2022, managers found value across various sectors, with Sherwin-Williams, T-Mobile, and Home Depot being particularly notable. Many of these high-conviction and new-money purchases received positive economic moat ratings from Morningstar analysts.

title: Sherwin-Williams Co. stock underperforms Tuesday when compared to competitors
summary: Shares of Sherwin-Williams Co. (SHW) dropped 3.01% on Tuesday, closing at $268.04, underperforming the broader market and its competitors. This decline ended a three-day winning streak for the company, which is currently $86.11 below its 52-week high. Competitors like Home Depot Inc., PPG Industries Inc., and Masco Corp. also saw declines but generally fell less than Sherwin-Williams.

title: Suspect in San Jose Home Depot Fire Appears in Court
summary: Dillyn Jaycruz Gogue, accused of intentionally setting a Home Depot store on fire in San Jose on April 9, appeared in court to face numerous charges including arson. His public defender indicated a conflict in representing him, likely due to other alleged crimes like thefts on the same day. Gogue is expected back in court on June 29 to determine if an alternate defender's office can take the case.

title: Walmart is using its thousands of stores to battle Amazon for e-commerce market share
summary: Walmart is leveraging its extensive network of nearly 4,700 stores across the U.S. as "shoppable fulfillment centers" to boost its e-commerce market share and compete with Amazon. The retailer is transforming its physical locations into hubs for drone deliveries, automated online grocery order fulfillment, and direct-to-fridge drop-offs, aiming to provide faster and more efficient service. This strategy also involves wooing third-party sellers by offering fulfillment services from its stores and expanding its delivery and membership programs like GoLocal and Walmart+.

title: Home Improvement Market Size & Share | North America, Europe, & APAC Industry Forecasts 2027: Graphical Research
summary: The global home improvement market is projected to grow significantly through 2027, driven by homeowners seeking to enhance comfort, style, and value, particularly influenced by the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on living spaces. Key trends include the rise of DIY projects in APAC, increasing renovations across the region, and a surge in DIFM projects and exterior replacements in North America. Europe is also seeing momentum in property and kitchen upgrades due to an aging housing stock and demand for smart home technologies.

title: Beyond the distribution center
summary: The article discusses how evolving customer demands and e-commerce growth are pushing retailers to rethink traditional distribution center models. It introduces three new fulfillment horizons: within the store, around the store, and in the neighborhood (Q-commerce), detailing how retailers are using existing assets, strategic partnerships, and rapid delivery services to meet modern customer expectations for speed and agility. The authors urge retailers to act quickly, invest in future-proof models, and foster cross-functional and external partnerships to stay competitive.

title: Home Depot Upgrades 2.3K Retail Edge Locations Using SUSE Rancher, K3s
summary: Home Depot has transitioned its 2,300+ retail locations to a new architecture leveraging SUSE's Rancher and K3s technology. This shift aims to automate the maintenance of containerized applications at edge locations, eliminating the manual effort previously required. The K3s, a lightweight Kubernetes version, combined with Rancher's management capabilities, enables efficient deployment; updates of operating systems and Kubernetes layers; and management of thousands of remote clusters with limited IT resources.

title: The Home Depot Foundation Invests to Build and Improve More than 800 Housing Units for Veterans Facing Homelessness
summary: The Home Depot Foundation has granted an additional $8 million to nonprofit partners to combat veteran homelessness, bringing its total investment in veteran causes to over $110 million. This funding will support the construction and renovation of more than 800 housing units, short-term residential programs, and supportive services for veterans. The Foundation is partnering with organizations like the National Coalition of Homeless Veterans, Volunteers of America, and Community Solutions to provide affordable housing and assistance across the nation.

title: Hold the Presses: H-E-B Grocery Store Not Yet Coming to Fort Worth at Parkside at Alliance Town Center
summary: News that H-E-B would anchor the Parkside at Alliance Town Center in Fort Worth was prematurely announced. While Hillwood initially indicated an H-E-B as the anchor, public relations officials later clarified that the grocery store has not yet agreed to build there. However, four other dining and retail concepts — Torchy’s Tacos, CAVA, Black Rifle Coffee Company, and Dash Nail Spa — are confirmed and under construction, with planned openings for early 2023.

title: Home Depot Wins Suit Prohibiting Employees From Wearing BLM Logos
summary: A judge has ruled in favor of Home Depot, prohibiting its employees from wearing Black Lives Matter apparel while on the job. The administrative law judge stated that the BLM message does not meet the requirements for legal protection as it primarily addresses the unjustified killings of Black individuals and acts as a political umbrella for social concerns. This decision follows a complaint by the US National Labor Relations Board against Home Depot for allegedly interfering with employees' rights by banning BLM messaging on aprons.

title: 8 Money-Saving Secrets Home Depot Employees Want You to Know
summary: This article reveals eight money-saving secrets when shopping at Home Depot, directly from employee insights. Key tips include returning dead plants within a year, renting expensive tools instead of buying, and utilizing free DIY workshops. Additionally, shoppers can find deeply discounted cull lumber and "mistake paint," check online for coupons, time purchases during major sales, and benefit from their 110% price match guarantee.

title: Home Depot, Costco and 3 More Retail Stocks to Buy
summary: The article identifies five retail stocks poised for success despite recent declines in retail sales. It highlights companies like Home Depot, Costco, AutoZone, Academy Sports + Outdoors, and Dollar General, explaining why each is a promising investment opportunity in the current economic climate.
