title: How Home Depot’s Pro Xtra Program Alone Helped Me Save $1,400 This Year
summary: The author details how Home Depot's Pro Xtra program helped him save $1,400 this year through perks, coupons, and special offers, highlighting that individuals don't need to be licensed contractors or business owners to sign up. The article also suggests exploring similar discount programs at other retailers and leveraging small business status for additional savings. It emphasizes asking for volume discounts and considering licensing for industry-specific benefits.

title: $210M loan secured for Inland Empire industrial development
summary: JLL Capital Markets has arranged a $210 million construction loan for the first phase of Ontario Ranch Business Park, a 1.68-million-square-foot industrial development in California's Inland Empire. The project, a joint venture between Real Estate Development Associates, LLC and Clarion Partners, LLC, will include seven buildings, with its largest preleased to The Home Depot. The Inland Empire industrial market is experiencing extremely low vacancy rates, indicating strong demand.

title: The Home Depot Adopts HPE GreenLake for Aruba Networking and Aruba ESP to Drive Enhanced Customer and Associate Experiences
summary: The Home Depot has selected Aruba ESP delivered via HPE GreenLake for Aruba networking to enhance customer and associate experiences across its U.S. stores. This partnership aims to provide a solid network foundation with speed, scale, and flexibility, supporting interconnected capabilities and streamlining IT management. The technology investment will enable features like in-store navigation and easy product look-up for associates, improving the overall retail experience.

title: Home Depot Refreshes Tech To Boost Customer Service
summary: Home Depot is partnering with Aruba, a Hewlett Packard Enterprise company, to enhance in-store connectivity and improve customer and employee experiences. They are implementing Aruba ESP via HPE GreenLake for Aruba networking, and Zebra Technologies’ handheld devices, to provide a seamless omnichannel retail experience. This technology refresh aims to streamline IT management, proactively monitor network health, and enable features like in-store navigation and image search, ultimately making home improvement projects easier for customers.

title: The 13 Best Grill Brands
summary: This article identifies and reviews 13 top grill brands, highlighting what makes each manufacturer stand out in the market. It discusses various types of grills, including charcoal, gas, pellet, and griddles, outlining their price ranges, top products, and unique features. The selection criteria prioritize durability, performance, versatility, and availability across different retailers, catering to diverse user needs and budgets.

title: New externship program gives law students taste of in-house legal work with businesses
summary: Mercer Law School is launching a new Corporate Counsel Externship Program this fall to provide students with hands-on experience in in-house legal work. Led by former Tractor Supply general counsel Ben Parrish, the program addresses the growing demand for in-house legal professionals and will partner students with companies like Home Depot and Aflac. Students will gain practical skills in areas such as contract drafting, compliance, and negotiation, preparing them for diverse legal career paths.

title: Lowe's Cos. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors
summary: On Thursday, Lowe's Cos. stock experienced a decline of 0.81%, closing at $174.67, amidst a broader market downturn. This performance meant Lowe's underperformed its competitors, such as Home Depot Inc. and Kingfisher PLC ADR, which saw gains. The stock closed significantly below its 52-week high, and its trading volume was higher than its 50-day average.

title: A new ETF investing in disaster relief launches in time for hurricane season
summary: A new exchange-traded fund (ETF) called Procure Disaster Recovery Strategy ETF (ticker: FEMA) has launched, focusing on companies involved in disaster recovery and risk reduction. The ETF's creation was inspired by Hurricane Katrina and invests in a diversified basket of companies across various sectors, including those that provide communications tech, risk assessment, engineering, and cloud computing services. Since its launch on June 1, the FEMA ETF is down about 11%.

title: Fire breaks out in Home Depot in Williston
summary: A fire broke out in the Williston Home Depot on Thursday afternoon after a stove caught fire in the receiving area, igniting nearby boxes. An employee extinguished the initial blaze before firefighters arrived, who then ventilated moderate smoke from the rear of the store. The fire was deemed accidental, and no injuries were reported.

title: The Homer Fund: Supporting Associates in Need with the Annual Orange at Heart Campaign
summary: The Homer Fund, The Home Depot's employee assistance program, aids associates facing hardship through grants. Funded by both associates and the company, it's celebrated by the annual Orange at Heart campaign, ensuring every dollar donated directly helps fellow employees. Since its inception in 1999, the fund has distributed nearly $233 million to over 165,000 associates, including support during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Evernote, Home Depot outsource network management
summary: Evernote and Home Depot have outsourced their network management to vendors like Meter and Aruba, respectively. This strategy allows their in-house IT staff to focus on business-critical projects rather than the daily tasks of network maintenance. Both companies found that a subscription-based "network as a service" (NaaS) model was more cost-effective and agile for adapting to changing business needs.

title: Pace is attracting new people and businesses, while trying to maintain the same ol' charm
summary: Pace, Florida, is experiencing significant economic and population growth, transforming from a bedroom community to a commercially vibrant suburb. While residents appreciate the increased availability of goods and services, concerns are rising about traffic congestion and the proliferation of chain stores. Local officials and residents are looking for infrastructure improvements and more diverse entertainment options to manage this rapid development while retaining the area's community feel.

title: Celebrating 30 Years of Business and Partnership with American Carpet South
summary: American Carpet South (ACS), The Home Depot’s largest carpet provider, is celebrating 30 years in business. Joe Santagata, CEO, invested his college fund to partner with his father, Bob, and expand their flooring services, eventually becoming CEO in 2007. ACS has been recognized as National Flooring Service Provider of the Year by The Home Depot and attributes its success to strategic partnerships and a focus on customer service.

title: Home Depot taps Aruba platform to power customer, associate experiences
summary: The Home Depot is expanding its partnership with Aruba by deploying Aruba ESP and HPE GreenLake for Aruba networking across its U.S. stores. This initiative aims to enhance both customer and associate experiences by providing a robust, flexible, and fast network. The upgrade supports interconnected capabilities like in-store navigation and image search for customers, and empowers associates with handheld devices for efficient inventory management.

title: Bath & Body Works changes return policy
summary: Bath & Body Works is updating its return policy, effective September 14, to limit non-receipted returns or exchanges to $250 within a 90-day period at select U.S. stores. The company will use an electronic system for tracking these returns, requiring customers to show a government-issued ID. While maintaining a 100% satisfaction guarantee, the updated policy will no longer accept products showing excessive wear and tear.

title: Two single-tenant North Carolina retail properties sell for $23.93M
summary: JLL Capital Markets announced the $23.93 million sale of two single-tenant retail properties in Durham, North Carolina: a 120,000-square-foot Home Depot and a 148,663-square-foot Costco. Armada Hoffler Properties sold the properties to a New York-based buyer at a blended 4.0 percent cap rate. Both retailers operate under long-term absolute NNN ground leases in a high-visibility location near Duke University.

title: Home Depot’s 12-foot $300 skeleton is back in stock for Halloween
summary: Home Depot has brought back its popular 12-foot skeleton, "Skelly," along with other Halloween decor, for the spooky season. The $300 skeleton, which features animated LCD eyes, first went viral and sold out in 2020. The Halloween items launched online and will be available in brick-and-mortar stores from late August to early September.

title: This family moved into a Home Depot shed after going into debt ⁠— then made a huge profit selling it
summary: A Georgia couple, Nick and Meghan Lucido, got out of significant debt by moving into an 860-square-foot Home Depot shed. After paying off $82,000 in nine months, they sold the shed for $312,000, making a substantial profit. This allowed them to build their dream farmhouse and achieve financial freedom.

title: Make Your Halloween Set-Up Haunted AF With A 15-Foot Phantom & 12-Foot Flying Witch
summary: Home Depot's Halloween 2022 decorations are back in stock, featuring the 12-foot skeleton, Skelly, and a new 15-foot phantom. This article highlights some of the Halloween items available to help enthusiasts create a spooky setup.

title: The Home Depot signs on for major distribution operation at new Childress Klein Steele Creek development
summary: The Home Depot is set to occupy a large industrial facility of over 603,000 square feet at The Concourse, Childress Klein's mixed-use development in the Steele Creek area of Charlotte. This marks another significant industrial presence for the home improvement retailer in the Charlotte region. Sources indicate this is a major distribution operation.

title: Jose "Pepe" Rodriguez | President – Mexico
summary: This article profiles Jose "Pepe" Rodriguez, the President of The Home Depot Mexico. It details his responsibilities, which include overseeing sales, operations, online platforms, and over 18,000 associates across 140 stores. The profile also highlights his career trajectory, from joining Home Depot in 2001 as a financial analyst to his various leadership roles in finance and operations both in Mexico and the U.S.

title: The Home Depot Announces Latest Carbon Emission Reductions, New Supplier Diversity Spending Goal and Progress on Community Investments in 2022 ESG Report
summary: The Home Depot announced significant progress in its 2022 ESG Report, detailing a reduction of approximately 172,000 metric tons in combined Scope 1 and 2 carbon emissions in 2021 and a 50 percent cut in U.S. store electricity usage since 2010. The company also set a new goal to spend $5 billion annually with diverse suppliers by 2025 and highlighted over $400 million contributed to veterans' causes by The Home Depot Foundation since 2011. These achievements underscore the company's commitment to its environmental, social, and governance pillars.

title: Home Depot’s giant 12-foot skeletons are already back but sold out quickly
summary: Home Depot's highly popular 12-foot giant skeletons, including a new Inferno Pumpkin version, have quickly sold out again this year for Halloween. These decorations, which have gained significant social media attention, often require customers to pay exorbitant resale prices if they miss the initial sale. Home Depot recommends signing up for notifications to be alerted when they are back in stock.

title: HOME DEPOT TAKES A WIN: Home Depot Barely Dodges TCPA Class Action Suit in Georgia
summary: Home Depot successfully had a TCPA class action suit dismissed with prejudice, despite failing to compel arbitration. The plaintiff, Melissa Carson, alleged Home Depot sent unwanted text messages after an unsubscribe request, but the court found she did not plausibly allege Home Depot itself sent the messages or assert an alternate theory of liability against the company. The court rejected Home Depot's attempt to enforce an arbitration clause through equitable estoppel, but ultimately dismissed the case because Carson's claims were not directly against Home Depot.

title: Thieves steal zero-turn mower, trailer from Tractor Supply Co., sheriff says
summary: Thieves reportedly stole a zero-turn mower, a trailer, and a grill from a Tractor Supply Co. in Denver early Friday morning, as stated by the sheriff. The incident, valued at $8,500, was caught on video surveillance, showing the culprits fleeing in a pickup truck. Authorities were alerted by an alarm company after a break-in was reported.

title: DeWALT recall announced for 1.4M miter saws due to injury, laceration hazards
summary: DeWALT has recalled over 1.4 million 12-inch Sliding Compound Miter Saws in the U.S. and Canada due to a safety hazard. The saws' rear safety guard can break or detach, posing injury and laceration risks from projectiles or direct blade contact. The company has received 571 reports of guard failure, including nine laceration injuries, and advises consumers to stop using the saws immediately and contact DeWALT for a free repair kit or service center repair.

title: Burberry appoints ex-Tesco CFO as Non-Executive Director
summary: Burberry Group has appointed Alan Stewart, former Chief Financial Officer of Tesco PLC, as its new Non-Executive Director, effective September 1, 2022. He will also become a member of Burberry's Audit and Nomination committees and is expected to replace Matthew Key as Audit Committee Chair. Stewart brings extensive experience from his previous roles at major public companies like Tesco, Marks & Spencer PLC, and WH Smith PLC.

title: A The Home Depot Joins Billion Dollar Roundtable, Continues to Expand Supplier Diversity Programs
summary: The Home Depot has joined the Billion Dollar Roundtable Inc. (BDR), a nonprofit recognizing corporations that spend over $1 billion annually with minority and woman-owned suppliers. In fiscal year 2021, the company spent $3.3 billion with diverse suppliers, demonstrating its commitment to expanding its supplier diversity program to foster growth, reflect customer diversity, and strengthen communities. This move aims to leverage innovative and unique products and perspectives from diverse businesses, ultimately meeting customer needs and increasing shareholder value.

title: The Home Depot unifies customer experiences with Adobe
summary: The Home Depot has successfully unified its online and in-store customer experiences using Adobe products, leading to a 62% increase in personalized campaigns and a 14% rise in net sales year over year. The company leverages Adobe Real-Time Customer Data Platform and Adobe Experience Platform to create unified customer profiles, enabling highly relevant messaging and inspiration for customers' home improvement projects. This data-driven approach, along with innovative tools like a mobile app for in-store navigation and AI-powered product search, allows The Home Depot to cater to diverse customer journeys, from project-based customers to item buyers and contractors.

title: News | Home Depot Plugs Into Duke Realty's Most Energy Efficient Warehouse to Date
summary: Home Depot has leased a 529,000-square-foot energy-efficient warehouse in Irwindale, California, developed by Duke Realty. This "smart" industrial building, the most energy-efficient to date for Duke Realty, features advanced technologies expected to save significant electricity and reduce its carbon footprint. The lease represents one of the largest industrial deals in Los Angeles County, highlighting the growing demand for sustainable commercial properties.

title: Victoria Town Center to open Boot Barn, Burlington Coat Factory
summary: Victoria Town Center, a new shopping development in Victoria, Texas, has announced Boot Barn and Burlington Coat Factory as its first two tenants. Boot Barn is expected to open by the end of the year, with Burlington Coat Factory following early next year. The city anticipates the $31 million private investment will generate significant property and sales tax revenue, with the developer needing to meet a $54.4 million sales revenue target by 2027.

title: The Home Depot Announces Second Quarter Results; Reaffirms Fiscal 2022 Guidance
summary: The Home Depot announced record-breaking second-quarter results for fiscal 2022, reporting sales of $43.8 billion and net earnings of $5.2 billion. The company reaffirmed its fiscal 2022 guidance, expecting total sales growth and comparable sales growth of approximately 3.0 percent. This strong performance reflects continued high demand for home improvement projects.

title: 'Our customer is in a really good place': Demand for home renovations fuels record Home Depot profits
summary: Home Depot is experiencing record profits due to strong demand for home renovation projects, despite rising interest rates and recession concerns. The company’s business performance indicates a robust homeowner appetite for renovations. This trend is notable given the broader cooling in the Atlanta housing market.

title: Home Depot Stock Surges as Profit and Sales Top Forecasts
summary: Home Depot reported stronger-than-expected second-quarter earnings of $5.05 per share and reaffirmed its 2022 financial guidance. This positive performance, which included a 5.8% rise in same-store sales, led to a surge in the company's stock.

title: Introducing Vining Ivy: GLIDDEN Paint by PPG’s ‘bluish, greenish’ 2023 Color of the Year
summary: PPG announced Vining Ivy (PPG1148-6) as the joint 2023 Color of the Year for both its Glidden and PPG paint brands. This versatile "bluish-greenish" teal is described as energizing yet grounding, suitable for diverse design aesthetics and spaces. The color is available in various PPG products, including Glidden Diamond paint and Speedhide Pro-EV Zero interior latex paint.

title: Home Depot pushes ahead of Lowe’s as it leans on pro customers
summary: Home Depot reported record quarterly sales and earnings, driven by its strong performance with pro customers, which helped offset a shortened spring selling season that negatively impacted DIY sales. In contrast, competitor Lowe’s experienced lower-than-expected sales, primarily due to its heavier reliance on DIY customers, whose spending has moderated. While both companies reaffirmed their annual outlooks, Home Depot's focus on pro customers appears to be a key differentiator in a challenging economic environment.

title: The Home Depot Names Ted Decker Chair of the Board
summary: The Home Depot announced that its Board of Directors has elected CEO and President Edward "Ted" Decker as chair of the board, effective October 1, 2022. Decker, a 22-year veteran of the company, will succeed Craig Menear, who is retiring. Greg Brenneman, the board's lead director, praised both Decker's passion for customers and associates and Menear's visionary leadership.

title: The Home Depot Declares Second Quarter Dividend of $1.90 and Announces $15 Billion Share Repurchase Authorization
summary: The Home Depot announced that its board of directors declared a second quarter cash dividend of $1.90 per share, payable on September 15, 2022. The company also authorized a new $15 billion share repurchase program, replacing its previous authorization. This marks the 142nd consecutive quarter the company has paid a cash dividend.

title: The Home Depot proposes a third St. Johns County store
summary: The Home Depot plans to open its third St. Johns County store in the World Commerce Center, near the intersection of I-95 and International Golf Parkway. This proposed 136,014-square-foot facility includes a garden center, tool rental, and seasonal sales area. The move comes as Lowe's Home Centers also proposes a second location in northern St. Johns County, intensifying competition in the region's home improvement market.

title: Tractor Supply Co. plows into Clayton for grand opening
summary: Tractor Supply Co. celebrated its grand opening and ribbon-cutting in Clayton on July 29, 2022, in partnership with Forward Rabun and the Rabun County Chamber of Commerce. The new store, located at 1563 Highway 441 South, features a greenhouse and a dog/pet washing station. The grand opening was extended with events including an adoption day with Rabun County Paws 4 Life and local vendors on August 6.

title: Home Depot finally coming to this Lehigh County shopping center
summary: After more than a decade, Home Depot is set to open a 136,058-square-foot store in the Macungie Crossings shopping center in Lower Macungie Township, Lehigh County. The township board of commissioners approved the development, which includes design customizations and plans for shared parking with future retailers, aiming for a summer 2023 opening. This project is part of a larger vision to create a walkable, village-like atmosphere at Macungie Crossings.

title: Home Depot Strengthens Store Networks to Support Hardware Refresh
summary: Home Depot is upgrading its in-store network infrastructure to support the rollout of 125,000 new multi-function hdPhones to its store associates. This network refresh, utilizing Aruba ESP via HPE GreenLake, aims to enhance interconnected retail experiences for both customers and employees. The initiative addresses challenges posed by store environments and expands coverage to outdoor areas for services like curbside pickup, following extensive testing to ensure seamless operation at scale.

title: With Spoken, two retail newbies are exposing white labeling across furniture retailers

title: The 7 Best Plumbing Supply Stocks To Buy Now
summary: This article identifies the seven best plumbing supply stocks to consider for investment, highlighting companies like Ferguson PLC, The Home Depot Inc, and W.W. Grainger. It details each company's market position, financial performance, and dividend information, while also discussing why plumbing supply stocks are generally considered a good and stable investment due to constant demand, aging infrastructure, and new construction.

title: W.W. Grainger Inc. stock rises Tuesday, outperforms market
summary: W.W. Grainger Inc. (GWW) stock rose 0.62% to $675.84 on Tuesday, outperforming the broader market which saw the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average decline. This marked the second consecutive day of gains for the stock, placing it $33.37 short of its 52-week high. The company also outperformed competitors like Amazon.com Inc., Home Depot Inc., and Lowe's Cos.

title: City Known for Agriculture Gets Long-Awaited First Sprouts Farmers Market
summary: Stockton, California, a major agricultural hub, has finally welcomed its first Sprouts Farmers Market, located in the Sherwood Place mall. This 26,800-square-foot lease earned a 2023 CoStar Impact Award for its role in revitalizing the long-struggling mall. Brixton Capital's redevelopment plans for the property included Sprouts as a prominent tenant, aiming to better serve the community's grocery needs.

title: Fabuloso recall 2023: Full list of products that have been recalled
summary: Colgate-Palmolive issued a voluntary recall in February 2023 for millions of bottles of Fabuloso multi-purpose cleaners in the US and Canada due to potential bacterial contamination. The recall affects specific scents and sizes of products manufactured between December 14, 2022, and January 23, 2023, which may contain Pseudomonas bacteria due to insufficient preservative levels. Customers are advised to stop using and dispose of recalled products and can claim a refund, though no infections have been reported to date.

title: The Home Depot Announces Grants for 36 HBCUs at 2023 Retool Your School Awards Celebration
summary: The Home Depot awarded over $2 million in grants to 36 Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) through its 2023 Retool Your School program. This year, the program expanded to include needs-based grants for initiatives like Innovation Lounge renovations and scholarships, in addition to the campus improvement grants. The program has invested over $9.25 million in HBCUs since its inception in 2009.

title: Nordstrom Rack coming to Jacksonville Beach
summary: Nordstrom Inc. announced it will open a new 30,000-square-foot Nordstrom Rack store in Jacksonville Beach in spring 2024. The store will be located in the South Beach Regional shopping center, taking over the former Stein Mart space. This addition will mark Nordstrom's 18th Nordstrom Rack store in Florida, alongside six full-line stores.

title: Fastenal Sales Up 9% in First Three Months of 2023
summary: Fastenal reported a 9% increase in sales to $1.86 billion in the first three months of 2023, exceeding Wall Street projections. The company's gross profit, operating income, and net earnings also saw significant increases. Fastenal attributed its strong performance to broad pricing actions, robust demand in industrial capital goods, and the expansion of its "Digital Footprint" operations.

title: How an American Logging Giant Bills Itself as a Climate Hero
summary: Weyerhaeuser, one of the world's largest timber companies, is promoting its logging activities as sustainable and a solution to climate change, despite plans to increase lumber production. The company is investing in carbon offsets from its vast forest holdings, claiming that replanting trees and using wood for products stores carbon. However, critics argue that the math is "fuzzy," as regrowing forests take decades to reach full sequestration strength and logging can lead to continued carbon emissions.

title: Pleasanton Home Depot employee Blake Mohs identified as victim shot, killed during shoplifting confrontation
summary: Blake Mohs, a 26-year-old Home Depot loss prevention employee, was shot and killed while confronting a shoplifting suspect in Pleasanton, California. He was engaged to be married in the summer. Two suspects have been arrested and face charges including murder and child endangerment.

title: Home Depot dog bite case should have been comp exclusive: State high court
summary: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court has ruled that a Home Depot dog bite case, where an employee was injured by a customer's dog, should fall under the exclusive jurisdiction of workers' compensation. This decision reverses lower court rulings that allowed the employee to pursue a negligence lawsuit against Home Depot, asserting that the workers' compensation law provides immunity to employers in such third-party actions. The court found that the case did not meet the criteria for exceptions to the workers' compensation exclusivity rule.

title: Stanley Black & Decker recalls about 2.2 million sledgehammers due to injury risk
summary: Stanley Black & Decker has issued a recall for approximately 2.2 million DeWALT, Stanley FATMAX, and Craftsman Fiberglass Sledgehammers due to a risk of the hammer heads detaching unexpectedly. This defect has led to 192 reported incidents, including two resulting in face and head injuries. Consumers are advised to stop using the recalled sledgehammers and contact Stanley Black & Decker for a refund.

title: Home Depot to open new location in Katy’s Cane Island
summary: The bustling Cane Island area of Katy, Texas, is set to welcome a new Home Depot store. The Katy City Council approved an economic development agreement with Home Depot USA Inc. for the new location. This development follows the city's annexation of a 24-acre plot of land to facilitate the project, which Mayor Dusty Thiele highlighted as an example of smart economic development for Katy.

title: Bed Bath & Beyond Files for Bankruptcy With Plan to Shut Stores
summary: Bed Bath & Beyond Inc. has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New Jersey, planning to liquidate its 360 Bed Bath & Beyond stores and 120 Buy Buy Baby shops. The company is actively seeking a buyer for its assets, with the possibility of halting store closures if a successful sale occurs. This move puts thousands of jobs at risk as the retailer struggled to adapt to evolving consumer behaviors.

title: After Dog Bite at Work, Exclusivity Leashes Home Depot Employees Tort Claims
summary: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that a Home Depot employee bitten by a customer's dog at work could not sue the company beyond workers' compensation benefits due to the state's exclusivity provision. The court found that the injury was inextricably linked to the workplace incident, even though the employee argued Home Depot's negligence prevented a third-party suit against the dog owner. This decision upholds the principle that workers' compensation is generally the sole remedy for workplace injuries in Pennsylvania.

title: Long Island retail center anchored by ShopRite and Home Depot sold
summary: JLL Capital Markets facilitated the sale of Riverhead Centre in Riverhead, New York. This retail center is prominently anchored by major tenants ShopRite and Home Depot. The transaction highlights investment activity in the retail real estate sector.

title: Tractor Supply Is the Home Improvement Stock to Buy Now, Analyst Says
summary: An analyst suggests buying Tractor Supply stock, arguing it's a better home improvement play than Home Depot or Lowe's, despite a tough year for the sector. While first-quarter earnings for home improvement retailers might not be strong, the outlook for later in the year could improve.

title: The Home Depot Announces First Quarter Fiscal 2023 Results; Updates Fiscal 2023 Guidance
summary: The Home Depot reported first-quarter fiscal 2023 sales of $37.3 billion, a 4.2% decrease from the prior year, with comparable sales declining 4.5%. Net earnings were $3.9 billion, or $3.82 per diluted share. The company updated its fiscal 2023 guidance, expecting sales and comparable sales to decline between 2% and 5%, citing lumber deflation, unfavorable weather, and softening demand.

title: Home Depot Earnings Take a Hit as Company Sticks with ‘Woke’
summary: The National Legal and Policy Center (NLPC) presented a proposal at Home Depot's annual shareholder meeting to require an independent board chair, coinciding with a 4.2% drop in the company's Q1 revenue. NLPC attributes Home Depot's lagging performance compared to Lowe's and recent financial hits to its continued emphasis on ESG priorities. The organization warns that "woke agenda politics" could negatively impact Home Depot's business, citing examples like Disney and Anheuser-Busch.

title: The Home Depot Partners with Army & Air Force Exchange Service to Offer Tax-Free Major Appliances
summary: The Home Depot is partnering with the Army & Air Force Exchange Service (Exchange) to provide tax-free major appliances to eligible military shoppers. This program allows active-duty service members, their dependents, retirees, DoD civilians, and honorably discharged veterans to purchase appliances online through ShopMyExchange.com and in up to 60 planned Home Depot appliance showrooms at various military bases. The initiative reflects The Home Depot's commitment to supporting military families, with 100% of Exchange earnings benefiting military communities.

title: Lowe's stock bounces back, as U.S. same-store sales beat rival Home Depot for first time in more than 2 years
summary: Lowe's Companies Inc. saw its stock reverse to a gain after reporting fiscal first-quarter profit that exceeded expectations. Despite same-store sales missing forecasts, they surpassed those of rival Home Depot Inc. for the first time in over two years. Although Lowe's lowered its full-year guidance for earnings and revenue, the revised outlook still aligned with Wall Street's projections.

title: Costco earnings miss estimates as shoppers curb discretionary spending
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp (COST) missed quarterly earnings estimates as consumers reduced non-essential spending due to inflation and economic uncertainties. The retailer experienced a drop in demand for high-margin products like home furnishings and electronics, despite a rise in membership revenue. This trend also impacted other major retailers such as Target and Home Depot.

title: Costco earnings miss estimates as shoppers curb discretionary spending
summary: Costco Wholesale Corp missed quarterly earnings estimates as shoppers reduced discretionary spending due to high inflation and economic uncertainty. The warehouse retailer, like others, saw a decline in demand for high-margin non-essential items, leading to lower-than-expected profits and revenue. Despite this, membership revenue, which accounts for most of Costco's gross margin, increased.

title: The Home Depot to Host 2023 Investor and Analyst Conference on June 13
summary: The Home Depot announced it will host its 2023 Investor and Analyst Conference on Tuesday, June 13, at 9 a.m. ET. A webcast of the event will be available on the company's investor relations website, with a replay accessible approximately two hours after the event concludes. The company also provided details on its store count and market performance.

title: Gary Rasor | Son of Hillsborough Home Depot worker killed wants crackdown on theft, he tells 'Nightline'
summary: The son of Gary Rasor, a Home Depot employee who died after confronting a shoplifter, is calling for a crackdown on organized retail crime. Rasor, 83, was fatally injured while trying to stop someone stealing pressure washers. His son, Jeff Rasor, told "Nightline" that there need to be severe consequences for such crimes, emphasizing that no merchandise is worth a human life.

title: Home Depot Files Opening Brief in California Supreme Court Case Set to Determine Validity of Time Clock Rounding
summary: Home Depot has filed its opening brief in a California Supreme Court case challenging a Sixth District Court of Appeal ruling that found the company's total time rounding for non-exempt employees unlawful. The appellate court's decision in Camp v. Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. ignored prior precedent, asserting that employers must pay for all exact time worked if they can capture it. Critical to the appeal, the California Employment Law Council and the Employers Group have enlisted Sheppard Mullin to draft an amicus brief arguing for the continued validity of time rounding practices for employers in California.

title: The Home Depot now sells surprisingly stylish build-it-yourself tiny homes – for under $50,000
summary: The Home Depot is now selling surprisingly stylish build-it-yourself tiny homes for under $50,000. These pre-fabricated, one-bedroom homes range from $4,000 to $40,000 and can serve as an addition or a primary residence, offering a compact and accessible housing solution. While the initial price is attractive, buyers need to factor in additional costs for essential features like doors, windows, and electrical/plumbing systems.

title: The Home Depot Provides Update on Strategic Objectives; Reaffirms Fiscal 2023 Guidance; Establishes Market Stability Outlook
summary: The Home Depot held its 2023 Investor and Analyst Conference to discuss strategic objectives, reaffirming its fiscal 2023 guidance, which projects a sales and comparable sales decline of 2% to 5%. The company also established a "Market Stability Base Case" outlook, anticipating low-single-digit overall market growth and 3% to 4% annual sales growth once the home improvement market stabilizes. CEO Ted Decker highlighted the company's strong competitive advantages and significant growth opportunities within the fragmented home improvement market.

title: Big Changes Inside New York Home Depot Stores
summary: Home Depot stores in New York, including the Wappingers Falls location, are increasingly locking up various items like power tools and copper wire. This change is a response to high rates of shoplifting, making it necessary for customers to request employee assistance to handle or purchase these products. The new policy aims to deter theft, but it also means that shopping at Home Depot now takes longer for items that are under lock and key.

title: Glen Carbon panel approves Dick's Sporting Goods concept plan
summary: A Glen Carbon building and development committee approved the concept plan for Dick's Sporting Goods at the Orchard Town Center (OTC). This marks the first step toward bringing the store to Glen Carbon, with the company slated to occupy over 6.5 acres of the development. The approval also provided updates on the two-phase development, traffic improvements, remaining outlots, and plans for a greenspace with a stage and amphitheater.

title: P&G’s Vanished Forest Degradation Commitment
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has removed its commitment to prohibit forest degradation from its latest forest sourcing policy, despite previous investor pressure. This move suggests a backtracking on responsible sourcing claims, leaving P&G as a continued driver of degradation in Canada's boreal forests, which has significant climate and biodiversity impacts. The NRDC highlights that P&G's previous claims were misleading and calls for a genuine commitment to eliminate forest degradation.

title: First Trust Exchange-Traded Fund III - First Trust Morningstar Dividend Leaders Index Fund (FDL) News, Articles, Events & Latest Updates
summary: This article provides recent news and updates for the First Trust Morningstar Dividend Leaders Index Fund (FDL). It highlights several financial articles discussing FDL and other dividend ETFs outperforming the S&P 500, offering current income, and gaining investor interest amid market volatility and sector rotations. The feed includes news from Zacks and Stocktwits discussing various dividend-focused investment strategies and company-specific financial reports impacting dividend stocks.

title: The Home Depot launches $500M cost-savings plan
summary: The Home Depot is implementing a $500 million cost-savings plan expected to be completed in fiscal year 2024. This initiative involves reducing excess supply chain holding capacity that was expanded due to increased demand during 2020 and 2021. The company is also optimizing its downstream supply chain through forecasting, labor management, and technology, while continuing to leverage past investments in supply chain infrastructure.

title: Home Depot adds automatic fee and customers need to watch out where they shopped
summary: Home Depot has introduced a 15% restocking fee on returned or canceled special orders, a policy that can lead to substantial charges due to the often high cost of these customized items. This policy differs from their standard no-fee return for most purchases. Other retailers like Levi's, Urban Outfitters, and Kohl's also have return fees, with some offering ways to avoid them such as in-store returns or membership programs.

title: Home Depot Wages Settlement
summary: Home Depot employees are seeking preliminary approval for a $72.5 million settlement in a California wage and hour class-action lawsuit. The lawsuit, brought under California's Private Attorneys General Act, alleges that Home Depot failed to pay employees for off-the-clock work, including time spent locked in stores after shifts, and for tasks like putting on aprons, impacting over 272,000 workers since March 2012. The settlement aims to resolve these allegations, with Home Depot denying wrongdoing but settling to avoid the costs of litigation.

title: Riot leverages Texas power strategy to fund operations as BTC balance increases
summary: Riot Platforms reported producing 460 Bitcoin in June 2023, a 40% decrease from May, but successfully leveraged its power strategy in Texas to generate $10 million in revenue, equivalent to an additional 361 BTC. This strategy, which involves participating in ERCOT's ancillary services and the Four Coincident Peak program, allowed Riot to avoid solely relying on Bitcoin sales for funding operations during a heatwave. The company also announced plans to significantly boost its hash rate with an order for 33,280 new MicroBT miners.

title: Rabina completes $13.5M refinance of Home Depot warehouse in Auburn
summary: New York real estate investment company Rabina has secured a $13.5 million refinancing for its 210,000-square-foot distribution center in Auburn, Massachusetts. The property at 26 Millbury St. is fully leased by an affiliate of The Home Depot. The refinancing, arranged by Kelleher & Sadowsky Associates with Rockland Trust, was sought due to existing debt maturity and current interest rate volatility.

title: Top Women: Meet the Class of 2023
summary: HBSDealer has announced the "Class of 2023" for its annual Top Women in Hardware & Building Supply event, recognizing leaders and rising stars in the industry. The honorees, selected from a record number of nominations, will be celebrated at a live event in Chicago on November 15-16. The initiative aims to promote the role of women and amplify their contributions to the hardware and building supply sector.

title: Beating the benchmark? How AI-driven ETFs stack up
summary: The article discusses the performance of AI-driven ETFs and whether they offer an information advantage in stock selection compared to traditional benchmarks. It highlights examples like the QRAFT AI-Enhanced U.S. Large Cap Momentum ETF (AMOM) and the AI Powered Equity ETF (AIEQ), noting AMOM's outperformance against a momentum benchmark while AIEQ trails the S&P 500. The piece also explores the potential benefits of AI in portfolio management, such as a lack of emotion and more frequent rebalancing.

title: Ahead of Earnings, Is Home Depot Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Ahead of its second-quarter earnings report on August 15, Morningstar assesses Home Depot (HD) stock as overvalued with a 2-star rating and a fair value estimate of $259. The analysis highlights concerns about slowing top-line momentum and discretionary spending, while also noting the company's wide economic moat due to its brand intangible asset and cost advantage. Investors are advised to watch for trends in consumer spending, pro backlog, and potential trade-downs in upcoming earnings.

title: $72.5M Settlement in California Home Depot Wage & Hour Class Action
summary: Home Depot has agreed to a $72.5 million settlement in a California wage and hour class action lawsuit. The lawsuit, filed by Utne in 2016, alleged the company violated labor laws by underpaying over 272,000 employees. The settlement aims to resolve claims ranging from unpaid "off the clock" work for closing shifts and shift preparation to lost pay due to the company's rounding policy for hours worked.

title: Markets News, Aug. 15, 2023: Dow Drops More Than 350 Points on U.S. Banking Concerns, Weakening Chinese Economy
summary: U.S. stocks, including the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq, fell due to concerns over the creditworthiness of U.S. banks, a potential downgrade by Fitch Ratings, and a weakening Chinese economy. The Chinese central bank cut a key interest rate, while the U.K. saw record wage growth. Individual stock movers included Amgen and Home Depot rising, while JPMorgan Chase, American Express, Goldman Sachs, Dow Inc., Caterpillar, 3M, Chevron, and Walt Disney Co. declined.

title: O’Reilly Auto Parts opens new store in Caguas
summary: O’Reilly Auto Parts has opened its third store in Puerto Rico, located in Caguas, expanding its presence which includes two other stores and a distribution center. The new 15,000-square-foot store at Las Catalinas Mall will offer sale prices from August 16-29, with a grand opening celebration on August 19. This expansion represents a significant investment by the company in Puerto Rico, creating jobs and ensuring quick parts delivery from its Bayamón distribution center.

title: A Class Action Lawsuit Against Amazon & Wayfair Was Approved In Quebec & You Could Be Owed Money
summary: A class action lawsuit against Amazon, Wayfair, and Home Depot has been approved in Quebec, potentially entitling consumers who purchased extended warranties between 2019 and 2023 to compensation. The lawsuit alleges that these companies violated Quebec's Consumer Protection Act by not adequately informing customers about existing warranties. While Home Depot has already reached a settlement, Amazon and Wayfair's cases are still pending, with affected customers in Quebec eligible for reimbursement and punitive damages.

title: Walmart and Target executives speak out on retail crime
summary: Executives from Walmart and Target are raising concerns about the persistent issue of retail crime and organized retail theft, which continues to impact company profits and employee safety. Both CEOs, Doug McMillon of Walmart and Brian Cornell of Target, highlighted the financial strain ("shrink") caused by these thefts, with Target expecting a half-billion-dollar hit to profits. They emphasized the need for action, particularly at the local jurisdictional level, to combat this growing problem.

title: Introducing Limitless: GLIDDEN Paint by PPG’s ‘Anything but Yellow’ 2024 Color of the Year
summary: PPG's Glidden paint brand has announced "Limitless" (PPG1091-3) as its 2024 Color of the Year. This warm honey beige hue is described as a versatile neutral, suitable for various design styles and applications in both residential and commercial spaces. Glidden color experts state that this modern neutral signals the end of cool grays, embracing a new era of warmer tones.

title: Advance Auto Names New CEO Shane O’Kelly
summary: Advance Auto Parts Inc. has appointed Shane O’Kelly, formerly of Home Depot Inc.’s HD Supply unit, as its new CEO, effective September 11, following a quarter where profits missed estimates and the company lowered its outlook. The company also initiated a strategic review of its business as it grapples with inflation and a significant drop in its stock value this year. O’Kelly replaces Tom Greco, who will remain as an adviser for an unspecified period.

title: Advance Auto Parts Announces Executive Leadership Changes
summary: Advance Auto Parts has announced key executive leadership changes, appointing Shane O’Kelly as the new president and CEO, effective September 11, 2023. O’Kelly, former CEO of HD Supply and PetroChoice, succeeds Tom Greco, who is retiring. Additionally, Tony Iskander has been named interim chief financial officer following Jeff Shepherd's departure, with a search initiated for a permanent CFO.

title: Boise Cascade agrees to purchase door and millwork company
summary: Boise Cascade has announced its agreement to acquire Brockway-Smith Co. (BROSCO), a wholesale distributor specializing in doors and millwork, for $172 million. This acquisition will expand Boise Cascade's millwork business with BROSCO's two distribution centers and extensive product offerings. The transaction is expected to finalize in early Q4 2023, pending customary closing conditions and antitrust approval.

title: Advance Auto Parts falls out of the S&P 500 and names new CEO
summary: Advance Auto Parts is undergoing significant leadership changes and an operational review following a sharp drop in its stock price and removal from the S&P 500. Shane O'Kelly will replace Tom Greco as CEO, and CFO Jeffrey Shepherd is also departing. The company, facing supply shortages and wage inflation, aims for profitable growth within a year, while analysts note competitors have not experienced similar issues.

title: Home Depot SWOT Analysis (2026)
summary: This article provides a comprehensive SWOT analysis of Home Depot, examining its strengths such as helpful staff, online shopping, and strong brand, alongside weaknesses like inadequate store layout and high prices. It also explores opportunities in the home renovation market and smart technology, and threats including intense competition and economic fluctuations. The analysis concludes that strategic planning and customer-centric approaches are crucial for Home Depot to maintain its market leadership.

title: Dollar Tree Threatens to "Discontinue" Products Over Theft Concerns
summary: Dollar Tree is considering drastic measures, including discontinuing products, to combat rising retail theft that has impacted its recent profits. The company's CFO attributed a decline in financial results to "unfavorable shrink trends" and other factors. CEO Rick Dreiling announced new anti-theft strategies, potentially leading to fewer items on shelves or products being removed from inventory entirely.

title: Shoppers Are Abandoning Dick’s Sporting Goods, Data Shows—Here’s Why
summary: Dick's Sporting Goods recently reported a 23 percent drop in profits and failed to meet Wall Street expectations for its second fiscal quarter, despite an overall increase in sales driven by the back-to-school season. Factors contributing to this decline include macroeconomic uncertainties such as the upcoming student loan payment resumptions, a decrease in outdoor gear sales, and a significant impact from "shrink" (theft, damage, and cashier error). The company has reduced its global workforce by less than 1 percent, primarily in customer support, and expects flat to 2 percent sales growth for 2023.

title: The Top Fifty, revisited
summary: This article revisits the HBSDealer Top 150 Industry Leaderboard, focusing on observations beyond just sales figures for the top fifty companies. It highlights key strategic moves, financial performances, and leadership changes for major players like Home Depot, Lowe's, and Builders FirstSource, as well as significant developments for companies ranging from 11th to 50th on the list.

title: The Home Depot Introduces Decor Days to Offer Big Style Savings for Holiday Prep
summary: The Home Depot is launching its first-ever "Decor Days" event from October 5-9, 2023, offering significant savings on home decor, furniture, and other related products. This event aims to help customers prepare their homes for the holiday season with stylish updates and DIY projects at competitive prices. Exclusive discounts of up to 60% will be available on national and proprietary brands through HomeDepot.com/decor.

title: Residential demand for lawn equipment plummets, leading to rare Toro quarterly loss
summary: Toro experienced a rare quarterly loss due to plummeting residential and professional lawn equipment demand, attributed to dry weather, economic uncertainty, and pandemic-era purchases. To address this, the company announced a new retail partnership with Lowe's for next spring. Despite stronger performance in other business segments, Toro's stock dropped, and the company reduced its sales and earnings guidance for the remainder of the year.

title: Homesense building-out at Riverplace Shopping Center
summary: Homesense, an off-price home decor retailer owned by TJX Companies, is building out its new store at Riverplace Shopping Center in Mandarin, Jacksonville. The city issued a permit for the $2.14 million remodel of the former Stein Mart store. Homesense is actively hiring for various positions at the new 36,076-square-foot location, which will offer a wide array of home goods at discounted prices.

title: Home Depot Slammed Over Botched Appliance Delivery
summary: A Massachusetts man is accusing Home Depot of a botched appliance delivery after paying for premium "white glove" service for over $10,000 worth of appliances. The man claims the appliances were left on his front lawn, leading to mold growth and damage, despite his efforts to facilitate easy access. Home Depot has since apologized, acknowledging a miscommunication regarding shipping options for the specific brand purchased, and is working to replace the damaged units.

title: The Zacks Analyst Blog Highlights Walmart, The Home Depot and Costco Wholesale
summary: The Zacks Analyst Blog highlights Walmart, Home Depot, and Costco Wholesale as top blue-chip retail stocks for stable, long-term investment. These companies are praised for their financial resilience, consistent growth, and ability to weather economic downturns, making them dependable choices for investors. Each company's strategic initiatives, market capitalization, earnings expectations, and dividend payouts are detailed to showcase their strong investment potential.

title: Lowe's Cos. stock falls Friday, underperforms market
summary: Lowe's Cos. (LOW) stock fell by 4.70% on Friday, closing at $220.02, underperforming the broader market as both the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average also declined. The stock closed $17.19 below its 52-week high reached on July 27th.

title: The Home Depot Announces 2023 Innovation Award Winners
summary: The Home Depot announced the winners of its 2023 Innovation Awards, recognizing products that enhance efficiency for both Pros and DIYers. Leviton's Decora Edge™ was named the overall winner for its safer and more efficient light switch and outlet installations. Other top honors went to Ecolab Scientific Clean Line for bringing professional-grade cleaning solutions to homes and Glidden Cool Touch Exterior Floor Paint for its temperature-reducing technology.

title: Home Depot is selling a tiny home for $6,000 - customers say it's 'very sturdy'
summary: Home Depot is selling a Colonial Williamsburg DIY shed kit that can be converted into a tiny home for just over $6,000. Customers praise its sturdiness and ease of assembly. The kit measures 8 by 12 feet, includes a floor, and features fungal decay and termite-resistant paneling with a 50-year rot-resistant warranty.

title: Target announces nine store closures, cites 'organized retail crime'
summary: Target announced it would close nine stores in major cities across the U.S., explicitly blaming retail theft and organized retail crime for the decision. The closures, representing less than 1% of Target's total stores, will affect locations in New York City, Seattle, San Francisco, Oakland, and Portland. This move comes after Target's CEO previously noted a worsening trend in retail theft affecting safety, product availability, and business performance.

title: PPG receives top honors for product innovation, DE&I at The Home Depot’s 2023 Innovation Awards
summary: PPG has been recognized with two top honors at The Home Depot’s 2023 Innovation Awards: a second runner-up Innovation Award for its GLIDDEN® floor paint and concrete stain featuring COOL SURFACE TECHNOLOGY™ and the first-time Supplier Diversity Tier II Partner of the Year award. These accolades highlight PPG's commitment to delivering innovative products that simplify projects for both professionals and DIY customers, as well as its dedication to advancing diversity, equity, and inclusion within its business practices and supply chain. The Cool Surface Technology formulation limits surface temperatures by up to 20 percent, while the diversity award recognizes PPG's consistent performance in supporting diverse suppliers.

title: Home Depot Tracked a Crime Ring and Found an Unusual Suspect
summary: Home Depot and Florida law enforcement busted an organized retail crime ring led by Robert Dell, a pastor who ran a drug recovery program. Dell allegedly instructed individuals in his program to steal tools from Home Depot stores, which he then resold online for profit. The operation, which involved $3 million in stolen goods sold since 2016, resulted in Dell and four others being arrested and charged with racketeering and dealing in stolen property.

title: Tractor Supply’s Unsung Apparel Edge
summary: Tractor Supply Co. is actively expanding its apparel business, which already accounts for $1.2 billion to $1.3 billion in annual sales. The retailer is focusing on workwear and Western-inspired fashion, utilizing social media, brand partnerships, and shops-in-shop to attract a younger, more suburban customer base. Despite solid financial performance, the potential of its apparel segment is often underrated compared to other business strategies.

title: Greener Pastures for the Housing Market
summary: The U.S. housing market is projected to recover, driven by eased pressures from high interest rates, prices, and supply shortages, with new-home construction expected to rise 2% in 2024. This recovery presents significant opportunities for sustainable investing, particularly in green home construction and renovation, bolstered by environmentally conscious consumers, government incentives, and decreasing costs of clean technologies. Equity strategists anticipate growth in sustainable housing as demand for eco-friendly building practices aligns with the broader market's resurgence.

title: Papa Johns Appoints John Garratt And Stephen Gibbs To The Board
summary: Papa John's International, Inc. (PZZA) has appointed John Garratt, former President and CFO of Dollar General, and Stephen Gibbs, former Chief Accounting Officer and Corporate Controller at The Home Depot, to its Board of Directors. These appointments expand the board to 10 directors, with eight being independent. Both individuals bring extensive financial leadership and corporate strategy experience to help guide Papa Johns' growth plans.

title: Dallas-Based Spirit Realty Capital Acquired in $9.3 Billion Deal
summary: Dallas-based Spirit Realty Capital is being acquired by San Diego-based Realty Income Corporation in an all-stock transaction valued at $9.3 billion. This merger will create a combined company with an enterprise value of approximately $63 billion, enhancing Realty Income's size, scale, and diversification. Spirit shareholders will receive 0.762 newly-issued Realty Income common shares for each Spirit common share they own, resulting in them owning approximately 13% of the combined company.

title: Homesense Opens New Store in Jacksonville, FL
summary: Homesense, part of the TJX family of brands, is opening a new store in Jacksonville, FL on November 2nd at the Riverplace Shopping Center. The store offers a wide range of home furnishings, decor, and seasonal items at discounted prices, with new merchandise regularly arriving. To celebrate the opening, Homesense will donate $10,000 to Habitat for Humanity of Jacksonville.

title: Why Home Depot is evolving its media strategy, starting with branded content
summary: Home Depot is changing its media strategy by focusing on branded content, beginning with a shoppable CTV series on Vizio for the holiday season. The series, titled ‘Merry & Bright,’ stars Jordin Sparks and aims to engage early holiday shoppers. This move signifies Home Depot's evolving approach to reaching consumers through diverse media channels.

title: Home Depot co-founder: My customers are 'getting killed' by Biden’s inflation
summary: Home Depot co-founder Bernie Marcus criticized President Biden's economic policies, stating that inflation is severely impacting American consumers and Home Depot customers.
