title: New stores, comps drive Tractor Supply’s Q1 sales to $3.4B
summary: Tractor Supply Co. reported Q1 net sales of $3.39 billion, a 3% increase from the previous year, driven by new store openings and comparable sales growth. The company is maintaining its full-year financial guidance and plans to open additional Tractor Supply and Petsense stores, along with a new distribution center. Despite a shift in consumer spending from goods to services, analysts are confident in Tractor Supply's long-term outlook due to its focus on essentials and strategic growth initiatives.

title: Masonite approves big deal
summary: Masonite International Corporation shareholders have overwhelmingly approved its proposed acquisition by Owens Corning. Shareholders will receive $133.00 per share in cash, and the transaction is expected to close in mid-2024, pending regulatory approvals. This deal aims to enhance Masonite's position in the door industry through its "Doors That Do More" strategy.

title: Nearly 400,000 Honda Lawn Mowers and Pressure Washer Engines Recalled Due to Injury Risk
summary: American Honda Motor has expanded a recall to nearly 400,000 lawn mowers and pressure washer engines due to a potential injury hazard. The recall, involving Honda HRN216 series lawn mowers, Honda HRX217K6 lawn mowers, and Honda GCV170/200 G5B pressure washer engines, stems from improperly manufactured camshafts that can cause the starter rope to retract suddenly. Over 2,900 additional incidents and 38 minor injuries have been reported since the initial recall announcement in September 2023.

title: The Home Depot Announces First Quarter Fiscal 2024 Results; Reaffirms Fiscal 2024 Guidance
summary: The Home Depot announced its first-quarter fiscal 2024 results, reporting sales of $36.4 billion, a 2.3% decrease from the previous year, and net earnings of $3.6 billion. The company reaffirmed its fiscal 2024 guidance, including approximately 1.0% total sales growth (including a 53rd week) and a roughly 1.0% decline in comparable sales for the 52-week period. These figures do not include the impact of the pending acquisition of SRS Distribution Inc.

title: Home Depot sales slide as housing market weakens
summary: Home Depot's sales have declined for the sixth consecutive quarter, with same-store sales falling 2.8% due to a weak housing market and reduced demand for large discretionary projects. Transactions over $1,000, like kitchen and bathroom remodels, were down 6.5%, as consumers face financial constraints and high interest rates. The company is, however, strengthening its focus on professional builders and contractors, exemplified by its recent acquisition of SRS Distribution.

title: How supply chains used FLOW after the Baltimore bridge collapse
summary: The Department of Transportation's Freight Logistics Optimization Works (FLOW) program was tested following the Baltimore bridge collapse, providing critical insights to its members. Companies like C.H. Robinson, ITS Logistics, and Home Depot utilized FLOW's data-sharing capabilities to monitor disruptions, re-route shipments, and assess asset availability. While still developing and not encompassing all ports, FLOW proved useful in offering forward-looking data and coordinating responses during the crisis.

title: Some consumers are punting big purchases like pools and mattresses
summary: Consumers are delaying big purchases like furniture, pools, and mattresses due to high interest rates and persistent inflation. This trend indicates a broader slowdown in consumer spending, which could signal to the Federal Reserve that its interest rate hikes are having the desired effect on the economy. However, the impact is uneven, with lower-income consumers struggling more, while higher-end goods still see steady demand.

title: Why Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF Is One of the Best Dividend Funds Available
summary: The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) is highlighted for its sensible, transparent, and risk-conscious approach, aiming for better long-term risk-adjusted returns than the Russell 1000 Value Index. The fund's strategy focuses on 100 dividend-paying stocks with strong financial health, offering downside protection and strong exposure to the quality factor. Despite a challenging 2023, its overall performance since inception demonstrates strong risk-adjusted and absolute returns within the large-value category.

title: After Earnings, Is Home Depot Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Morningstar's analysis suggests Home Depot's stock is overvalued at $265 per share following its fiscal first-quarter earnings, despite sales being in line with expectations, noting a 2.8% drop in comparable store sales. The company maintains a wide economic moat due to its brand and cost advantage, a strong financial position, and a medium uncertainty rating. Home Depot is expected to return substantial capital to shareholders, although economic headwinds like weak consumer spending and higher interest rates pose risks to future growth.

title: The Home Depot partners to expand same-day delivery options
summary: The Home Depot is partnering with Instacart to offer same-day delivery for a wide range of home improvement items from nearly 2,000 stores across the U.S. This expands their e-commerce capabilities, including Instacart's Big & Bulky solution for larger items. The move aims to provide customers with increased flexibility and convenience, complementing their existing partnership with Walmart's GoLocal delivery service.

title: Home Depot’s Memorial Day Hours Are Great News for DIYers
summary: Home Depot stores will be open for their regular operating hours on Memorial Day 2024,

title: Procure Disaster Recovery Strategy ETF (NASDAQ:FIXT) Up 35% Since Launch
summary: The Procure Disaster Recovery Strategy ETF (FIXT) has seen a 35.02% increase in its net asset value since its launch two years ago, as of April 30, 2024. FIXT invests in companies involved in recovering from natural disasters, a market segment experiencing increasing economic losses globally. ProcureAM, the issuer, also reduced FIXT's management fee on Earth Day to encourage investment in disaster prevention and recovery.

title: Virginia Gateway shopping center in Gainesville sells for $215M
summary: Federal Realty Investment Trust has acquired the Virginia Gateway shopping center in Gainesville for $215 million. The 110-acre development, approximately 95% occupied, includes major retailers like Giant Food and HomeGoods. This acquisition aligns with Federal Realty's strategy for dominant, irreplaceable regional shopping centers with affluent trade areas.

title: Federal Realty Acquires 665,000-Square-Foot Virginia Gateway Retail Center in Gainesville, Virginia for $215 Million
summary: Federal Realty Investment Trust has acquired Virginia Gateway, a 665,000-square-foot retail center in Gainesville, Virginia, for $215 million. The property, situated on 110 acres, was 95 percent occupied at the time of sale and includes major tenants such as Giant Food, HomeGoods, Ulta Beauty, Total Wine & More, and Hobby Lobby.

title: Federal Realty Acquires Northern Virginia Retail Center for $215M
summary: Federal Realty Investment Trust has acquired Virginia Gateway, a 665,000-square-foot retail center in Gainesville, VA, for $215 million. The property boasts a 95% occupancy rate and is strategically located at the intersection of Route 29 and I-66. This acquisition expands Federal Realty's Northern Virginia portfolio to 3.6 million square feet, solidifying its presence in the region.

title: Back in Black: Orion Returns to Profitability as Sales Recover
summary: Orion Energy Systems, Inc. reported a net income of $1.6 million for fiscal Q4 2024, ending a streak of unprofitable quarters and marking a significant turnaround. The company achieved a 17.1% increase in total revenue for the fiscal year, driven by growth in LED lighting, EV charging, and maintenance services, and projects continued growth for FY 2025 through strategic diversification and expanding market presence.

title: The Toro Company Q1: Answers The Shorts, But Still Not Cheap (NYSE:TTC)
summary: Toro stock, after dropping due to short report concerns about inventory buildup, rebounded following Q2 earnings. The company appears to be effectively managing dealer channel inventory destocking and a Home Depot phase-out without significant sales impact. Despite addressing short-seller worries, the stock is considered a Hold around $90 due to anticipated slower growth and margin pressure.

title: Lowe’s names new chief marketing officer who will lead retail media efforts
summary: Lowe's has promoted Jennifer Wilson to Chief Marketing Officer, a role in which she will oversee the company's retail media network, One Roof Media Network, and lead strategic marketing initiatives. Her appointment, effective June 10, comes as Lowe's expands its retail media capabilities, including a beta partnership with Google for off-site retail media solutions. Wilson's extensive background in marketing and merchandising at Lowe's and other agencies positions her to drive customer engagement and business results.

title: Kimberly-Clark Is on a Roll with New Forest Policy and Goals
summary: Kimberly-Clark, maker of Kleenex and Scott tissue products, has announced a new Forests, Land, and Agriculture Policy and a goal to eliminate natural forest fiber from its entire product line. This move sets a higher standard in the industry, aiming to reduce forest degradation, particularly in critical northern forests, and includes commitments to Indigenous communities' rights. The policy puts pressure on competitors like Procter & Gamble and aligns with increasing global regulatory scrutiny on deforestation and forest degradation.

title: The Home Depot Announces Expiration of Hart-Scott-Rodino Act Waiting Period
summary: The Home Depot announced the expiration of the Hart-Scott-Rodino (HSR) Act waiting period for its acquisition of SRS Distribution Inc. This satisfies a key condition for the transaction, which is now expected to close around June 18, 2024, subject to customary closing conditions. The company also included a comprehensive forward-looking statements disclaimer detailing potential risks.

title: Resideo Completes Acquisition of Snap One
summary: Resideo Technologies, Inc. announced the completion of its acquisition of Snap One for approximately $1.4 billion. This acquisition is expected to expand Resideo's presence in smart living products and distribution, enhance its growth and margin profile, and be accretive to non-GAAP Adjusted EPS in the first full year of ownership. Following the closing, Nate Sleeper and John Stroup of Clayton, Dubilier & Rice LLC joined Resideo's Board of Directors.

title: Weil Advises The Home Depot in its $18.25B Acquisition of SRS
summary: Weil, Gotshal & Manges LLP advised The Home Depot on its acquisition of SRS Distribution Inc. for approximately $18.25 billion. The transaction involves Home Depot acquiring SRS, a leading residential specialty trade distribution company serving professional roofers, landscapers, and pool contractors. A large Weil team, including partners Michael J. Aiello and Eoghan Keenan, handled various aspects of the deal.

title: The Home Depot Completes Acquisition of SRS Distribution
summary: The Home Depot has completed its acquisition of SRS Distribution for approximately $18.25 billion, a move that is expected to increase its total addressable market by approximately $50 billion to $1 trillion. This acquisition enhances The Home Depot's capabilities in serving professional residential customers and establishes it as a leading specialty trade distributor across multiple verticals. Ted Decker, CEO of The Home Depot, stated that SRS is an excellent fit, complementary and additive to their growth, thanks to its strong vision and customer service.

title: The Home Depot Completes Acquisition of SRS Distribution
summary: The Home Depot has finalized its acquisition of SRS Distribution, Inc. for approximately $18.25 billion, as announced on March 28, 2024. This acquisition significantly expands The Home Depot's addressable market and strengthens its position in serving residential professional customers across various specialty trade verticals, including roofing, landscaping, and pool contracting. The integration of SRS is expected to accelerate Home Depot's growth in this segment and enhance its service offerings.

title: Home Depot Buys SRS Distribution As DIY Giants Turn To Pro Market
summary: Home Depot has acquired SRS Distribution Inc. for approximately $18.25 billion, aiming to expand its reach in the professional contractor market, which it estimates will increase its total addressable market to $1 trillion. This acquisition is part of a strategy to better serve residential professional customers for complex projects, especially as DIY sales have softened. The move reflects a broader trend among DIY giants to focus on pro markets to bolster growth.

title: Home Depot (HD) Buys SRS Distribution, Reaches $1 Trillion TAM
summary: Home Depot (HD) has finalized its acquisition of SRS Distribution for $18.25 billion, expanding its total addressable market to $1 trillion. This acquisition is expected to boost Home Depot's Pro business by offering more fulfillment and service options to residential professional customers. The company continues to invest in strategic initiatives, including its "One Home Depot" plan, to enhance its interconnected retail strategy and Pro capabilities.

title: Shares of swimming-pool makers slide after warning about weakening demand
summary: Pool Corp. issued a profit warning for 2024, citing weak demand for new pools, causing shares of swimming-pool makers to decline. The company projects new-pool construction activity to fall 15% to 20% and remodel activity to decrease by as much as 15%. This grim outlook from an industry leader indicates a slowdown in consumer spending on swimming pools and related equipment.

title: Home Depot and Lowe’s Target the Pros
summary: Home Depot and Lowe's are increasingly focusing on professional builders and contractors, a segment that accounts for a significant portion of their revenue, despite individual consumers driving the majority of sales. This shift comes as the general home improvement market slows down due to high mortgage rates and changing consumer spending habits post-pandemic. Both companies are implementing strategies, including acquisitions and specialized services, to capture a larger share of the pro market, which collectively represents nearly $100 billion in annual sales for the two giants.

title: EXCLUSIVE: Home Depot builds retail media network around DIY needs
summary: The Home Depot has developed its retail media network, Orange Apron Media, to better connect brands with its unique DIY customer base. Launched in 2018 and upgraded in March 2024, the network helps suppliers like Scotts target residential and professional customers at crucial points in their buying journeys. Home Depot plans to expand its focus to multicultural and pro audiences, leveraging its brand trust for greater impact.

title: How A Broken Furnace Led To An Innovative New Power Solution
summary: Entrepreneurs Pierre Delforge and Jane Melia, both Ph.D. Cambridge University engineers, founded Harvest Thermal after their home furnace broke in 2018. Their company developed the Smart Thermal Battery, which combines heat pump technology with thermal energy storage to reduce home emissions, lower heating bills, and provide superior comfort. Harvest Thermal's system has gained recognition and awards, securing nearly $11 million in funding, and is expanding its reach in new construction, home retrofits, and multi-family housing.

title: Tractor Supply Co. Just Made a Bold Change to Drop DEI at the End of Pride Month
summary: Tractor Supply Co. announced it would be eliminating its DEI department at the end of Pride Month, a decision influenced by a conservative activist campaign. This move follows similar quiet cutbacks in DEI funding by other major companies, despite general public support for DEI initiatives, highlighting a correlation between DEI support and political affiliation. The article suggests that for companies with a conservative customer base, pulling back on DEI might be a smarter business move to avoid controversy.

title: 4 Reasons to Buy Home Depot Stock Like There's No Tomorrow
summary: This article argues for investing in Home Depot stock, highlighting four key reasons. It emphasizes Home Depot's market dominance and vast network, its reliable dividend history despite occasional growth pauses, the current 14% discount from its recent high making it a good buying opportunity, and the anticipated recovery in the homebuilding market which will benefit the company.

title: Beloved retail chain with 400 locations to close down store after 24 years - and enters 'final phase' sales up to 70%
summary: A Bassett Furniture franchisee in Redmond, Washington, is closing its store after 24 years, offering final sales with discounts up to 70% on rugs and up to 65% on other furniture. The liquidation sale began in April, with the last day for shoppers being July 7, 2024. This closure follows Bassett Furniture Industries, Inc. reporting an operating loss, though no new corporately owned stores are planned for 2024.

title: Home Depot fined $1.6M for allegedly selling environmentally harmful refrigerant in Washington
summary: The Home Depot has been fined $1.6 million by the Washington State Department of Ecology for allegedly selling banned products containing environmentally harmful hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs). Despite repeated attempts by the Department of Ecology to ensure compliance between 2001 and 2003, Home Depot continued to sell an automotive HFC refrigerant called R-134a through its website in Washington, with 1,058 units sold during that period. The company has 30 days to appeal the penalty.

title: Report: North American furniture market to experience significant growth
summary: A report by Allied Market Research predicts significant growth in the North American furniture market, with its value projected to reach over $400 billion by 2030. The residential segment, driven by increased consumer spending, urbanization, and work-from-home trends, is expected to maintain the largest market share. The commercial segment is also forecast to grow rapidly due to companies investing in comfortable office environments, though raw material price increases pose a potential challenge.

title: Macy’s hires new CIO from within
summary: Macy's Inc. is promoting Keith Credendino to Chief Information Officer, effective August 4, 2024. He will replace Laura Miller, who is retiring. Credendino has been with Macy's for over two years, having previously held positions at Inspire Brands, The Home Depot, and other companies. His promotion comes at a turbulent time for Macy's, which is facing a takeover bid, board changes, and plans to close 150 locations.

title: Home Depot to settle fine for violating California consumer protection law
summary: Home Depot has agreed to a $750,000 settlement for violating California consumer protection laws related to gift card redemption. The lawsuit alleged the company did not allow customers to redeem gift cards with balances under $10 for cash, as required by state law. As part of the settlement, Home Depot will implement changes to its systems, provide notices about the law, and train employees on proper gift card redemption procedures.

title: Home Depot overcharges customers for rentals class action claims
summary: A new class action lawsuit alleges that Home Depot systematically overcharged customers using its tool rental service by charging excessive late fees and inflated Damage Protection costs. The lawsuit claims Home Depot's practices violate consumer laws and breach its own rental contracts from two distinct periods: 2015-2019 and 2022-present. E&G Enterprise Inc. is seeking to represent all impacted Home Depot customers nationwide to recover damages and legal costs.

title: VCR: Consumer Discretionary Sector Dashboard For July (NYSEARCA:VCR)
summary: This monthly article series provides a dashboard with aggregate subsector metrics in the Consumer Discretionary sector, highlighting that consumer services are the most attractive subsector based on value and quality scores. It also points out that the auto and components industry is below its baseline for both scores. The article suggests Vanguard Consumer Discretionary Index Fund ETF Shares (VCR) as an alternative to XLY and identifies nine stocks that were cheaper than their peers in July 2024.

title: Conn's HomePlus stores closing nationwide after company filed bankruptcy
summary: Conn's HomePlus, a home goods retailer, is closing several stores after filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on July 23. This move follows three consecutive years of fiscal losses and an over 80 percent drop in shares in 2023. The company, founded over 130 years ago, has listed 174 stores for closure, including six in Tennessee and two in Mississippi, and is holding a going-out-of-business sale.

title: Dollar Tree selling $1.25 dinner essential - 94% cheaper than Williams-Sonoma
summary: Dollar Tree is selling Royal Norfolk Stoneware Dinner Plates for $1.25, which are a dupe for Williams-Sonoma's Le Creuset Vancouver Dinner Plates that cost $20 each. This makes the Dollar Tree plates 94% cheaper. Shoppers are praising the quality of these budget-friendly plates and Dollar Tree is also noted for its other popular dupes, including beauty products from Five Below.

title: Going Into Earnings, Is Home Depot Stock a Buy, a Sell, or Fairly Valued?
summary: Ahead of its Q2 earnings report, Morningstar assesses Home Depot stock as overvalued with a 1-star rating despite increasing its fair value estimate to $270 after incorporating the SRS acquisition. The article details what to watch for in the Q2 earnings, the impact of the SRS acquisition on financial outlook, and Home Depot's competitive advantages, financial strength, and risk profile. Morningstar rates Home Depot with a wide economic moat and a low uncertainty rating.

title: Appellate Court Backs Home Depot in 401(k) Excessive Fee Suit
summary: A federal appellate court has affirmed a lower court's decision in a 401(k) excessive fee lawsuit against Home Depot, ruling that plaintiffs bear the burden of proving that plan losses were caused by imprudent fiduciary actions. The Eleventh Circuit Court concluded that Home Depot's investment decisions were objectively prudent and that the plaintiffs failed to demonstrate loss causation. This decision highlights a split among federal circuits regarding the burden of proof in ERISA excessive fee cases.

title: 11th Circuit Sides With Home Depot in 401(k) Excessive Fee Lawsuit
summary: The 11th Circuit Court of Appeals affirmed a lower court's decision in a 401(k) excessive fee lawsuit against The Home Depot Inc. The ruling places the burden of proof on workers to show how the company's conduct caused them to suffer losses, diverging from rulings in several other circuits. The case, Pizarro et al. v. The Home Depot Inc. et al., involved allegations that Home Depot offered imprudent investment options with higher fees than similar plans.

title: Michaels bolsters same-day delivery with DoorDash, Uber Eats
summary: Michaels is expanding its same-day delivery services by partnering with DoorDash and Uber Eats, making crafting supplies and home decor available from over 1,200 stores nationwide. This move aims to enhance omnichannel experience, convenience, and reach new audiences, mirroring a broader trend of retailers using on-demand delivery platforms beyond restaurant services. Other businesses like Home Depot and Lowe's have also ramped up their same-day delivery offerings.

title: 11th Circuit Appeals Court Rules With Home Depot on 401(k) Fee Suit
summary: The U.S. 11th Circuit Court of Appeals sided with Home Depot in an excessive 401(k) fee lawsuit, affirming a lower court's decision that the plaintiffs failed to prove Home Depot's conduct caused their losses. This ruling highlights a circuit split, as other appellate courts and the Department of Labor place the burden of proof on fiduciaries once a breach and loss are established. The court reiterated that plaintiffs must demonstrate that a hypothetical prudent fiduciary would not have made the same investment choices, concluding that Home Depot's decisions were "objectively prudent."

title: Investors - Governance - Board of Directors - Person Details
summary: This page introduces Keith Credendino as the Chief Information Officer of Macy's, Inc., a role he assumed in August 2024. The article also highlights his previous experience at Macy's as Senior Vice President, Technology Product Development, Customer Experience, and prior roles at Inspire Brands, The Home Depot, InterContinental Hotels Group, and Cox Enterprises, emphasizing his expertise in large-scale e-commerce, loyalty systems, and cloud-native infrastructure.

title: Home Depot reports another quarter of soft earnings as potential rate cut comes into view
summary: Home Depot reported soft earnings for the seventh consecutive quarter, with revenue of $43.18 billion and adjusted EPS of $4.67, missing revenue expectations. The decline is attributed to high interest rates and cautious consumer spending on major home improvement projects. The company anticipates a turnaround with potential interest rate cuts, with fiscal 2024 guidance updated to expect total sales to increase by 2.5% to 3.5%, while comparable sales are projected to decline between 3% and 4%.

title: The Home Depot Announces Second Quarter Fiscal 2024 Results; Updates Fiscal 2024 Guidance
summary: The Home Depot reported second-quarter fiscal 2024 sales of $43.2 billion, a 0.6% increase from the prior year, though comparable sales deceased 3.3%. The company updated its fiscal 2024 guidance, including SRS Distribution Inc. acquisition, projecting total sales to increase between 2.5% and 3.5% and comparable sales to decline between 3% and 4%. The CEO noted consumer demand pressure due to higher interest rates and macroeconomic uncertainty.

title: Home Depot’s stock bounces as home improvement demand may have just bottomed
summary: Shares of Home Depot Inc. bounced on Tuesday despite the company reporting worse-than-forecast fiscal second-quarter comparable sales and a cut in its full-year profit outlook. The rebound was driven by an implication that lower interest rates could stimulate interest in large home improvement projects, leading the company to raise its total sales growth guidance. This suggests that the demand for home improvement services might be nearing a bottom, potentially driven by anticipated monetary policy shifts.

title: Stocks of Lowe's, Behr paint seller Masco get a boost after Home Depot earnings
summary: Shares of home improvement companies, including Lowe's and Masco, saw a boost after Home Depot's earnings report and favorable inflation data. While Home Depot missed sales expectations due to high interest rates impacting demand for larger projects, optimism grew that demand would improve once the Federal Reserve starts lowering rates. This led to stock gains across the sector, including paint sellers and building material suppliers.

title: Qualified Remodeler's ‘TOP 500’ Residential Remodelers Offers Insights on $500 billion R&R Market
summary: Qualified Remodeler has released its 46th annual TOP 500 list, highlighting that the largest residential remodelers generated $21.7 billion in sales from 2.1 million jobs, an increase from $19.9 billion the previous year. This growth occurred despite challenging market conditions, with specialty home improvement firms showing the fastest expansion. The article also announces the upcoming TOP 500 LIVE conference in October.

title: Walmart Overtakes PepsiCo on Top 100 Private Carriers List
summary: Walmart Inc. has become the largest private motor carrier in North America, reaching No. 1 on Transport Topics' Top 100 Private Carriers list for the first time since 2002. This move unseats longtime leader PepsiCo Inc., driven by Walmart's expansion of its fleet to 12,663 power units and investments in its driver training programs. The updated list also highlights significant changes due to mergers and acquisitions, introducing several new companies to the Top 100 rankings.

title: Conn’s Closures Leave Behind A Swath Of Empty Retail, Industrial Space In Texas
summary: Conn’s Inc.'s Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing will result in 174 Conn’s HomePlus stores and 380 Badcock Home Furniture stores closing, leaving millions of square feet of retail and industrial space empty across Texas. The closures are expected to have a significant impact on Texas's commercial real estate market, particularly given Conn's large existing footprint in the state, including 83 locations and nearly 4M SF of industrial space. Despite the potential for landlords to re-tenant spaces and raise rents due to strong market fundamentals, the large floor plates of Conn's stores and the possibility of a "domino effect" on smaller tenants could present challenges.

title: Lowe’s Cuts Full-Year Guidance Amid Soft Housing Market
summary: Lowe's has lowered its full-year guidance due to a softened housing market, leading to reduced consumer spending on home renovations and DIY projects. The retailer now anticipates comparable sales to fall by 3.5% to 4%, a steeper decline than its previous forecast, and expects lighter adjusted earnings. Despite this, Lowe's reports making progress with professional customers.

title: New: Roofing Material Market to Increase 57% by 2034
summary: A new report by Future Market Insights forecasts the global roofing material market to reach over $231 billion by 2034, growing at a CAGR of 4.6%. The U.S. domestic market is expected to hit $29 billion in the same period. This growth is attributed to increasing global construction, rising demand for energy-efficient solutions, and technological advancements in materials.

title: Unlock Homebuilder Gains: ITB vs. XHB—Which ETF Is Your Golden Ticket to Housing Market Success ?

The piece aims to guide investors in aligning their ETF choice with their investment goals and risk tolerance in the dynamic U.S. housing market.

title: Hertz adds former Home Depot CEO and ex-GM general counsel to its board
summary: Hertz Global Holdings has appointed Frank Blake, former CEO of The Home Depot, and Lucy Clark Dougherty, former GM deputy general counsel, to its board of directors. These additions aim to strengthen the board with their extensive experience in business, government, law, and driving business transformation. Their diverse backgrounds are expected to help steer the company toward future success.

title: Home Depot Sued Over Use of Plan Forfeitures
summary: Home Depot Inc. is facing a lawsuit from a former employee alleging misuse of 401(k) plan forfeitures. The complaint, filed in U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia, claims the company breached ERISA duties by using forfeited funds to reduce employer contributions instead of covering administrative expenses. This case follows similar lawsuits against other major employers regarding 401(k) forfeiture practices.

title: The Home Depot Inc (HD): Is It a Buy? – Acquirer’s Multiple Stock Screener Analysis

The analysis points to the stock's 14.32% increase over the past year and provides several financial indicators supporting its potential as a 'buy'.

title: Mandarin Kmart building cleared for demolition for new Home Depot
summary: The former Kmart building at 9600 San Jose Blvd in Mandarin, which has been closed since 2016, is approved for demolition. Home Depot plans to build a new 132,975-square-foot store, including a large garden center, on the 11.64-acre site. The Jacksonville City Council rezoned the property for this purpose in May, and the demolition permit was issued on September 6, 2024.

title: Wood Products Market Opportunities and Strategies to 2033:
summary: The global wood products market is projected to grow from $788.45 billion in 2023 to $1.58 trillion by 2033, driven by increasing focus on home renovation, infrastructure development, demand for energy-efficient buildings, and rapid urbanization. Strategies for companies include focusing on sustainable materials, AI integration, automation, and strategic acquisitions to capitalize on market opportunities.

title: Home Depot places huge Valley warehouse on sublease market
summary: The Home Depot Inc. has put its 1.3-million-square-foot warehouse in Goodyear, Arizona, on the sublease market. This move comes after the company rapidly expanded its industrial footprint to meet increased demand during the COVID-19 pandemic. Home Depot had signed a 10-year lease for the facility in late 2021.

title: New Report Finds Shoppers Value In-store Shopping
summary: A new report by Ryder System reveals that despite the flourishing e-commerce market, consumers are increasingly valuing in-store shopping experiences. The study found that 61% of shoppers enjoy the in-store experience, a significant increase from last year, and many use their mobile devices while shopping in physical stores for price comparisons and product information. Additionally, 55% of consumers now prefer to return online purchases in-store, often leading to additional purchases during their visit.

title: Big problems for big furniture store chain with 14 NJ locations
summary: Bob's Discount Furniture is facing significant online problems, including a network disruption that began on Thursday and escalated by Friday. Although their physical stores remain open for business, customers expecting deliveries are advised to check emails for updates, as the company cannot provide real-time information or adjustments. The issue has also made it impossible to contact the company via phone, affecting its 14 New Jersey, 16 Pennsylvania, and 180 nationwide locations.

title: 2 Dividend Growth ETFs That You Can Count on for Recurring Income for Decades
